Summary: Add Jmol filter, either to main distribution or to filter download page
Description:
I've published a Jmol-based filter which renders molecular data files:

http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=36973



The filter is very simple (just a single filter.php file). It requires Jmol, which I've suggested placing at /lib/jmol/ - since the software is LGPL open-sourced, it should be feasible to include Jmol in the main distribution if desired.



The files that would be required from Jmol are Jmol.js, JmolApplet.java, COPYRIGHT.txt and LICENSE.txt - a total of approx 600kb. No other files from Jmol would need to be included in the distribution.



The filter doesn't require any heavy server-side work. It just turns a link to a molecular data file into the recommended Jmol javascript expression. On the client side, only Java and Javascript are required.

Summary: Change the column order of the mdl_log index 'courseuserid'
Description:
The log table usually has the most rows in it and can be very large. In the site level user logs Moodle does queries like SELECT COUNT(*) FROM mdl_log l WHERE l.userid='1'.



Usually these kind of queries are quite fast, but with very large tables they start to get slower too, if the WHERE column is not indexed.



MySQL can't use the index 'courseuserid' very efficiently for the WHERE userid=id type of queries. From MySQL docs: If the table has a multiple-column index, any leftmost prefix of the index can be used by the optimizer to find rows. For example, if you have a three-column index on (col1, col2, col3), you have indexed search capabilities on (col1), (col1, col2), and (col1, col2, col3).



Now, there is already an index 'coursemoduleaction' in this table which can be used to match any WHERE course=id queries. Changing the index 'courseuserid' to 'useridcourse' makes no difference in size and for queries that hit both userid and course, but that would give a big boost to those WHERE userid=id queries...

Penny, I'm assigning this to your as you were involded with the MDL-4112 also. I somehow complete missed this when the single userid column was added to the log table, sorry. 



But now with the single userid index maybe a better alternative to this bug would be to change the courseuserid index to just course? PostgreSQL manual supports this also :-) : Multicolumn indexes should be used sparingly. In most situations, an index on a single column is sufficient and saves space and time.



Or, courseuserid might be dropper completely, as now there is coursemoduleaction and userid so WHEREs hitting both userid and course column can use these? I have a feeling that a couple of single columns are better in overall than multicolumn indexes. (A feeling... ooo... maybe I should do  some query analyzing instead :-) )

From Martin Langhoff (martin at catalyst.net.nz) Tuesday,  13 June 2006, 04:04 PM:

Samuli -- yes, query analysis over mdl_log tables with real data is needed here. A bit of why these multi-column indexes are here... MySQL 3 and 4 use only one index per table (at least with the traditional isam and myisam engines).



Perhaps with InnoDB and/or v5 MySQL may behave better, but with v3 and v4 analyse will show you the expected behaviour. PostgreSQL doesn't have this problem, but the fact still remains that a multicolumn index is faster than 2 column indexes. 



If you do an annotate on the file, it should trace back to the commit. If it was the catalyst team that added the index, I am pretty sure we had some particular queries in mind (from our slow query log), so any change should be tested with those.  



There are many different queries being used on mdl_log, and we've tried to be smart about what indexes we added, and how they could be combined. Of course it can be improved, but let's see what the impact is ;-)

You're right about MySQL using only one index, didn't think of that. I benchmarked with the courseuserid vs. separate course and userid indexes, and MySQL can only catch on either one of the separate ones. And are there queries on the log table with just the userid but no course. There is a slight difference in favour of userid against useridcourse when doing select * from mdl_log where userid = 1 for example.



The bottom line: maybe better leave this as Deferred or Won't fix, waiting for MySQL 4 to be dropped :-)

Description:

Many users of moodle in school environemnts would appreciate the ability to either have a course reset button located in course settings or possibly a site reset located in admin.

 - Removal of forum posts

 - Emptying student data out of all modules

 - Deleting uploaded student files (assignments, etc)

 - Deletion of comments in modules

 - I am sure there is much more



The current system of backup/restore is not viable when the whole site needs to be reset for a new school year. A reset like this would add much needed functionality to this process.

11/Oct/06 1:01 PM;557058:aefadb44-443a-4323-97b5-367d90764f30;Some recent discussions on related issues make me think of this some more and I concluded that instead of 3 states, which may be confusing to some users, it may be better to have two separate flags, one controlling whether resources/activities are visible and another whether they are active. Then, the instructors will clearly see both states as icons (in edit mode) and as gray whether invisible or inactive (I would seriously consider including the state icons -- only as markers not as buttons -- after the title for people with editing rights).

Usage scenerios:

Visible and active -- the obvious usage -- we have it now.

Invisible and inactive -- the obvious usage -- we have it now.

Visible but inactive -- give us accountability and predictability when needed. For example, students have to take 4 quizzes or whatever throughout the semester. I can make all of them visible, so students know what awaits them, but make only one active as needed. This will couple particularly well with using conditional activities. Right now, we make them group activities with no students being in a group the activities are assigned to, but the message (when trying to open the closed activity) is confusing to most students and we must fiddle with groups to make them active. Other people mentioned other scenerios on the forums.

Invisible but active -- gives us more flexibility for less typical usage scenerios. For example, we use moodle to sign students up for an exam. Most students use a choice but some have to use a dialog and be manually signed by the instructor. We have a webpage resource which explains who does what and why and include there  links to choice and to dialog. To avoid students seeing them on the front page, we use the trick (used by many others) of having an extra topic with these activities with the count of topics is set to one less. They still show, however, in activities block. Another usage for us is offering a print version of specific ressource: we have information amended and formatted different ly and that extra resource is a link from the resource for online reading. 15/Apr/12 2:49 AM;557058:daab1da7-93dc-4527-9291-17a43ee7fb46;Several years late with this comment, but will make it none the less.  This feature is essential for teachers who want to be able to control presentation and visual flow in a topic area and fully overcome the scroll of death.  

When resources and activities are created in Moodle they are displayed in a single column list within a topic or weekly area.  These lists contribute to the scroll of death, and the fact that links to resources and activities can only be made available to students via these lists severely limits the ability of teachers to deliver learning content in a pleasing and thoughtful manner.  These Moodle "laundry lists" give Moodle a distinctly dated appearance that no amount of theming can overcome.  

A solution to this is to place topic area content within a label and within the label use a table to create a layout of editable areas.  Although the links Moodle creates to resources and activities cannot be moved into labels, links to resources and activities can be manually created within labels.  This method allows teachers to lay out topic area content as they choose. However, so that links to resources and activities don't appear twice within a topic area (in the label and outside of the label in a laundry list), the Moodle generated links to resources and activities must be moved to another topic area (usually at the bottom of the course or in an intentionally orphaned topic area).  Unfortunately, hiding Moodle generated resource and activity links from students by placing them in an orphaned topic area creates major problems for many Moodle features that expect Moodle generated resource and activity links to reside in the topic areas where they are made available to students.

Allowing teachers to designate resources/activities hidden but available/active would empower teachers to leave Moodle generated resource/activity links in the topic areas where they are being made available to students through label links, but hide the laundry list of these activities and resources from student view.  This would enable teachers to provide much better topic area layout without losing the benefit of important Moodle features (i.e. - Profile Activity Reports, Activity block summary reports, etc.).  This is an essential feature if Moodle is to become capable of creating the Web 2.0 styling and content flow expected/demanded by teachers and students.

As it was mentioned above couple of times, since such "third visibility state" will affect only course view page, this is completely responsibility of the course format. 
But at the same time I can see that this issue collected lots of votes and discussions so we might think of some generic solution.

My suggested approach:
- Add two methods to the format_base class (base class for course format plugins) that return whether the triple visibility mode is supported for particular course - for modules and for sections. By default it will return false, but each course format can overwrite it and even have in course settings if desired. These methods may also have coursemoduleid/sectionid argument to make it even more flexible for course formats.
- Add DB fields course_modules.visibleoncoursepage and course_sections.visibleoncoursepage (default to 1). Ensure they are backed up and restored, supported by web services, generator, and whoever else works with the whole tables.
- Make sure those properties are cached in modinfo, add new magic properties cm_info::uservisibleoncoursepage and section_info::uservisibleoncoursepage that will return  *($this->uservisible && ($this->visibleoncoursepage || !course_format_supports_triple_mode_for_this_entity))*
- Change all functions in core that can be used to display course view page and/or navigation to check ->uservisibleoncoursepage instead of ->uservisible
- Change the default functions to display edit controls to support third state and also add a checkbox on the module/section edit page.
- Each course format that wishes to support triple states must change uservisible to uservisibleoncoursepage in it's code if it uses custom output or navigation building.
- We may add this to our topics and weeks formats and also social format (involves changes in social block)

With this approach we don't break any other code accessing course modules and sections outside of the course view page - gradebook, reports, checking access when actually on the module page, etc. Also existing 3rd party course formats that do not wish to support the third state will not need to make any changes to their code.

21/Sep/16 2:27 PM;712020:6a0fb255-2f86-4645-b3b5-89acd899e684;We recently had an accessibility issue raised by one of our instructors over the overlap between hidden items and hidden topics. The current practice of dimming the color for hidden item and an opacity for hidden topic was not providing enough contrast. 
The color changes, dimming, and opacity in the proposed solution have the same issues. However, I think the new labeling you have developed should overcome this.


This did get me looking back into the visibility and availability (restrict access) settings and I now think we need to consider breaking backwards compatibility and implementing a new solution that clearly separates visibility and availability. I am not a UI person so there are probably some UI/UX issues that would need to be smoothed out and the language strings would need work. I think most of the visual implementation (color changes, dimming, opacity and labels) of the items you have developed would still work.

terminology:
visible = visible to students on course page
not visible = not visible to students on course page
available = generally available to students (other access restrictions may still apply)
not available = not available to students (other access restrictions DO NOT apply)

The current implementation being proposed has:
four actions in the Edit menu that result in these states (implemented as almost two toggles)
Hide = not visible + not available
Show =  visible + available
Make available = available (no change to visibility)
Make unavailable = not available (no change to visibility)
If the item is in a hidden topic the Hide and Show options are not present.

one setting 'Visible' in Common module settings with these choices and resulting states
Show =  visible + available
Hidden from students = not visible + not available 
Available but not displayed on course page = not visible + available
If the item is in a hidden topic the Show option is not present.
Special case if the item is a Label in a hidden topic only Hidden from students is present.


Instead I would like to see two independent settings.
four actions in the Edit menu that result in these states (implemented as two toggles)
Visible =  visible
Not Visible = not visible
Available = available
Not Available = not available
If the item is in a "not visible" topic the Visible and Not Visible options are not present.
NOTE: This means a change is also needed for the Hide/Show at the topic level. Possibly
Topic & Items Visible / Topic & Items Not Visible
- this would implement the not visible display on everything in the topic, similar to the current Hide minus the availability change
All Topic Items Available / All Topic Items Not Available
- this would toggle the availability setting on all items in the topic

a setting 'Visible' in Common module settings with these choices and resulting states
Visible =  visible
Not Visible = not visible
If the item is in a hidden topic the Visible setting is disabled and shows Not Visible or Topic Not Visible

a setting at the top of Restrict access called 'General Availability' with these choices and resulting states
Available = available
Not Available = not available
Special case if the item is a Label the General Availability option is disables and shows Available or Not Applicable.
The tooltip / docs for this setting would indicate that when Not Available is selected the other access restrictions are ignored - no students can access this item.

I know by having two toggles you could have a visible + not available item. I think this should result in the access restriction text of "Not available" being displayed.

For implementation it is possible you could use the existing 'visible' setting to store this new visibility value - I don't know the issues this might cause, so I would say no.
I think there should be two new settings. I think 'visibleoncoursepage' works for the new visibility value and maybe 'generalavailability' for the new availability setting. I could also see the availability setting being stored with the other access restrictions.

I have not looked at any of the code to try and figure out how this would be actually implemented. I wanted to get this idea back out for consideration before this is accepted for integration.

Summary: HTML templates for questions
Description:
Currently the code for producing the html for displaying a question is hidden deep inside the code. I would like to see a separation of logic and layout there by using html templates similar to what Moodle always does for its forms. 



In each question type directory there should be a file question.html which consists of html with the occasional <?php p($data->something) ?> where $data->something is some data that has been set by the print_question method of the questiontype before including question.html.



This will have to big advangages:

1) it will allow more people to improve the layout of the questions without having to understand the details of the questiontype code.

Summary: Questiontype giving hints
Description:
In connection with Quiz question (maybe even lessons) it would be good to be able to chose to provide hints.



I have for many years used a tutorial.pl script that has provided hints if the students choose it. It has been very appreciated and most have used it well. 



Sometimes students have looked at tips before trying at all. Even if they can follow the tips, they won't have internalized the process as well as if they have tried unsuccessfully first so they notice what they didn't think about. I haven't used the online tests in my grading. But it they are used for grading the hints should be able to be tied to penalties.



Often the hints contain a lot of strategic thought that even the pupils that got THAT question right might have use for in other problems. So I included the possibility to see all the hints even after a student has the right answer.

I even recommended that as standard practice.



The linking to the Hints should be made so the learner does not have to scroll after clicking the link.  



 This is what I would like to be able to do in connection with each question:

***********************

Teacher's interface:



(No hints/ 1 Hint choosable after each trail answer/ (All) Hints choosable after one trial answer/ Hints choosable)



Hint 1 ______________________________________ Penalty___  0-99%

Summary: Units in quiz answers not checked if numerical answer matches sample answer exactly
Description:
The requirement to have units as part of an answer is a key part of engineering science.  At present this option in moodle seems to address convertion from alternative unit systems into the one used by the teacher.  If no units are entered then the answer is used as given and compared with the teachers calculation.



What should happen is that an answer without a units component should be classified as incorrect.  In a perfect world feedback should be separated between numerical inaccuracy and incorrect use of units.



In the example below (Moodle XML format), where the answer is a vector (12.5 i m/s, you need a diagram which is not included to work it out), the complete answer is required for the solution to be correct. However if the student enters 12.5 then the marks are awarded as if the complete answer had been entered.

From Vy-Shane Sin Fat (vy-shane at moodle.com) Thursday,  20 April 2006, 11:32 AM:

Hi there,



Glad to hear that you enjoy using moodle enough that you want to contribute code!



I have had a look at the code that you attached. I see that you have added functionality to the print_log() function in /course/lib.php. It would be better to write separate functions for generating the excel and the text files instead of putting everything in print_log(). It is also best if you do not have checks like if($download = optional_param('download', NULL)) in functions that are in lib.php. These checks really belong in the log.php file. What I would suggest is this:



1) Perform the action check in log.php. Do we want to display on the page? Do we want to export as excel? Do we want to export as text?



2) Then branch to the correct funtion, for example, print_log(), export_xls(), export_txt().



Ideally we don't want a function to do too much (jack of all trades). We also want a function's behavior to depend on the arguments supplied (more predictable). In this case, it would be best if we don't have the function print_log() do different things depending on a check on $download = optional_param('download', NULL) inside the function itself. $download in this case is introducing a global variable in the function by bypassing the function's arguments. You could pass $download as an argument, but the best solution would be to have different functions for printing, exporting to excel and exporting to text. If you find that there are common bits shared by all these functions, you can always refactor the common bits out into a separate function that is called by all 3 functions.



If you want to write this functionality for 1.6, please bear in mind that the directory structure has been changed to support report plugins. The log report now lives in /course/report/log.



If you would like to contribute code, the best place to start would be to head over to http://docs.moodle.org/en/Developer_documentation :-)



Again, thanks for your interest :-)

Summary: Log table index 'timecoursemoduleaction' is mostly redundant
Description:
This applies to MySQL, haven't tested on PostgreSQL:



Queries that hit all of the four columns (time, course, module, action) end up using the 'coursemoduleaction' in all of my MySQL EXPLAIN tests. This might be because the 'time' criteria is always a range criteria, but the other three are all equalities.



Thus by replacing the 'timecoursemoduleaction' with just a 'time' index maintains the same speed for the recent activity queries (that have all of these in the WHERE), but lightens the log index load quite a bit. INSERTs to the log table are a bit faster too.
Comments:
31/Mar/06 12:40 AM;557058:04670d95-8ea4-4705-9d43-683a4fdf2d81;From Samuli Karevaara (samuli.karevaara at lamk.fi) Thursday,  30 March 2006, 03:56 PM:

cc'd Penny (again, sorry Penny :-) ), and also informing that the same effect (not using the timecoursemoduleaction index) happened in both MySQL 4.1 and 5.0.

From Samuli Karevaara (samuli.karevaara at lamk.fi) Thursday,  30 March 2006, 03:57 PM:

For example

EXPLAIN SELECT DISTINCT u.id, u.firstname, u.lastname, l.time FROM mdl_user u, mdl_user_students s, mdl_log l WHERE l.time > '1143530089' AND l.course = '2' AND l.module = 'course' AND l.action = 'enrol' AND l.info = u.id AND u.id = s.userid AND s.course = '2' ORDER BY l.time ASC;

From Samuli Karevaara (samuli.karevaara at lamk.fi) Thursday,  30 March 2006, 04:00 PM:

I was maybe too hasty, for example

EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM mdl_log WHERE time > '1143532707' AND course = '1' AND module = 'course' AND action LIKE '% mod' ORDER BY time ASC; _did_ use the index...



Changing to WFM for the moment, and doing more test on the effect on using time + coursemoduleaction vs. timecoursemoduleaction.

From Samuli Karevaara (samuli.karevaara at lamk.fi) Thursday,  30 March 2006, 04:40 PM:

Spamming a bit more: this is a borderline case, and might have to be tested in a wider scale than just individual queries.



Queries with a specified narrow time range will use the 'timecoursemoduleaction' index, but queries with a wider time range will switch to 'coursemoduleaction'. On the other hand, queries with a narrow time range will be quite fast with just the 'time' index too...



A trivial solution is to leave it as is, naturally, but the four column index (with the three of them in another index) might be a slight overkill after all.



Closing this for now.

Summary: import/export for custom question types
Description:
Currentlly you can write a new questiontype because types are now plugins, but you can't add it to the known qtypes in import/export formats.

Example: Joseph Rezeau regular expression questiontype is only a slight variation of the shortanswer qtype. So if you use Joseph's original idea of REPLACING shortanswer qtype, you are able to import/export questions in a lot of formats including GIFT and XML.

But if you ADD it as a new question type (We choose 'regexp' with Joseph as name for this qtype and the code is ready and working) you are not able to export/import any regexp questions !

This is unfortunate so I think the import/export code should be made expandable if we want new custom qtypes to be really popular.

Maybe as a first step if Moodle xml was modified it will be a good start, but maybe also designing a general way for formats to be expandable would be better ?

Gustav, can you forward this to Howard Miller ?
Comments:
30/Apr/06 12:35 AM;557058:04670d95-8ea4-4705-9d43-683a4fdf2d81;From Gustav Delius (gwd2 at york.ac.uk) Wednesday, 5 April 2006, 02:23 AM:

Yes, I have been discussing this with Howard already. In order to have a true plugin capability for both questiontypes and for import/export formats we need one file for each questiontype - format pair. This file should contain the code to extend the questiontype class by the functions needed for importing and exporting that questiontype in that format. 



Using classes for this has the advantage that new questiontypes can inherit the import/export functions from existing questiontype classes in those cases where they are very similar.



I agree with you that the XML format is the first one which should be made extensible in this way.

From Gustav Delius (gwd2 at york.ac.uk) Friday,  28 April 2006, 05:41 PM:

I am assigning this to Howard because it is clear that I won't have the time to do anything about it

From Howard Miller (howard.miller at udcf.gla.ac.uk) Friday,  28 April 2006, 05:46 PM:

Yes, it's all very true. But... I haven't the slightest idea how to actually do it.



The trouble seems to me to be that in most case 90% of the processing takes place before you know the questiontype. GIFT for example simply infers the questiontype from the syntax of the question - it must all be parsed before the code can judge what the question is. How do you make that expandable.



I have a vague notion about adding a 'custom' method that can be overriden to deal with unknown import formats before an error is thrown, but I haven't thought that much about it (yet).

For the users of custom question types the important thing is to have a mean to exchange question banks, whatever the format is, they don't need all formats to work.

One possible work around is to have the multiple choice questions be worth 2 points. Summary: Add support for enrol systems in backup/restore
Description:
After some chats with Ethem Elvice we have agreed this points about the authorize enrol system (that could be used for the rest too) and it's behaviour in backup/restore.



1.- Create a new section in backup files, called: <ENROLDATA>

2.- Under it, store all the enrolment info needed. This code should be present under enrol/xxx/lib.php/backup_enrol_info().

3.- This info should be  only saved if the user performing the backup is one admin or if the enrol system has some sort of mechanism to define if teachers can handle enrolment data (like the authorize one has).

4.- Implement the same login in the scheduled backup.

5.- Implement the restore of the <ENROLDATA> section whose code will be present in enrol/xxx/lib.php/restore_enrol_info()

6.- This info only will be restored if:

   - The site is the same than the original one.

   - The user perforing the backup has perms to handle enrol data (like point 3).

   - The enrol data belongs to one user that isn't currently enrolled in the course.

  - Backup file course enrol type and destination course enrol type are the same.

7.- If all the above are not satisfied, both course->enrol and user_students and user_teachers->enrol will default to the site default!



All this should be implemented AFTER 1.6 branch and release, of course.



Some questions remains in the air?



- In the schema above, we assume that all the students enrolled in one course have the same enrol system. Is this ok? Else we'll have to process things differently. And 6 and 7 will have to be re-defined.

- Verify that all the conditions above are correct and enough.



Sure this is one will be updated with more info/cases... thanks to Ethem for his ideas/explanations...



Ciao :-)

Backup/Restore is only required for INTERACTIVE plugins. No need for other enrolment plugins. Because the others are controlled by remote systems like DB, LDAP, PLAINTEXT.

Admin has to accept payment within 30 days, otherwise; the transaction is cancelled. While this duration, student can't re-pay for the same course.

From   (hephappy at gmail.com) Saturday,  29 April 2006, 07:06 PM:

Martin,



Authorize status is not related with Moodle-level backup/restore. It is related to payment status. Therefore, backup/restore process must import/export only table data. It must NEVER enrol student with authorize table. After admin accepting payment, authorize uses enrol_student() function.

How it works?

1- We assume there is a record courseid=x,userid=y,status=AN_STATUS_AUTH in authorize table. This means, admin enabled 'order review' and user y made a payment for course x, stutus displays the credit card was authorized. It is waiting admin approval for capture.

Summary: Search engine
Description:
Hi - Would it be possible to have a search engine facility, so a user can search the site for documents or pages using keywords?  No existing search engine (eg Google) can do it, because documents are held in the moodledata directory and so not available via the web (which is the whole idea of putting them outside of the www folder in the first place!) and pages with links to the documents don't really exist either, as they're assembled on the fly from database entries.  A search engine would therefore have to search the Moodle's mySQL database for the keywords, so it would have to be a Moodle feature and not an external engine.



It occurs to me that doing a search on Moodle pages should be very possible, because all Moodle pages are basically assembled as the result of queries on the database, using parameters such as which course the user is enrolled on and what level of access they've got (student, teacher, etc), so another query based on keywords should be possible.  It would also then be possible to restrict the results of the query to items which the user is allowed to see anyway, so a student didn't see results from courses they're not enrolled on, or things which are only available to teachers, admins, etc.



Searching documents would be a lot harder, because the moodledata folder would have to be scanned for keywords and a keyword table created.  Restricting results to documents which a user is allowed access to would be a pain as well, so perhaps it would be better to stick to just querying titles and descriptions of courses, links, etc.



What do you think?

Summary: Course Import - Smarter Import of Question Categories for Quizzes
Description: Currently, the exports the question categories and the questions and creates a second copy in the given course. This is fine and I would suggest keeping it as the default provided that the course being copied from actually is the 'owner' of those questions. However, in the case where the questions are being shared from a third course that has published those questions, I would like to see the import use those questions. This is helpful with shared question banks and will prevent the questions from being replicated and then questions arising from which question is the most updated, correct, etc. I like to use a teacher repository for my courses and then if a student discovers an error in the question I change it in one spot and it is then fixed for all of my courses (and anyone else). This approach highlights the social constructionist pedagogy a little more accurately (IMHO). Some folks view courses as independent entities and this would allow that to continue. But this option would also allow for a more collaborative approach to teaching and that is one of the things I am trying to encourage among our faculty. Perhaps a New Question Categories dropdown box with options for yes or no (similar to the Course Files dropdown box) would be helpful in giving folks the power to choose. Thank you for your consideration of this request.

From Anthony Borrow (aborrow at jesuitcp.org) Saturday,  15 July 2006, 06:09 AM:

What I am advocating for is a smarter and perhaps more accurate export/import process. If a course is simply using questions from another course, should we assume that the user wants a duplicate copy of them in that course or should we assume that they want to replicate as closely as possible the course that they are importing from. If the original course copied the questions then the import process should make a copy of them; however, if the original course is using questions from a published category, then so should the imported course. I do not see the loss of  functionality here but rather a gain in precision in the import process which becomes a valuable tool for sharing and collaboration. Summary: Restore course from previous semester - with wrong year!
Description:
One usability problem that we have for the backup/restore module of Moodle is that, our instructors often backup their courses taught on moodle in previous semesters and restore them to the current semester. However, the due dates for the activities (quizzes, assignments, etc.) would still remain as they were previously. If Moodle could automatically detects the system clock or something and prompt the user whether he/she want Moodle to change the year to current year/semester (sort of a smart approach), I think that would be great! A lot of our instructors have requested such feature. This is particularly useful when some courses have a LOT of activities that require manual date changes (for due dates..etc.) for all the activities (quiz, assignments..etc).



This occurs mostly with the year from Fall to Spring semesters. For example, a course backed up in Fall, when restored in Spring semester it will have Fall's year on it (and all the activities due dates would remain last year).

In short, what I am requesting is that the fields available for students to sort by be configurable by the teacher.

Summary: New export/import Cloze questions
Description:
MOODLE - New XML export/import functionality for Quiz Cloze-type questions by Philippe Vignoles (and Joseph Rezeau) 28 MAY 2006.

ATTACHED FILE cloze_format.zip



There are 2 *different* versions: for all 1.5+ (including 1.5.4) versions and for 1.6 version.



NOTE.- The version for 1.6 includes support for Joseph Rézeau's regexp question type.



Rationale

Standard distributions of Moodle 1.5+ and 1.6 (beta) do NOT include support for exporting/importing Cloze/Embedded type questions. We are providing support for these questions (for the Moodle XML format only). All you have to do is to copy the relevant format.php file to overwrite the format.php file in your current Moodle installation. Please note that this new functionality does not restrict export/import to Cloze-type questions; it will allow you to export/import question categories containing all types of questions, including Cloze-type questions.



Installation

\moodle\ means the folder where your moodle installation is.



FOR MOODLE 1.5+

Copy file \15\format.php to overwrite file \moodle\mod\quiz\format\xml\format.php.



FOR MOODLE 1.6

Copy file \16\format.php to overwrite file \moodle\question\format\xml\format.php.



IMPORTANT.- When exporting/importing question categories including Cloze type questions, always select Moodle XML format from the export/import File format dropdown list!

Summary: Database should offer 'smart playlists' like iTunes, for returning list of entries
Description:
I'm sure there's a better term for these things but in iTunes you can search through your database of music by entering text, which narrows the list to only tracks containing that term. Which is what Database offers right now.



iTunes offers a second option called 'smart playlists' where you can specify a number of 'rules'.



First you select a field from the dropdown (e.g. Artist - text, BPM - numeric, Compilation - boolean, Date added - date). Then you are offered an appropriate way to narrow the search e.g. for Artist (text) you get:



* contains

* does not contain

* is

* is not

* starts with

* ends with



for  numbers you get:



* is

* is not

* is greater than

* is less than

* is in the range



You'd either need a few pages or some nifty AJAX to provide the appropriate UI e.g. for the numbers example above the all expect one number entered into a textbox, except the last one which makes to textboxes appear (with 'to' between them) when you select it.



iTunes also lets you specify multiple rules and boolean AND or OR them together ('match all' or 'match any' in iTunes speak) though that might be too fancy.



I realized this would be a useful feature when I was trying to link to all the 3rd party Modules for Moodle in the Modules and plugins Database. With that use-case in mind, a re-usable URL would be good, the more human readable the better (if that is at all possible).

07/Jan/15 1:15 PM;712020:219f891d-87cb-4483-b06c-13cbad3e2b87;All proposed patch are very old and not adapted to recent Moodle versions.
So I have made a new one that
* add a "Display in left menu?" checkbox to all questions edition page. This checkbox is quite similar to the one displayed when you edit a content page but contrary to content page it is *unchecked* by default. So if you want a question page to be displayed in left menu, you have to click on it.
* overwrite the get_displayinmenublock for each question page type so that it now return true.

The advantage of my patch is compatibility: nothing is modified for existing lessons and users not wanting to use this new feature have nothing to change to their habits, they just left the new checkbox unchecked :-)
Of course the drawback is that each time you want a question displayed in the left menu, it will add one click to your question creation process. It seems to me this is a small price to pay for this new feature.
Of course we could go further and add a new setting to the plugin configuration settings so that the admin of a moodle website can choose if this checkbox must be checked or unchecked by default or we could choose to do this at the lesson level. But there are already so many settings and this is already so confusing for new lesson users that I am somewhat reluctant to do that. Please comment if you think I am wrong.

Summary: Export of published categories is not being blocked
Description:
When other teachers (who were NOT teachers in my course) attempted to export categories that I had published, Moodle 1.5.2 blocked them, saying Only the teacher can export quiz questions.  I liked that behavior because it prevented other teachers from copying my work.  I was willing to allow them to SHARE my work, but not to copy it (see MDL-5500 for a good discussion of sharing vs. copying in a social constructionist context).



In later versions (including 1.6), Moodle allows published categories to be exported.  I think Moodle should revert to the previous behavior.



I realize that, with expanded roles and capabilities in version 1.7, teachers may be able to constrain what can be done with exported categories, but meanwhile, can we revert to the more conservative behavior? 



To reproduce the behavior:

1.  Look for a category published by a course in which you are NOT a teacher.

2.  In your course, go to Quizzes->Edit Questions

3.  Select the published category from the Category menu

4.  Click the link Export Questions to a File

Summary: Let questions have customized text in place of Correct/partially correct/&qu
Description:
There seems to be a requirement for more feedback in quiz questions.



I think that the best bang-for-buck approch to this is to replace the existing Moodle-generated messages Correct, partially correct and Incorrect with customisable strings stored in the question table.



These should default to the Moodle-provided strings.



To implement this we need to:



1. Add the columns to mdl_question.



2. Change the base class to store, load and display this information.



2. Change the edit form for each question type to let these strings be edited.



3. Change backup and restore to include these fields.



4. Change all the import and export filters to do something appropriate with these fields. Initally, import can just use the default strings. Export is harder, and once we start exporting them in some formats, we need to be able to import them again.



(This is OU MDL-1191.)

The way questions (with any answers, feedback, scores, etc) are laid out is not great. I think the features of the various question types have evolved over the years a bit at a time, and different questions have done different things.

At some point, I'm going to have to sit down and look at this across all question types, and get a good clear and consistent layout for all this.

A lot of the quiz user interface is like that. It has evolved into a bit of a mess a little at a time. The trouble is, it is adequate for getting most things done, even though it is not great, which makes fixing it a lower priority.

1-Answer

6-marks the student received (or this could be put between 2 and 3)

Summary: Automatically scroll to any errors when updating the database
Description:
See this forum thread: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=48717



When you are doing a big database upgrade (for example Moodle 1.5 to Moodle 1.6) you normally end up with a huge page of ouput which is mostly Success, but with a few ERRORs hidden in there.



It is possible, but a pain in the neck to scan through the whole page by eye to find the problems. It would be nice if the page automatically scrolled to the first error, and they you had a link to click to go to the previous/next error.



If I was going to do this, I would probably do it all in JavaScript. Add an onload event handler that finds the errors (probably by looking for all the <div class=notifyproblem>s), scrolls to the first one, and adds the links to the page. That would require fewest code changes to the database upgrade code.



However, I don't have time to play with stuff like this now, so I throw the idea out here in the hope that someone else feels inspired.

Summary: Give a warning if, because of random questions, a quiz may require more questions from a category than are there
Description:
At the moment, you only get errors when a student attempts the quiz (or when teachers "preview" the quiz), which is a bad way to organise things.

Old description below. The above is point 3. The others are non-issues or duplicates.

-----------------------------------------------

I want to create a test made up of randomly selected questions from a certain category of questions, e.g. My questions.

I create the test, go into Editing Quiz mode, and at the bottom of the Questions window, I click on Add (2) random questions. Those 2 questions are added to the list of questions in my quiz.

If I then click on the Preview tab at the top of my Editing Quiz window, I can preview the test, comprising the 2 randomly selected questions. However, there are a number of problems here.

1- It would be more logical for the Test preview mode to display 2 different randomly selected questions each time I click on the Preview button. Of course, the questions will really be randomly selected in Student mode, but why not in Teacher mode?

2- While in Quiz Editing mode, In the Action column, the behavior of the two icons Preview and Edit is not as expected.

2a- The Preview link displays this error message: The number of random questions required is more than are still available in the category!, which is silly.
2b- The Edit link displays something totally unconnected with editing the question at hand...

3- The correct place for the control mechanism, and ensueing error message should reside with the Add (x) random questions at the bottom right of the screen, not with the individual Edit question link in the left part of the screen.

PS Same bugs in Moodle 1.7

04/Oct/06 12:47 PM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;Argh! One issue per bug report please. 

1) As Anthony rightly says, this is not a bug. The quiz preview intentionally keeps the same preview attempt open until you click the 'Start again' button, then it re-randomises.

2a) The preview link makes no sense, and should be removed. This is a duplicate of MDL-6650.

2b) The edit screen is useful. It lets you change the two important properties of the random question (which category is picked from, and whether subcategories are included). So not a bug.

3) This is a genuine issue that is not reported elsewhere, I am editing this bug report so that it covers this single issue.

Brain-dump of how such a check could be implemented:

The following test would have to be done every time the list of question in the quiz changed, and every time questions were created, deleted, moved to another category or imported. However, we would have to be sure this did not make everything unbearably slow.

1. Given a list of question ids. (e.g. all the questions in a particular quiz).

2. Get a list of all the categories that contain random questions from the list of question ids.

3. For each of those categories, compare:

A) The number of questions in that category that are not in the list of questionids, and which are of a type that can be used by the random question type

and

B) The number of random questions from the list in this category, or in a parent of this category and which are set to pick from the parent category and its subcategories.

4. If any of the comparisons give the wrong answer, display a warning message listing the categories that do not have enough questions.

Summary: the logic of ungraded
Description:
I discovered this problem by accident. I was grading some manually graded essay questions, and accidentally forgot to change the grade of one from zero to 10, but I had added a comment to it. I noticed this as I was saving it, so it wasn't a problem and I changed it, but I noticed that even though I had given the student a comment on the essay, it was still being listed as an ungraded question. In theory, a teacher should be able to give a student a zero on a essay question and it be considered graded. It seems to me that a decision needs to be made about what is considered ungraded. Is it:



1-A question without a comment and a grade of zero? (now it is, and it seems that it should remain this way)

2-A question with a comment but a grade of zero? (now it is, but not sure whether that is proper)

3-A question of any grade but no comment? (do we force teachers to make a comment?)



Maybe the way to solve this is to set the default grade as null rather than zero. Then it will be very clear whether a question has been graded or not.

Summary: table_column does not change serial columns correctly
Description:
Hi,



It seems that table_column is telling more lies :) (see MDL-6169). If you make a call like this:



    table_column('table', 'id', 'id', 'serial');



The table_column function changes the type to 'serial' just fine, but then clobbers the sequence default (which is nextval('seqname').



At the moment 'serial' is being handled really as part of the catch all handling in table_column. It needs its own special handling to handle:



  * changing a column to be of type 'serial primary key'

  * changing the name of the sequence if the name of a serial column changes.



I will attach a patch that fixes these issues so you can do:



    $status = $status & table_column('table', 'id', 'id', 'serial');



and



    $status = $status & table_column('table', 'id', 'id', 'serial primary key');



And of course, renaming the column.



Also included in the patch is a function to rename a table. Under MySQL it might be easy to rename the table (and it would be under postgres too), but because moodle expects the sequence to have the naming scheme prefix_table_field_seq, the sequence must be renamed also. The function handles the sequence rename for the postgres case.







-------------

Summary: Check for directory permissions problems in Health Center
Description:
I hit this PHP bug: http://bugs.php.net/bug.php?id=34552 when trying to install Moodle on my laptop, and it took me ages to find that this was the problem.



Basically, if one of the folders above $CFG->dirroot has 'x' but not 'r' permission for apache, then require_once can't work out the canoncial path for files and some files can get included more than once.



However, that took a lot of working out, because the effect of the bug was that on some pages, but not others, moodle just gave no output.



To test for this, I think you just need to do realpath('.'), and see whether that looks like $CFG->dirroot . 'somthing', or './somthing'.

22/Sep/11 7:55 AM;712020:12b8a5be-52e9-4011-9899-f023474e5c79;Anthony, 

Thanks for the comment. The start of the term has kept me busy, but I've been meaning to reply. My original comment makes most sense in two parts: assignments and quizzes. 

Assignments

At present, grading options only allow for integers with assignments. I take your point that everything is relative, but for many instructors the points that they would like to assign to an assignment have an intrinsic weight within their scoring schemes.Others don't tend to see things necessarily in terms of the entire course score, and so just weight the points accordingly. A particular assignment merits a particular point value. In some cases, then, instructors really want to give 5.5/10 as this is what works within their grading structure.

I’ll give you the flavor of an actual comment  "You can’t manually edit grades. I take of 10% for failing to follow standard formatting or properly naming files. Sometimes, that results in a fractional grade, like 40.5/50 or 23.8/30. To enter those grades, I have to go into the grade book, turn editing on, and manually enter the grade. It would be better if you could type in the grade rather than select a grade from the drop-down menu."

Being restricted to a grade of 100 on an assignment has also been a cause of concern. If you use the attendance block, then the attendance score can only total 100 for the entire semester. We have had an instructor who wanted to give 10 points per week for 15 weeks, but this was not possible without working around the issue. Sometimes a solution would be much simpler. 

Quizzes

The issue with not being able to add decimals in quizzes occurs when you try to add decimal point values during quiz creation. Let’s say you have a 10 question quiz but you want it to total 15 points. You cannot add the value 1.5 in the quiz and it total 15 points. What you can do is put the total as 15 and then have Moodle calculate the discrete values of items. I have had this issues noted on several occasions. First of all, it is confusing that there is no identification of the actual value of each of the items until the test is taken by students and reviewed by the instructor. If there were some way to highlight the actual calculated values, then this would be an improvement. Second,  some people would like to have more control over the actual values of each test item rather than have it automatically calculated or have to adapt their scoring scheme to meet the requirements of the system (same line of thought as with assignments).
 
I hope this helps better explain the concerns. Instructors would like to do what they would like to do rather than feeling they are being restricted by the available options . Any further thoughts would be appreciated. It seems as though this issue has been noted by several others as well. 

Thanks, 

Robert

22/Sep/11 9:27 AM;5e85c713c8077c0c1f10b082;"With regard to quizzes, I thought that decimals were allowed and that it would score them to a particular number of decimal places."
One might hope and expect this behavior based on the grade type being real and being able to specify grades to be displayed with x decimal places, however it is not the case. The system will compute my grade aggregate out to so many decimals and display them, but it will not allow me to specify a fractional grade weight for a question. It must be whole numbers. Additionally If I create questions with grade weights of 0.5 (the interface will let me type that in) it will save it as a 0. I find this to be a more clearly glaring error. it should either allow decimals or not, not allow them in the form and then transform them in the background to something less that useful.

I can add additional scenarios where this comes into play. Many times (usually in a Corporate client engagement) we encounter a ranking system or scheme that is already in use that uses fractional points to weight the success of the candidate in their testing or review. 1 for success, 0.5 for an attempt, and 0 for fails to show behavior. The hurdle to choosing Moodle then becomes one of choosing to retool the entire review process to handle whole numbers, or not choose Moodle.

I guess the other comment I would make is that it just seems from a user perspective to be a rather arbitrary and odd limitation. The database can (and does) store the values as real numbers as well as the display (except for the dropdowns which are troublesome with large value sets anyway). 
Is there a NEED for manual transmissions when automatic transmissions work perfectly fine virtually always? maybe not. Do I want to give mine up just to keep automobile designs simpler? absolutely no. I feel the argument goes very parallel here, is there really a compelling dire need to have real numbers for grade point values? maybe not, I think it really hinges on weather or not you feel that telling the user that they cannot do what they want to do is a compelling reason or not.
However, I might pose the counter question, is there really any compelling reason not to give the user the interface experience and grade item value control that they want?

Right now it sort or reads like the response is "We hadn't planned on that and now its kind of difficult to change" which in all fairness is more or less the user's argument as well, "We hadn't considered the possibility that the software would only let me use whole numbers, I do not really want to change my process to accommodate that."
I certainly feel that the interface requires some adjustment to be consistent. Either support the fraction that I type into the form or change the quiz forms to not allow values that are not supported.

Summary: Dilimiter ; and ,
Ability to specify a range of IP adddresses in quizzes
Description:
Currently the quiz subnet specification does not allow you to specify a subset of IP addresses, for example, from

133.101.32.1 through 133.101.32.48.  This functionality is necessary in order to specify all of the computers in a specific classroom, since other classrooms often contain addresses that are a continuation of the range in the previous classroom.



I have modified the code for the function in moodlelib.php that handles the IP subnet verification 



function address_in_subnet($addr, $subnetstr) 



so that ranges can be handled by specifying the string as:



 xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx-yyy



The code, based on 1.5.4+ is in the attachment, subnet.txt

Summary: Default opening within Frames
Description:
When composing a new resource linking to a file or a website there is an option to have the resource open in a frame.  This is defaulted to on, which means the majority of teachers do this.  Given the difficulty with printing and linking to a web-page in frames it is proposed that the default be set to unticked (i.e. that the resource opens as a normal web-page), and that the windowing help file be amended to explain some of the dangers of having a resource open in frames.  



Both of these have been taken care of by myself, and the updated code posted in the developers forum should anyone be interested or want to push it through

Summary: Backup files should not be included in new backups
Description:
When backups are set to save in the course folder and course backup files are included in new course backups. If a large enough number of backup files are kept (for example 20), then course sizes quickly grow to several gigabytes in size. 



In our particular case the client was then locked out of their account because they overloaded their quota.



This was on a Moodle 1.6 install, but I believe impacts many versions of moodle.

Hi Jonathan,



when you say, are set to save in the course folder I assume that you are generating such backups to the moodledata/1 directory. Is that correct?

Summary: force unique/unseen questions in quiz retakes
Description:
When retaking a quiz, there is no way to force retakes to pull ONLY unseen questions from the pool, so that EVERY retake has completely unique/unseen questions in it. For example, I have a pool of 100 questions, and want to create a quiz with 25 questions in it. I want to give the student 4 chances at the quiz, and every time the student takes the quiz, he gets completely new questions, such that if he takes it 4 times, he will have seen all 100 questions. This would work well in conjunction with randomizing questions, which currently just pulls a random set for each retake, but allows for the same questions to randomly be pulled into each retake.

This would be useful in the flashcard type of lesson too.

It would be nice to do everything in one database query. The following is my idea. I have not tested it, so it probably does not work. It also needs to be tested for performance, but the idea is worth pursuing.

{code:sql}
SELECT q.id, COUNT(qst.id) AS numprevioususes

FROM mdl_question q
LEFT JOIN mdl_question_states qst ON qst.answer LIKE CONCAT('random', q.id, '-%')

WHERE q.category IN ($categorylist)
AND q.parent = 0
AND q.hidden = 0
AND q.id NOT IN ($questionsinuse)
AND qtype NOT IN ($this->excludedqtypes)
AND qst.attempt IN ($avoidquestionsfromattempts)
AND qst.seq_number = 0

GROUP BY q.id

ORDER BY numprevioususes ASC
{code}

Do that query with get_records_sql_menu. That will give you an array of questionid => number of times that question has been used in previous attempts, in order of number of attempts.

That way, you can use the first part of the array to get questions that have never been used before, then use the next bit to get questions that have been used once before, and then questions that have been used twice before, and so on.

22/Jan/15 6:42 AM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;I'm sorry it took me so long to look at this.

This is looking much better. The basic idea of having an array where each question has a numprevioususes field, and to sort by that but otherwise shuffle, is good.

Unfortunately there are still problems:

1. The caching in $this->availablequestionsbycategory does not take note of the $questionsquiz list that was passed. So, if you call the function twice with different lists, you will be given the wrong results.

2. The shuffling does work properly. usort is not a stable sort (http://php.net/manual/en/function.usort.php "If two members compare as equal, their relative order in the sorted array is undefined.") so shuffle then usort does not give the result one hopes for.

3. The code violates an important design principle. There should be no mention of 'quiz' anywhere in 'question' code. In fact you are only passing a list of qaids. It is just the variable name that is wrong.

4. The list of qaids is potentially very long. Passing around long lists of ints is not good design. We already have a better abstraction for hadling this, the qubaid_condition class. If you use qubaid_list, then the list of question-usage ids is going to be an order of magnitude smaller then the list of qaids. Better still would be to use the qubaid_join class.

5. Is it really necessary to have two completely separate code-paths for the two cases? In the trivial case when there are no usages, just set numprevioususes to 0 for all questions and use the same code.

6. The code should continue to use 
$questionids = question_bank::get_finder()\->get_questions_from_categories in all cases, rather than duplicating the code from within that function to moodify it. Probably best to add a new method question_bank::get_finder()\->get_questions_from_categories_with_usage_counts.

7. Once we get a working implementation with good design, you need to format the SQL the way Moodle likes. See https://docs.moodle.org/dev/SQL_coding_style#Indentation

I'm sorry, but this needs more work.

Description:
The quiz settings page has a 'questions per page' option where you can select an integer, or 'unlimited'. This gives the impression that quizzes are automatically paginated.

Well, if the option 'shuffle questions' is turned on, then they are automatically paginated.

But if the shuffle option is off, then they are actually manually paginated. The quiz 'questions per page' option then only has an effect when a new question is added. On the quiz editing page, there is a tick-box 'show page breaks' that can be turned on. If you do, you can then see where the page breaks are and move them up and down. With the check-box on, there is also a dropdown that can be used for repaginating the quiz. That is only only effective way to change the questions per page option after questions have been added to the quiz. Changing the quiz settings dropdown does not trigger an automatic pagination.


Anyway, it is horribly confusing, as evidenced by several bug reports and forum posts. And I have been thinking about the quiz for months, and only just understood all the intricacies myself. We need something less confusing. I suggest:


On the quiz settings form, we add the option 'manual page breaks' to the 'questions per page' dropdown.

If one of the current 'questions per page' options is selected (unlimited or n) then the quiz is always automatically paginated, and the 'show page breaks' option and the other options it hides are not available.

If 'manual page breaks' is selected, the page breaks are always shown, and the manual repaginate dropdown is always present, and when new questions are added to the quiz, no automatic page breaks are added.

It is an error to try to select both 'shuffle questions' and 'manual page breaks' at the same time.

When making this change, all existing quizzes will be analysed for where the page breaks actually are. If the page breaks are uniformly spread, then they will be set to that automatic pagination value. If the page breaks are irregular, they will be set to manual pagination.

At the same time, I propse to change the default setting for new quizzes to 'one question per page' becuase I believe that pedagogically it is best for students to concentrate on one thing at a time.

And if only one question per page is shown, I propose to change the paging bar, so that instead of 'page' is says 'question' (and references to description items will be referred to as 'info', not given a number).

...... so it should be 1 qpp.

Tim,

Do you have any evidence to support this proposal? This may be the case with lengthy case study type questions, for example, but makes no sense at all for, say, a wholly MC quiz. How many paper based tests have you encountered with  one MC question per sheet?

Unlimited is the most sensible default. Please don't change this on a whim.

And if only one question per page is shown, I propose to change the paging bar, so that instead of 'page' is says 'question' (and references to description items will be referred to as 'info', not given a number).

This makes sense and would be welcome improvement.

Summary: email backup files to designated email address
Description: One of the critical problems I am finding with the automated Moodle backups is the fact that they are stored on the same server as the Moodle site by default. This means that if something were to happen to that server, the backups would be lost. An ideal situation would be if Moodle could be configured to email the zip file containing the backups to an email address as an attachment. 1. It is bad to include locallib from lib, for performance reasons.

The reason for having separate lib and locallib files is that lib.php is included from lots of other places in Moodle, and therefore needs to be small to maximise performance. So we split out the library functions that are essential for the other parts of Moodle to access, and put them in a small lib.php, and then we put all the internal library functions in locallib.php

So the solution is to move the function quiz_get_user_attempts (the only one you seem to be using) from locallib to lib.

2. I don't understand some of the things the code is doing.

2a) I do not understand the logic about whether it prints $strquizopens or $strquizcloses. What about quizzes that have neither an open nor a close date?

2b) You seem to be computing a variable $numattempts, and then not using it for anything.

3. You should not concatenate language strings - it is not translatable. Instead you should use the three-argument form of get_string. Also, there is not really any point getting 

4. The code is not indented according the the Moodle coding guidelines (4 spaces indent, no tabs) and there are spelling mistakes in the comments. Code to go into an open source project has to be better than this. Sorry to be harsh.

06/Aug/12 3:32 PM;557058:800d2609-d1a6-4f60-b9d9-0edd9cbd20bd;Hi Adrian,

I've just been looking at this and I've decided to send it back once more sorry.

There are a couple of things that I don't like about this solution when I sit down and look at it.

# block_delete_form is inheriting from moodleform but is not acting like a form.
# blocks don't need to be able to override the delete form like they do for the action form.

I think I get where you were heading with this but I think you've approached it incorrectly.
In concept the moodleform library is not supposed to have anything at all to do with page output. It should only be concerning itself with the form it is representing. That is how that library (quickforms+moodleform) is designed and is how it should be used.
The point of allowing a form to be overridden is so that its specification can alter the definition of the form, implement validation etc. Under your present use it is just a wrapper to output.
Its also worth noting that confirming the deletion of a block should never need to change, simply confirm yes or no. I can't think of a use case in which a blocks would need to override form and I really don't think it is worth doing.

What I think needs to happen here is pretty simple.

# Copy the code from block_delete_form::definition process_url_delete and do away with delete_form.php.
# Clean up that process_url_delete method within that !$confirmdelete condition.
# Make sure after any $output->footer() call within that function that exit is called to make sure nothing more can occur.

Cheers
Sam

Summary: Add serialize/deserialize to admin_settings class
Description:
All settings are stored in database in serialized form. Default config value should be serialized too. But when submitting the form with complex settings are data are in different form - also arrays. I think I found several problems in your implementation (and fix some of them), but the code is not easy to read and understand.

Proposal:
1/ add method serialize/deserialize to class admin_setting - with deafult implemenation just returning data as text
2/ always store defaults in serialized form (only strings - the same as in database)
2/ make get_setting() to return deserialized form (arrays, strings, etc)
3/ decide if write_setting() should accept only deserialized, serialized, or both forms
4/ fix all uses of write_setting() accorning to 3/

The resulting code should be easier to read, most bugs should be fixed during the conversion, it would be easier to add new complex types.

Summary: Standard Message API (code included)
Description:
I have found that recently every time I code a block or a module I end up writing up some sort of notification system to inform the user of errors or to inform the user that something worked successfully.

So, I thought that a standard API would be nice to have because I have noticed that other modules are also having to create custom code for informing the user of what has happened.  Also, by having a standard API, the look and feel of Moodle will be more singular.

The proposed API has a method for setting any number of messages.  These messages are stored in the session to allow for calling a redirect before printing the message.  And of course, the API has a method for printing all of the messages.  All messages are printed with notify().  

Note: The function for printing the messages could even be called in the theme header or in print_header so that all messages are printed in the same location.

Here is the PHPdoc of the two functions:

/**
 * Sets a message to be printed.  Messages are printed
 * by calling {@link print_messages()}.
 *
 * @uses $SESSION
 * @param string $message The message to be printed
 * @param string $class Class to be passed to {@link notify()}.  Usually notifyproblem or notifysuccess.
 * @param string $align Alignment of the message
 * @return boolean
 **/
function set_message($message, $class="notifyproblem", $align='center')

/**
 * Print all set messages.
 *
 * See {@link set_message()} for setting messages.
 *
 * Uses {@link notify()} to print the messages.
 *
 * @uses $SESSION
 * @return boolean
 **/
function print_messages()

30/Dec/11 3:35 PM;712020:69e98b18-53c2-437f-aa5b-c2f32e121a8c;I just encountered this problem and found a solution (not ideal but works)...

If you have access to your moodle database via phpmyadmin, find the table titled 'mdl_wiki'.

Browse that table and edit the entry for the wiki you want to change, then change the entry for 'firstpagetitle' to whatever you want your front page to be called.  Save the change.

Now go into your wiki and the first thing you will be asked to do is create a new page that has the new title you just set.  Do this and you will get a blank page.
Use the map tab to find your old first page and copy and paste the contents into the new first page.

Finally, go into the administration tab and deleted the old first page as it will now be an orphaned page.

Not ideal I know, but it does work...

Cheers,
Mike

23/Jul/12 11:33 AM;712020:18b177fe-fbcd-446c-8fb6-18f345ff27f7;To add to Mike's work around...

If you have access to your moodle database via phpmyadmin, find the table titled 'mdl_wiki'.

Browse that table and edit the entry for the wiki you want to change, then change the entry for 'firstpagetitle' to whatever you want your front page to be called. Save the change and make a mental note of the page contents and the previous first page title.

Find the table 'mdl_wiki_pages'. Browse that table looking for the previous page title in the 'title' field (if you just made the wiki, it will be the last entry)and the page contents in the 'cachedcontent' field. Edit and change the title to be the same as you changed it in 'mdl_wiki.' Save your change.

That's it...no need to copy contents and no need to delete an orphaned page, just go refresh/reload the browser view of the wiki and it should have the content on the newly named page.


"Not ideal I know, but it does work..."

Summary: Streamling editing questions when you are looking at the quiz response analysis
Description:
The Item Analysis report is a great way for teachers to find out where their students make mistakes, in order to address these specific points in their next lessons.

Would it be possible to add a column in this report with textboxes where teachers could input feedback for the most common mistakes (items in red with high percentages)? That would turn quizzes in adaptive mode into real private lessons where the student would get immediate correction adapted to their mistakes and a chance to find the right answer.

Of course, this is already possible by clicking on the question number in the report and editing the question feedback, but this means that teachers have to go way and back between this page and the item analysis report and do a lot of cut ting and pasting of the most common mistakes.
A new column for feedback in the report would make it so much easier!

(another column for points could let teachers change the points given for each individual answer: I often find out that there are other possible answers than the one I initially entered, and the Item Analysis report would be a good place to quickly change the points for many questions before recalculating the grades.)

 - switch core moodle + modules to a the new OO dmllib, with calls like $mdb->get_records()

 - it also allows us to rework things like what parameters they take - so we can re-design the API and drop things that have been bad ideas.

 - the legacy dmllib, when running insert_record/update_record()/select* runs striplashes and passes the call on to the new OO dmllib (which will use placeholders) - no security risk there - at the most we might strip an extra backslash accidentally

08/Dec/07 2:00 AM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;I am definitely in favour of this. The destination has to be an OOP interface with placeholders. I think placeholders speaks for itself. OOP needs more justification, but here are the benefits I see:

OK, an example of a interesting use of OOP datalib. This is something we have considered doing here using a nasty trick like messing with the $db global. 

You know the way the moodle.org grinds to a halt for a few minutes each day when it sends out the forum cron emails, because that hammers the DB. Well, to avoid that, you could consider setting up a second database that is a read-only mirror of the first, and run all the huge read-only reporting SQL against that, in cases where you don't really mind if the data show is missing the last few minutes live data. So logs and stats reports,  quiz and gradebook exports (not on screen where current data is more important and it is paged) some parts of cron etc.

To enable this, inside Moodle you would have two objects, $mdb and $reportingdb. Normally $reportingdb would connect to the same database as $mdb, but to ensure developers don't make mistakes, it would have to use a datalib subclass that gives an error if you call any of write datalib functions. Then gradually, you could move a few areas of the code to the new $reportingdb class for some queries, and some admins could set up the necessary replication, change the $reportingdb connection, and start moving the reporting load off of the main transactional database. That might even let you tune the two servers better. Apparently the OU uses this sort of setup for a lot of our other system, which is why we thought about doing the same for Moodle.

Description:
Current 1.6.2 Lesson dependency settings are based on time, score and completion.  However, completion is based upon question evaluation.  If the previous lesson has no questions, the completion criterion can not be met by a student.

I am hoping that some kind of standard dependency is built into a course in future versions of Moodle.  Something like Activity Locking which works on more than just Lessons.   In any event, this improvement should fit into that schema.

Summary: Having only a HEAD version for language packs causes major problems and inconsistencies
Description:
The language packs other than the en_utf8 one have only a HEAD version (i.e. no STABLE branch) since 1.6. This causes major problems.

1) Some modules breaks in 1.6.x with the introduction of new strings. See bug MDL-6644.

2) Deleting legacy strings like $string['studentviewoff'] creates regressions in the interface, when using up-to-date language pack. "Some strings that were translated are now in english. What's happened?"

3) Not adding new strings and not removing legacy ones (for conserving backward compatibility issue of point 2 above) doesn't allow smooth development, nor correct testing on development version using other language packs.

I suggest that we think about a mecanism allowing to have a stable version of language packs along with a dev one, so that could be resolved elegantly.
