Summary: Auto Lower Casing Of Uploaded Filenames... (As an option..)
Description:
Auto Lower Casing Of Uploaded Filenames... (As an option..)

This is a quick change for you... and should be made an option for people that want to use it... otherwise the general user/admin are not affected even with the change in place.

Also... since the lowercase happens in the clean_filename... then this automatically carried through into other things like mdl_resources without further change.

Basically ...  We have problems with staff creating documents... naming them in lowercase... uploading them... then later they edit them in another package... which then saves the same filename... but in all Upper case... not the staff members fault... but different software doing silly things.

We have ended up with confusion from duplicate files with different casing in their names... the average member of staff/student does not understand this.

So for the last 2 years... Everytime there is an update to   "moodle/lib/moodlelib.php"  I automatically edit it... and jump to line 4124 or thereabouts... and place an extra line in  the  function:  "clean_filename"

    ##### AJOS1 CHANGE ##### clean_filename #####
    $string = trim(moodle_strtolower($string));
    ##### AJOS1 CHANGE ##### clean_filename #####

Doing this has made things much easier in stopping duplicates... but I think it could be integrated into Moodle for those that want to use this idea... (as an option).

I am asking if you could have an option   like:   $cfg->lowercasefiles;   even better if it was settable under... SERVERS-SYSTEM_PATHS... or similar.

and then a code snippet like:

    $string = preg_replace("/_+/", '_', $string);
    $string = preg_replace("/\.\.+/", '.', $string);
    ....
    ....
    if ($cfg->lowercasefiles) {
        $string = trim(moodle_strtolower($string));
    }
    ....
    ....
    return $string;

This change would be highly appreciated... and I think if it was available others would use it.

Thanks in advance, Ajos1.

Summary: pass moodle_url to moodle_form constructor as action instead of passing url as a string
Description:
I attach a simple patch to optionally pass a moodle_url object (see http://docs.moodle.org/en/Development:lib/weblib.php_moodle_url) as the action of a form instead of a string to the moodle_form constructor 

The code checks if the $action param is a string or a moodle_url object. If it is a moodle_url object the object outputs the action url without any GET params and the params stored in the moodle_url oject are output as hidden params.

This is useful for complex pages where there are many GET params passing data from page call to page call. The hidden params can be used to pass an array of params not related to the form action from page to page. And the page params will always be processed in one place by optional_param / required_param at the top of the script.

The params are not output by the get_data method.
Comments: 21/May/07 3:38 AM;557058:e5b4189d-8e8c-487c-a61b-8e0d8b2ec186;Added some watchers to this issue who I hope will have time to look at this simple patch. Petr do you have any objection to me committing this to CVS?

21/May/07 5:19 AM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;:-( I do not think we should encourage passing of excessive data in hidden field - it often leads to sloppy code full of security problem. The problem is that each hidden field must be properly validated, it is IMO much easier/better to pass just one or two hidden fields and derive the rest.

21/May/07 6:59 AM;557058:e5b4189d-8e8c-487c-a61b-8e0d8b2ec186;Where possible it is surely better to derive data but it is not always possible to derive other params. A case in point is the question code which used to rely on storing params in a session variable. Now we pass params from page to page as hidden form fields or as GET params. When we have more params for a page it seems a good idea to have all the processing of the params for the page always processed in one place rather than having them processed both by optional_param and required_param for and by formslib when the form is submitted.

21/May/07 7:21 AM;557058:e5b4189d-8e8c-487c-a61b-8e0d8b2ec186;it seems quite logical to me to be able to pass an array of params that are already handled by the optional_param / required_param function at the top of the script page to formslib so that it knows to include these params as hidden fields and to know that these params should not be processed by formslib and should not be available in get_data returned contents.

21/May/07 8:10 AM;557058:e5b4189d-8e8c-487c-a61b-8e0d8b2ec186;Another comment on this :

It seems to me that being able to pass moodle_url to moodle_form would enable developers to properly seperate params that are needed to call up a page and params that are part of the form in that page. Params such as courseid, cmid etc are now included in the form definition which seems to be wrong since they are actually processed at the top of the script.

21/May/07 8:19 AM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;Yes, the last comment seems to be a really good use of it :-)

I saw several bad abuses of custom data in current codebase, I guess this could help to eliminate them

21/May/07 8:33 AM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;looking at the code...
are the hidden parameters cleaned (our PARAM_XXX) and validated (server side consistency checks) automatically? How would I do that in code?

I am still not sure about the security implications of hidden form fields here, because anybody can edit them before submission.

21/May/07 8:24 PM;557058:e5b4189d-8e8c-487c-a61b-8e0d8b2ec186;The hidden parameters that are put into a moodle_url should always be cleaned by required_param and optional_param before they are put in the moodle_url. The idea is that these 'page' params are cleaned at the  top of the script with required_param or optional_param and server side consistency checks are carried out *already*. Of course whatever is submitted in the form is picked up by required_param and optional_param at the top of the script, these params are also included in get_data output which is wrong I think. Better that we just output the hidden fields in the html and don't declare them as form elements in definition() - thus they are not output by get_data.

I can put a note in the moodle_docs and in phpdoc comments to make sure that when using a moodle_url the developer should make sure that params are cleaned before being added as a param to moodle_url. But anyway these params are cleaned on the first page call and they are similarly cleaned on subsequent calls.

Typical use of moodle_url I imagine would be :

1 required / optional param stuff happens
2 database queries to derive other page params and for server side consistency checks (if server side consistency check fails then an error stops the script).
3 moodle_url for this page is constructed (actually this can often be done at the same time as 1 and 2). You add the already cleaned params to the moodle_url object. Only adding params where the param is not the default or cannot be derived from other params with a db query.
4 moodle_url object can be used at various places in the code for outputting urls linking back to the same page with some extra params or for form submission to be processed by the same page.

22/May/07 6:29 AM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;+1 go ahead, I will review security when it is in :-)

Summary: Allow Admin to flag fields in user profiles as required and sortable
Description:
Currently, students are required to input user ID, password, last name, first name, e-mail, city, and a message. All but the last appear on the user account list, and most appear on the gradebook. However, at most colleges/universities, students are administered by a student ID number. I am aware that there is a similar field buried deep in the user profile. To see it we have to open each single user profile, and we cannot see it, nor can we sort by it in the gradebook or course participant list.
Those admins/teachers who like the status quo can simply refrain from setting student ID as a required/sortable field.

Summary: "Create and manage roles" capability not working
Description:
One would expect that a user with permission to 'Create and manage roles' should be able to create a new role.  For example, if a teacher is given such permission in a course context, the teacher should see a 'Define roles' link in the course administration block.  However this is not the case.  At best, teachers can Assign roles' and 'Override roles,' but not define new ones.

This presents a problem when a teacher wishes to give a specific permission to a specific student.  The only way to do this currently is for the teacher to (1) ask the administrator to create a new copy of the Student role (2) modify the copied role by adding the specific permission and (3) assign the modified role to the specific student.  This procedure clearly does not scale because the teacher will need a separate copy of the Student role for every special situation.  It is also a problem that such roles are globally visible.  If another teacher modifies such a role, the Student will inadvertently gain or lose privileges.

If the teacher could truly 'Create and manage roles,'  the teacher would be able to handle special situations like these without help from the administrator.  Such roles should be visible only to the teacher who created them.

NOTE: This seems like such a huge hole in the roles system that I'm wondering if I missed something.  I have posted to the Roles and Capabilities forum, but have not gotten adequate answers.  The forum is surprisingly quiet, considering the impact of this major new feature.  Even more surprising, there are no developers taking part in the forum.
Comments:
25/May/07 7:51 AM;712020:ad2b5cc1-3b42-4b54-a8b7-54d6da0ce992;I think I see the error of my thinking.  When the teacher overrides a role like Student in a particular context, it effectively defines a new role which is local to the context.  

The Override roles page could be improved by adding a short notice informing you that you are about to define a new role, not modify an existing one.
25/May/07 10:40 AM;712020:ad2b5cc1-3b42-4b54-a8b7-54d6da0ce992;The current override scheme still has a significant drawback: the same role can't be overridden more than once in the same context.

25/May/07 6:23 PM;712020:31584592-4e63-4822-b0af-1fe00b101d77;Hi John,

Teachers are not designed to create roles to begin with. Like you said, at best they can assign students to predefined roles and override them in their own courses. Creating a role is a system capability requiring high privilages, because anyone with the capability can technically create admin roles and use them, causing potential security problems. To be able to create a role you need both moodle/site:config and moodle/role:manage assigned at system level. Most teachers will have the default teacher role assigned at course level so they will not be able to create roles.

Cheers,

Yu

25/May/07 8:21 PM;712020:31584592-4e63-4822-b0af-1fe00b101d77;Hi John,

I think you can assign a teacher at course category level, thus making him the teacher for all courses in the category, and he should be able to override the capability for the student role in that category, which will apply to all courses under that category. Cheers,

Yu

26/May/07 6:58 AM;712020:ad2b5cc1-3b42-4b54-a8b7-54d6da0ce992;Yu,

The teacher wants some students to be able to choose but not see results, and other students to be able to see results but not choose.  Since the teacher can only override Student once in this context, the teacher will need a copy of the Student role, which must be created by the administrator.  I can imagine other scenarios where the teacher would need Student copy 1, Student copy 2, and in general, an unlimited number of Student copies.  I would be embarrassed to explain this scheme to a Moodle skeptic

26/May/07 7:39 AM;5a1ff37f40207c40ef913676;Hi John,

26/May/07 8:28 AM;712020:ad2b5cc1-3b42-4b54-a8b7-54d6da0ce992;It was just an example!   I do not want advice in solving the problem in this particular exampe.  I want a general solution to the following problem:

The Teacher is in some bottom-level context.

The Teacher needs to create several groups of Students, each with different capabilities (note, I am not talking about Groups with a capital "G")

The Teacher must have multiple copies of the Student role in order to create multiple overrides

The copies must have been created in advance by the administrator.

This does not scale.

28/May/07 7:46 AM;712020:ad2b5cc1-3b42-4b54-a8b7-54d6da0ce992;Yu Zhang wrote:
Teachers are not designed to create roles to begin with. Like you said, at best they can assign students to predefined roles and override them in their own courses. Creating a role is a system capability requiring high privilages, because anyone with the capability can technically create admin roles and use them, causing potential security problems. To be able to create a role you need both moodle/site:config and moodle/role:manage assigned at system level. Most teachers will have the default teacher role assigned at course level so they will not be able to create roles. 

I think this is exactly what makes roles difficult to understand and ultimately unscalable.  Moodle has two different mechanisms for role creation: one for admins (define new role) and one for everybody else (override an existing role).  In a given context, you can override an existing role exactly once.  If you need more than one override, you must have additional existing roles to work with (see my example involving the Choice activity).  That doesn't scale because you have to keep asking the admin to make additional copies of a role -- typically,  Student.

Roles would be (a) much easier to explain AND (b) scalable, if roles other than Admin could create and manage new roles.  Roles would be named and would live in a hierarchical namespace.  The role creation interface would only show those capabilities relevant to the current context, just as you do in the current Override role pages.  Safety is achieved by never allowing the user to pass on greater privileges than he possesses in a given context.

The roles forum is a very quiet place.  You could take this to mean that (a) everybody understands roles and there are no question or (b) not many people are using them yet (c) people are completely confused and have decided to stick with the default role behavior.  I think (a) is the least likely explanation.

There is a saying in programming that a design isn't simple enough until you can explain it to a child. By this standard, the roles system could use a lot of simplification.

12/Aug/07 2:51 AM;6210e69454698600765ea66a;It would be great to not only have this ability for assignments but for everything.

At the moment you have the option on all activities and resources to show and hide the from students. This is very useful. But it would be far far more powerful if you could restrict viewing to groups (multiple select).

Think about the scenario where you have 5 teachers teaching the same course. 80% of what they teach will be the same and 20% will be different - maybe only in small ways, like expectations for assignments or whether they actually have to do them.

The problem at the moment is that every student on the course will see all those differences for every teacher - so that creates another 100% of extra materials - of which only 20% is for them!

The current alternative is to set the main course as a meta course and have each teacher with their own course. But this is not a good solution. Students now don't know if materials are on the teacher's course or the main course. Plus the chances of teachers not collaborating or seeing good practices of other teachers are increased.

This would not seem like a huge change - the drop down box where you select visible to students could be changed to a list of check boxes where you select the groups that the activity/resource applies to.

Summary: File resources stored in a file version repository : subversion, CVS, M$ TFS (ex SourceSafe)
Description:
Dear all,

As far as I know on Moodle, the functionnality has not yet been implemented.
The objective is to ease the collaborative development of pedagogical resources to be refered by link in a moodle course.

The collaborative effort requires a file version management system (like Subversion, CVS). I do insist on the fact that these system are not only dedicated to text files but can also be used for binaries files (like ppt, doc, odt, ...).

The dream is a follow : By using tools like TortoiseSVN, teachers can work collaboratively, on their local machine, on their resources. Once finished, they commit their file (in the version management repository) and retrieve it directly in the Moodle files section (without any other action, or upload via Moodle).

A few ideas about the implementation :
Allow a new possible value for $CFG->dataroot (in config.php) like :
$CFG->versionroot = 'svn://localhost/didactic_resources'
If $CFG->dataroot left blank, then it would mean that any file resource would be versionned. 
If both were defined, each time a course would be created, the user would have the ability to choose the repository type :
classic or version managed (if $CFG->versionroot defined and $CFG->dataroot)

If any other work has already been done or is scheduled in a future version, let me know.

Thank you for the work already done anyway, fbab.

Summary: Blind choice
Description:
Here is a very simple enhancement to the Choice activity that would allow teachers to implement what I call blind choice. The main goal of blind choice is to allow teachers to randomize assignments.  Currently, only Exercise has a built-in assignment randomization feature.

Here is an example of blind choice in a brick-and-mortar classroom:  The teacher places assignments in unmarked folders. Each student is asked to choose a folder. Note that students are offered a choice, but from among alternatives about which they have no information until they open the folder. Typically, the folder will contain an assignment.

Choice currently has two fields for each alternative:

    * Option
    * Limit

In a blind choice, Options would be meaningless values like A, B, C, D.  We need a third field that is hidden until results are published (i.e., until after the Choice is closed):

    * Option
    * Limit
    * Actual choice

The Actual choice corresponds to the contents of the unmarked folder in my example. Typically, it will identify an assignment. For example, if students are studying U.S. history, the Actual choice might be the name of a president, such as Washington or Lincoln about whom students are to write an essay. Or, it might be the name of a file in a folder resource (the file contains a full description of the assignment).

Teachers could use blind choice with limits to effectively randomize assignments.  Currently, only Exercise randomizes assignments.  Blind choice would allow teachers to randomize assignments in other activities.

Summary: Provide a new predefined role called NoneSet
Description:
It would be very useful to have a predefined role called "NoneSet" for which all permissions have the value 'Not set.'  The primary use of this role would be to duplicate, then selectively set permissions to Allow.  An application is described below.

Say we want to allow selected teachers to create Site events, but we do not want them to have any additional capabilities.  The Admin duplicates the NoneSet role, creating role CanCreateSiteEvents, allows the two calendar-related capabilities, and globally assigns the role to the selected teachers.

I realize that the Guest role has most of its permissions marked Not set, and that Guest is therefore a reasonable alternative to NoneSet.  However having an explicit role will make its intended use much clearer.

Description:

09/Jul/08 12:23 PM;557058:ad4396bc-c0c2-4271-b0a9-df80010113dc;Generally speaking, I consider color selections to be theme issues rather than a usability issue. At the same time, I recognize that it is not always clear to the user where the turn editing on button is and that we actually have two options - the button and the link in the course administration block. I remember some talk about a highly accessible theme and perhaps we could have a highly usable theme that would cover color issues but I do not think that color alone will solve this issue. What might be helpful is to do a little research as to how editing mode is enabled in a variety of other systems (perhaps look at some other content management systems, LMSs, etc.) and see if there is a common theme that emerges. In general, it seems that having an editing on/off toggle button in the upper right portion of the screen works for Moodle once folks get used to it. I would want to make sure that we are consistent with that placement. For example, I think Gary Anderson told me that initially the editing button for the gradebook was on the left side. So I would want to make sure that we remain consistent and perhaps make a recommendation to developers for consistent placement of such buttons. Essentially it seems to follow the container model where by the editing options for that block (or container) are always in the upper right. Some questions I have that Laia might be able to research include:

Might we save some screen real estate by using an editing icon instead of the text 'Turn editing on'?
Would an icon confuse folks or be more consistent with how we use the editing icon in the gradebook? 
When do we use an icon and when should we use a text labeled pushbutton?
What would be the logic for determining when to use an icon or a text labeled pushbutton? 
Are there any UI standards that address these kinds of issues? 

An example of where I think we are inconsistent currently is in the gradebook (see screenshot) at: 
http://localhost/moodle/19stable/grade/edit/tree/category.php?courseid=3&id=3&gpr_type=report&gpr_plugin=grader&gpr_courseid=3 (just by way of example from a local test install). You will notice that the Hide Advanced appears twice on this screen within two different containers. Intuitively, this would indicate that you could hide advanced for each container; however, in fact they both function the same for the page so I think there should be one hide advanced pushbutton in the upper right of the page container. 

I realize that many of my comments on the usability issues will involve a fair amount of research; however, I think if Laia were to collaborate with folks like Gary Anderson and AT Wyatt she might be able to make some solid recommendations that would benefit the Moodle community. 

Peace - Anthony

09/Jul/08 12:25 PM;557058:ad4396bc-c0c2-4271-b0a9-df80010113dc;Here is the duplicated hide advanced I was referring to. Do we need the duplication on Turn Editing On? What alternatives might we explore to help make it more intuitive for users?

02/Aug/08 2:24 AM;557058:58fa5a3e-99fa-477b-9450-4f6159af01f9;I studied the different options Anthony commented in http://docs.moodle.org/en/Student_projects/Usability_issues/T5#If_the_.22Turn_editing_on.22_was_of_a_different_color_or_shape_the_usability_would_be_better and finally I concluded that the best solution would be a duplication of "turn editing on" (in all places it appears, not only in the administration menu but also in the grading system, etc.) and an addition of a help icon.

After talking with Gary, several usability problems with the gradebook where founded. To solve them, I made both an information architecture study and a usability test of the gradebook which can be read at http://docs.moodle.org/en/Student_projects/Usability_issues/T4. In this study some final concrete tasks are listed. Furthermore, other usability issues for instance tab key problems where discovered.

After this research, I tried to write a guideline for Moodle developers http://docs.moodle.org/en/Student_projects/Usability_issues/T7 in order to have there all the usability issues or consideration that should be taken into account to made Moodle usable and consistent. I would like to ask you if you have any comments about the guidelines, mainly in the "consistence" part which perhaps there are some more points that I have not worked with.

Summary: The sequence of the feedback forms for true-false questions is confusing
Description:
On the true/false question creation page, after the question, you specify whether the answer is true or false using a drop down (why not a radio button? There are ony 2 options!). Then there are two feedback fields - the first says Feedback (True) and the second says Feedback (False).

So it's confusing, because you may have a question where false is the correct answer (i.e. Bush is a great president), so you pick false as correct, and then the VERY NEXT field is feedback for the "True" response- so one believes it is feedback for the "correct' response, whereas it's in fact feedback for the "true" choice, which in this case is false. 

This is much less obvious (and less of a problem) for questions with true as the answer, but circuitous logic when false is the correct (not true) answer. It is also inconsistent with other question types where the feedback field relates to the answer that immediately proceeds/accompanies it. 

Proposed solution: Change the text to say Feedback if correct and Feedback if Incorrect, and change the display of feedback accordingly ( may involve a DB/code switcheroo). 
Barring that, since this is a usability issue and not technically a bug, some enhanced wording would be helpful - as in ("Note that feedback fields correspond to true and false answers, not correct and incorrect selections" - or something like that).

Summary: Adding support for all utf-8 symbols in "insert spaceial characterl" in HTMLarea editor
Description:
Moodle supports TeX filter to write complex expressions. However the use of TeX expressions is highly difficult and beyond general public usage.

However, almost anybody need to write some alphas o betas here or there. Or writing a mathematical operator, or some Arrows to point something. Nowadays text processors (MS-word and OpenOffice, for instace) have an "insert symbol" feature that allows to add any special symbol that cannot be accessed by keyboard typing. The full utf-8 range of symbols is available.

However, the HTMLarea editor only displays a reduced set of special characters in the insert special character" dialog. This patch is intended to add support  for all other symbol blocks existing in the utf-8 encoding: the full 154 blocks with chars from U+0000 to U+10FFFF.  Now this dialog will display the full range of unicode utf-8 characters supported by the web broser/font combination. A combo-box allows to choose the unicode block to show within UCS: Basic Latin, Greek, Math operators an so on. Even Arabic, gujarati, katakana and all others blocks, if desired.

To avoid making that selector too clumsy I have added a visibility setting that controls which of the 154 unicode blocks of characters are available. This could be added as as site setting in the admin tree (no done yet).

The attachment is tested in 1.9 HEAD, but should work as well in 1.7 and 1.8

Summary: No way to reliably add JavaScript onload handlers
Description:
It is not possible for included JavaScript code to add an onload handler in reliable or standard manner, because the body tag might have onload="setfocus()" added, which overwrites the JS-set handler. Also, if you have a case where two different pieces of code set an onload handler, these will overwrite each other even if setfocus is not used.

I'm going to write a utility JavaScript function addonload() that can add a function to be called onload, and change the focus code to use this instead of the body tag. $focus will then be set to false so the theme doesn't mess it up again.

Summary: Extend get_users_by_capability to have a $useviewallgroups parameter
Description:
In order to implement MDL-648 (see http://docs.moodle.org/en/Development:How_to_create_a_patch for a spec), we need to get users who:

a) are in group $studentgroup and have capability mod/quiz:emailnotifysubmission in the context of a particular quiz, or
b) are in any groups, and have capabilities mod/quiz:emailnotifysubmission and moodle/site:accessallgroups in the context of a particular quiz.

You could do that with three calls to get_users_by_capability, then combine the results in PHP.

Alternatively, you could change get_users_by_capability to optionally do the "in group $groups, or in any group and has moodle/site:accessallgroups". The attached patch does that.

I have no idea what effect the attached patch will have on performance (when $useviewallgroups is false, when it is true, things will certainly be slower).

The patch applies to Moodle 1.8 or HEAD.

Summary: Extending Course Format Flexibility
Description:
More Pluggable Course Formats:

Currently, we can -
- display a course page's *content* the way we want using '/course/format/[myformat]/format.php
- limit and control block display through the config.php
- add format specific language strings through course format language files
- add and manage speicific database tables and fields
- manage backup and restore for specific format needs
- define new roles and capabilities
- define course format specific styles

Limitations -
Display:
- can't control the header or footer output - these are output by the main /course/view.php

Function: 
- a number of arguments are handled in the main /course/view.php (eg. hide and show) that may wish to be handled differently
- all functions are in the main /course/lib.php - there is no way to replace them (we can force our own in the format.php, but that won't prevent the standard ones from being executed which can affect execution resources)

Course Settings:
- while we can add our own data tables, we cannot change the course settings page to use any specific new settings


Proposed Changes:
- create a simple class file (course_format.class.php), that can be extended by any course format
- break the current /course/view.php file into extensible pieces, and create extensible methods (where appropriate)
   > current layout -
      1. File inclusion - keep
      2. Argument loading - keep, although some of these should really be moved to specific formats
      3. Course data validation - keep,
      4. Login Access control - extensible?
      5. Page setup and section argument handling - extensible
      6. Ajax setup - extensible
      7. Module and section setup - extensible
      8. Output - header, page, Ajax scripts, footer - extensible
- change the course/view.php to use these methods, and look for existing extended class types in the specific format directories
- the 'view' method will do step 8, which will work 'as is' for all existing formats
- leave all existing course/lib.php functions where they are - they don't need to be part of the class for now, but all formats can use their own by adding to their own class files

- the biggest issue here is with the use of variables created in /course/view.php and used in the 'format.php' files (by inclusion). Make sure the base course_format class globalizes these. Currently, these are:
   $section (from arguments)
   $marker (from arguments)
   $course (still presumed global?)
   $PAGE
   $pageblocks
   $mods, $modnames, $modnamesplural, $modnamesused - used as globals
   $sections - used as global
 
CUSTOM COURSE SETTINGS:
Proposal is to modify the '/course/edit.php' function to handle any extra settings provided by the format. This modification is done in such a way to work with all existing formats as is.

The changes require calling an extra (optional) format function that provides any extra course information to the course object/record. When the standard main settings page is saved, if there is any extra settings defined in the format, then that form is displayed. That form is provided by a class function and a form class definition. The existence of these triggers the secondary settings.

27/Sep/07 9:04 PM;70121:e4689335-8ccf-4146-849c-c92eb29e3a9d;Hi Mike,

This all sounds pretty solid, but it still "forces" formats to have a left column of blocks, a center blob of content and then a right column of blocks.  Formats should be able to define their own layouts and block associations.  This could be done rather easily by allowing formats to define their own page class and then define their own block relationships.  So, instead of always associating a block instance with a course view page, the format could associate it with a format view page.  This currently doesn't work because of some of the flaws that you have pointed out and the following are the ones that I have ran into:

1.  A lot of core blocks assume that the $this->instance->pageid is the course ID.  This does not allow for blocks to be associated to other page types.
2.  The core backup/restore API only assumes there are blocks of page type course-view and whatever is inside of modules.
3.  Other API like the accesslib.php assume that there are only two columns for blocks, left and right.

These are just some of the limitations that I have faced while exploring the page class and block system.

To move forward, I think that formats would need the following work outlined here by Mike and they would need to be able to define their own page class definition.    As a result, formats will need to provide a method that returns all of the blocks that it uses.  That way when accesslib.php needs to run through all of the block instances to check role overrides, it can get all the blocks that the format may have tucked away or when it is time to backup, the format can tell the backup routine what blocks need to be backed up.  Finally, the core blocks need to be cleaned up to use the global $COURSE if they want to get the current course record.

I think this would really allow formats to come into their own and some really inventive course delivery techniques could be implemented.

PS: this work could be done generally enough so that it could also apply to modules as well.  I was trying to allow the lesson module pages to have their own blocks, but due to limitations outlined above, every page had to have the same blocks because I could only associate the blocks to the lesson instance and not to the lesson pages.

20/Oct/07 6:48 AM;5c3f7482e6047225b6d6494a;Hi Mark -

I agree with your ideas. My suggestions don't restrict you to the three column format because you can replace any of the display areas with your own methods. In the code I provided, the 'print_body' does the bulk of the course display, and uses the existing 'format.php' files so that all current course displays would continue to work.

But the intent is that if you create your own course format, you would override the 'print_body' with your own method. That way, the display could look any way you want.

I would like to nail down what global objects should exist and what should be used. I am unclear if using the page class is the best way or not. We may want to diagram out a more global structure of how things should be loaded, and determine what objects best suit this.

The way I have described above is an interim method to not break any existing formats.

09/Nov/07 11:21 AM;70121:e4689335-8ccf-4146-849c-c92eb29e3a9d;> My suggestions don't restrict you to the three column format because you can replace any of the display areas with your own methods.

Sorry, it is not your proposed code that restricts this, it is other areas in Moodle.  Example, in lib/accesslib.php:function get_child_contexts(), this function specifically only retrieves contexts from left and right blocks and no other position.

Some design ideas for your code:

What if you were to merge the course_format class with the page class definition in lib/pagelib.php for course pages?  Then allow formats to define their own pagelib.php and extend the default course page definition.  This is similar to how modules define their pages.  This would be easy to make backwards compatible since the default printing would be in the base course page extension and it could do all the variable setup and include the course/format/PLUGIN/format.php file.

> I would like to nail down what global objects should exist and what should be used. I am unclear if using the page class is the best way or not.

If everything is handled by the page class, then I think it would be best to store all the global type of information in the page object itself.  That way everything is easy to access via the $PAGE global.

Summary: Global search index maintenance process not fitted for complex information entities
Description:
Needs no HQ development.

Actual state of Global Search engine based on Zend fits well for simple information entities such as resources or forums where textual data is held in a single recordset. 

Some modules such as assignement, project, techproject, quizz, or any other module in which searchable data is spread out around multiple tables cannot be easily processes by the search engine croned updator because this updator uses a single textual unit strategy for adding, deleting or updating entries. Complex information models within Moodle should in fact be able to generate multiple searchable objects, what is actually not possible in the search engine implementation (one mod => one document class - based on mod name => one searchable object instance for indexing).

This may not have many consequences when the document aggregates all these distinct data such it can be accessed as a single browse target => a single url can be associated to the aggregated text content for indexing. 

Other modules may have more difficulties to be correctly handled by the indexor specially when access to the information it holds uses multiple url models (such as in techproject, that has fine-grained browse model inside, with information undertyping).

There may be a solution to that architectural issue increasing basic arity of asyncronous update/delete and update calls (from 'single object' paradigm to 'set of objects' processing). This would conclude in altering the <module>_single_document() entry, being allowed to return "more than one" single searchable object, based on an extension of <module>_db_names() return capaility (best return an array of arrays as a set of shemes to fetch parts of a complex document). (all these are in extensions of the SearchDocument class).

Reingineering chaîns will affect a lot of stuff in search engine integration code : 

All <module>_document.php should be reviewed for all classes returning an array of array by <module>_db_names()
All <module>_document.php should have <module>_single_document() reviewed for fetching multiple db schemes and creating as much search object instances as required. May this function keep its name "...single_document()" ?

update.php, delete.php, and add.php should be reviewed in order to update/delete/add a bulk of searchable objects obtained by considering a single "information unit" (larger than a single_document instance as the first implementation considered it.

Please feel free arguing about that architectural manoeuvres and tell me in which way enhancement of search engine could be driven.
Comments: 18/Apr/08 12:06 PM;557058:7e1bfbd6-11e7-4915-81fc-98f57783686a;All architecture plan retained and implemented in global search engine.

Summary: Streamline blackboard import
Description:
Programs like TestGen v7 can export questions in "blackboard format."  This is a zip file containing a .dat file (with the question text) and a directory of images.  Moodle's blackboard import just reads the .dat file, leaving broken image links. The user must  upload and relink the images manually.  

I recently pitched Moodle to a group of math teachers who were heavily invested TestGen for creating tests and assignments from publishers' material.  For them, the lack of interoperability with Moodle turned out to be a show-stopper.

The requested improvement is to combine the two steps into one so that by importing the zip file (rather than just the .dat file), both question text and images are imported.

Here is some information on  zip file, based on a sample (screenshot attached). The images reside in folder ppg/mabradle0907061259.  Within the .dat file, the image links are written in relative form, e.g., ppg/mabradle0907061259/foo.jpg.  To import the images, the importer must (a) perform the equivalent of  mkdir -p ppg/mabradle0907061259 in the course files root dir (b) copy the images to the directory (c) convert the image links in the question text to absolute addresses by prepending $CFG->wwwroot/file.php?file=/coursenum/

One additional improvement is needed.  The Moodle question name should be taken from the question id in the .dat file.  Currently, the Moodle name is defaulting to the first 33? characters of the question text.

Summary: Use of word "publish" in question categories is confusing/misleading
Description:
The word Publish in the category view of question management within a moodle course is accompanied by the same open/closed eye used in the rest of moodle to denote hidden/visible. The implication of the closed eye AND the word "publish" is that the questions will either not be available, or not usable, or not visible.

In fact this is not the case at all- Publishing denotes making the questions available to all others on the server, which is a very different functionality.

This word should be changed to something like "Share" or "Broadcast" or if need be "Share across courses" or even "Publish across courses". The icon should not be an eye, but something like a handshake, or little radio waves (i.e. broadcast) coming off a checkbox.

This is important because moodle newbies dont understand this, and publish their categories, thinking that necessary to make them active. The result is that everyone in a large installation sees HUGE numbers of categories showing up in their lists- making navigating the drop downs even worse.

Summary: Need to be able to grade AND reply to forums more easily
Description:
With assignments, grading is easy- you give feedback in the window, and have several buttons, with the option of saving and moving on to the next item, or closing the window.

In forums, not so. A typical forum with feedback takes several steps to complete with grade and feedback:
- click on submission (assuming each person posts one forum, the only way with a very large class)
- read, and assign grade and submit
- wait for page to refresh (3-5 seconds) or advance by clicking link and letting page reload
- clicking reply, waiting for that page to refresh
- typing in reply and submitting 
- wait for page to refresh (3-5 seconds) or advance by clicking link and letting page reload
- click on navigation/breadcrumb trail to go back to list of posts

This is OK for a few posts, but when you have classes that rely heavily on forums (public, sharing, constructivism, all that) you end up a LOT of this type of grading and it gets to be a real pain.

Suggstion for resolution:
- have a 2nd button on the post that says "submit grade and reply" or have that as an option in the forum. So when you click it after putting in a grade, it submits the grade and then jumps forward to the reply page, shortcutting several steps. 
- have a 2nd button on the reply page that says "submit and return to forum" which will take you back to the list of posts, not the thread you just finished with.

This would reduce this whole process described above to:
In forums, not so. A typical forum with feedback takes several steps to complete with grade and feedback:
1- click on submission (assuming each person posts one forum, the only way with a very large class)
2- read, and assign grade and submit and reply (added button)
3- typing in reply and submitting submit and return to forum (added button)

Downsides? Well, it provides more buttons, but this is one place that has hardly any, and in this case oversimplistic means too much work, esp. with a slow connection. Its possible the newbie would be confused by the 2nd button on the reply page- wondering what the difference would be- a few times they'd learn one returned to that thread, and another to the forum with all threads.

Summary: Make modules to declare and use Groupings
Description:
Groupings were introduced in version 1.8 as a way to organize groups within a course.  However, groupings do not have any practical use in version 1.8 or current 1.9 (HEAD).  As in 1.8/1.9 Groupings are more a useless complication than a useful feature. To be productive Groupings must be USED by activity modules. I have proposed a whole new range of groups/groupings features combining the design goals (but not yet implemented) of  OU and the implemented  version of Groupings working at ULPGC.  The spec proposal may be found at http://docs.moodle.org/en/Development:Groupings_and_Groups

At this stage I will concentrate in two new features:

a) Making possible to use different groupings by different activities. 
Activities can declare a grouping to use. This means that when that particular activity is set as visible/separate groups, the particular groups used are those belonging to the declared grouping. Hence, we can have simultaneous activities where users are distributed according to different criteria, activities & resources may be targeted to different audiences.

The needed changes are adding a field "groupingid" to the courses and course_modules tables to hold the grouping that the course itself or  each module instance will use when set in visible/separate groupmode. By "using grouping" I mean that  grouping-aware functions should operate nor on all groups associated with a course but only those associated with a grouping. So, you may have a forum declaring a grouping and thus using a particular set of groups. At the same time other activity  in the course, let say an assignment may declare other grouping and thus treat the same users as distributed in a completely different set of groups.

"Use grouping"  must be added to the configuration form for each module instance, parallel to  "groupmode" attribute. Best way is to add to te common module settings

Module code must be adapted to ensure that $cm->groupingid property now existing is passed to groups-API functions within the module code to return/manage only those groups belonging to the declared grouping.


b) Group-based content delivery
Once each activity, and resources, may declare a grouping to use, it is possible to make that those users that are not members of any group of that grouping  cannot access to the module content (being it an interactive activity or a Resource module instance)
A simple checking for group  membership at the beggining of the view.php file for each module  would do the trick
Group-membership may be checked at course page (function print_section() ) to make links to forbidden modules invisible to users without suitable access.

At ULPGC we have a test site with these features ENABLED, that is, already coded. You may find it at http://moodle.ulpgc.es/moodle19ulpgc/course/view.php?id=3
Try login as  user "prof01", "prof02" or "estudiante01", "estudiante02" ... with password "moodle" for all

The file attached is a unified diff against HEAD that can be used to explore proposed code changes.

10/Jul/07 9:25 AM;712020:6527e7b0-c431-4bbf-b180-7ee1fd61b16b;Hi Nick,
Nice to read you. I think we are basically in agreement.

Your spec and mine cover different aspects of Groups/groupings, one form the point of view of the user teacher and other from de code programmer. I think we would need to put together and consolidate the three views (with Petr) in a single document, or at least coherent parts of a whole. That's what Martin D and Moodle community expects, I think.

Agreement points: 
a) Grouping support at modules is essential and first task to accomplish. I think Moodle 1.9 cannot lack this feature
b) Global groups are quite problematic, mainly because backup/restore: Delay adoption
c) 6-table database structure is OK: most flexible, keeps all possibilities open for future additions. I do not see a power argument to change it.

Disagreement:
I strongly oppose making mandatory that any group must belong to a grouping. This implies to create a "default grouping" to hold groups, makes arise the problem of "not in a grouping"/orphaned groups. This is also a  problem when restoring old courses: they do not have a notion of "grouping". But this Groupings-first is not built in into DB or API, is a UI-imposed restriction.

UI criticism in 1.8/1.9
I think the main point to take into account is that the proposed UI insisted in creating Grouping first and then adding groups to a grouping. In pre-1.8 Moodle GROUPS are the main actors and I think that they should remain so: allow to create and manage groups _independently_ of groupings. ONLY if needed, the teacher may use groupings as a way to organize groups and to separate sets of groups for use in different activities.   

So I defend a groups-UI separate in tabs. One tab to manage groups and adding users to groups (the "classic") and another, separate, tab to manage groupings and populate groupings with groups. In this way the old-style logic and behavior is preserved, and new features may be introduced as new tabs as required. 

API Code polishing 
I basically agree with the changes indicated (MV,D). I do not see the rationale to maintain a separate lib/modulelib.php. The only "extra" point at module level is that groupingid is fixed. All functions in modulelib.php perform the same task as functions on basicgroups or grouping libs. For instance:

groups_m_get_group == groups_get_group_settings() or groups_groupids_to_groups() 
groups_m_get_groups_for_user() == groups_get_groups_for_user_in_grouping()  provided groupingid is known and passed

My point is that, in Python words, "better explicit than implicit". All *_m_* functions perform tasks that are covered by basic functions, provided groupingid parameter is passed. Why to complicate future maintaining tasks duplicating functions?

Summary:  We all agree groupings at modules is THE feature to add in 1.9. I think the main point now is in groups UI. 
Should we work to re-make the classic three pane UI with formslib? I think so

10/Jul/07 10:38 AM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;Hi!

my priorities seem to be different from both of you. The global groupings is the most difficult problem we are facing, that is why we should solve it first. I am not saying we should implement it first, but we should IMO find some solution first and then talk about the rest.

Originally everything was contained in courses - nothing was shared between them. It was nice and easy and everything worked fine. In 1.7 was a major breakthrough - global roles. As expected anything shared between course was difficult to implement, there are still some problems left and the resulting code is much slower. Course enrolments are one of those problems, I would really like to use global groupings to work around some problems there too.

Groups shared in groupings might seem fine when thinking about course groups only, but it will IMO cause trouble when we introduce global groups. If we do not share groups we need only minimal access control in the groupings - capabilities in system context for global groupings and in course context for course groupings. If we share groups we need to deal with it at the group level which would be much more complicated.

Shared groups in groupings - do we really need it? What are the use cases? How often do you need to reuse one group in several groupings inside one course?
* Sharing groups in groupings from one course? Not really sure we need it - more complicated UI, more complicated code.
* Sharing of groups between groupings from different courses? No. Use global groupings instead.

I agree the UI in 1.8.0 is not good, I do not think we need to discuss it much. I always wanted separate grouping and group forms because not everybody needs groupings. The orphaned groups were really bad idea, internally there should IMO always exist default course grouping which would be hidden in UI if no other groupings used in course.

I am working on my proposal too, adding some more info and explanation...

Example A (from N Hansen  http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=52134)
She has a course with three units and three levels of payment
Pay1 give acces to unit1
Pay2 give acces to both unit 1 and 2
Pay3 give access to al units form 1 to 3.
Let say she has three groups Pay1-3 according to the amount payed (a convenient way to classify users).
Unit 1 activities would use GroupingA=(Pay1, Pay2, Pay3) ie: any student can see and participate in these activities
Unit 2 activities would use GroupingB=(Pay2, Pay3)

My criticism is the other way around. Not about having a group in several groupings, what I see essential is to have groups _without_ groupings. Your scheme imposes that every group must belong to a grouping (and afterwards, to only one). But pre-1.8 groups did not belong to any grouping.  Yes, your scheme _demands_ a hidden "default grouping", special and different from the rest of groupings. I see this as a complication. Once groupings and groups are separated having a group in 0, 1 or n groupings are natural cases.

10/Jul/07 2:22 PM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;Hi Enrique,

hmm, that example with different levels of payments does not seem right to me, I would expect this to be handled with roles and new type of enrolment plugins (multiple instances of paypal plugin each with different enrolment role and money). This is a special case and maybe using different courses + one shared would be possible - again improved enrolment plugins doing enrolments into several courses with one payment would be useful in this case. Are there any other known uses for shared groups in groupings?

Groups without a grouping were bad from the programmers view - the problem is the speed of SQL queries, you have to combine results of two different queries. This has been discussed before, notably in bug 2245.  There is no way to delete a section (e.g. week or topic) from a Moodle course.  There seems to be general agreement that this is A Good Thing, but I can't really see why.  I understand the argument that you don't want the teacher deleting a populated section by accident, but you can't even delete an empty section.

The usual workaround is to move the offending section to the bottom of the course page, and reduce the number of sections the course displays.  However, bug 4719 indicates the drawbacks in this approach.  If a teacher wants to add a new section by increasing this number, the "deleted" block reappears.  This is irksome.

If a teacher/editor has powers to delete a resource or activity, shouldn't they have the power to delete an entire section?  You are asked for confirmation in cautionary terms every time you attempt to delete a resource, so why not have the same for a section, e.g. "Are you absolutely sure you want to completely delete the section 'foo'?"

section id, section number

User B who has not reloaded deletes the section that they see in position 1

1, 0
3, 1

Summary: Simple Deletion of submitted assignments
Description:
Hello!

I am using many assignments, mainly with uploaded files.

What I am looking for is a simple function for a teacher to fully delete submitted assignments, which is currently not possible with Moodle 1.8.2.

The functionality should be the same like with tests. A teacher can select several assignments for deletion, and after that the uploaded user files and all other database entries related to these assignments (marks, comments) are deleted.

Additionally all assignments should be automatically deleted (database entries and uploaded user files) by resetting a course, and also by deleting users from a course.

Kind regards, Daniel

Summary: Improvement to 'definition_after_data()' needed.
Description:
The definition_after_data function in formslib is defined as:
"This method is called after definition(), data submission and set_data(). All form setup that is dependent on form values should go in here."

This makes it a very useful function to provide non-trivial form function. The trouble is, that it is being called many times (up to 3) from a form, with no indicator of what function is calling it (state).

This function could be rendered much more useful if it passed a state value indicating which of the three possible callers is calling it. That way, code could act on the appropriate case.

So, something like:
definition_after_data ($state = 'unknown');
where $state is 'definition', 'submission', 'set_data', etc.

Summary: Allow teachers to choose which fields in newly created resources require a value
Description:
Instead of forcing all teachers to enter text in the fields "Name", "Description" and so on, Moodle should let the him decide which fields in all newly created resources and activities require a value. Therefore, additional options in the Settings Menu should let the teacher mark those fields in which he wants to be forced to enter a value. Please refer to the attached mock screenshot for an illustration of what these options could look like.

Behavior:
- If checked, the fields "Name" and "Description" would behave like in Moodle 1.8
- If unchecked, the fields would behave like in Moodle 1.6.5:  a missing value in the "Name" field of any resource or activity will automatically be turned into the generic name of that resource or activity (e.g. a Forum without a proper title had the name "Forum" assigned to it, any resource was dubbed "Resource" etc.) Empty description fields would be ignored.

Reason: Entering those values is often unnecessary, depending on the institution, the instructional design of a course and the teacher's work style, making it a time consuming requirement. Moreover, forcing descriptions will lead many teachers to simply add a dummy character which corrupts the original intention of making descriptions required. Please refer to my (German) post at http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=71251#337741 for a more detailed reasoning.

Summary: End dates of midnight are displayed in a potentially misleading way
Description:
Suppose you have something, say a quiz, and the deadline is midnight between Wednesday and Thursday. Then the student must think "I need to do that quiz by Wednesday at the latest", however, Moodle will tell them "This quiz closes on Thursday ...". Moodle is technically correct, but potentially misleading.

There are two possible solutions:

1. Encourage teachers not to set deadlines of exactly midnight, instead use 23:59:59. Of course, to do this, you have to change the date selector, because it often works in steps like 5 minutes.

2. Leave the deadline as midnight, but when we display it to students, actually print Wednesday 23:59:59 instead of Thursday 00:00:00, which is technically incorrect by one second, but sends the right message psychologically.

Of course, this would only apply to close dates, If a quiz opens at midnight between Monday and Tuesday, we want Moodle to display Tuesday 00:00:00, so the student can think "I can do this quiz any day on or after Tuesday."

Having thought about this a bit, I am pretty sure that 2. is the right solution, but I am not totally sure, so I am asking for other opinions.

Then, if that was true, and the date to be displayed was going to be midnight in the user's timezone, subtract one second before formatting.

18/Jul/07 6:28 AM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;Sam has proposed an option 3.

3. Subtract 1 second from close times when storing in the database, so that close dates are never exactly midnight.

Summary: Allow custom user profile fields to be ordered anywhere on the edit profile form
Description:
The new forms system and custom user profile fields capability in Moodle is a huge step in the right direction.  Many thanks!

However, the ability to order these fields and place them where you want them on the user profile form is limited to just ordering them among each other in their own separate section of the form.  What would truly make this capability useful would be to be able to situate your custom user fields among stock Moodle fields in any order you want. 

For example, one of my custom fields is "State/Province". It is of little use to have "Address" and "City" (both default Moodle fields) appear near the top of the edit profile page, and then to have "State/Province" way down at the bottom in my "custom fields" area. I want my users to be able to enter their address data all together, like they are used to doing on every other website where they've EVER entered their mailing address. So until Moodle allows me to place custom fields wherever I want in the form (including intermixing with default Moodle fields), this is of limited usefulness.

To see an example of the result that I'm looking for, you can see our site's current Signup form (the custom fields were accomplished by adding fields to the mdl_user table and adapting standard formslib code to include these additional fields):
http://www.sunsetonline.org/login/signup.php

Summary: Change HTML to make it easier to style multiple choice questions
Description: See http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=76228

Summary: Pre-populated answer (template) in essay questions
Description:
A pre-populated essay question allows teachers to pre-populate the "Answer" area of the essay question (i.e., the html area in which the student types) with arbitrary html.  For example, the teacher could insert an empty table that students fill in.

This could be a new feature of the existing Essay question type or an altogether new question type.  

There have been numerous requests for special question types (e.g., for accounting) that would be satisfied by this simple feature.

Summary: moodle/block:view to control block visibility
Description:
There are occasions where it would be useful to prevent users from viewing certain blocks. For instance, a course_list block might be placed on the front page to allow students to view their courses, but site administrators don't want guests to see a list of courses.

The natural way to control this behaviour would seem to be through roles. I would imagine the most frequently used workflow for this would be creating a prevent role overirde on the guest role of the block.

I've created a moodle/block:view capability which controls access to vew a block and works effectively.

There are a couple of issues though:

1) It seems to be assumed that CONTEXT_BLOCK capabilities will only come from block modules and not moodle components. Which means i've had to modified the langage string function and override functions to look at moodle components which have the CONTEXT_BLOCK capabilities. These are the only two places i've seen this assumption made, but presumably it could be in other places.

2) We have the capability cache 'problem', where by if a capability is changed it won't be observed in existing sessions because of the capability cache. It would be nice if we had a way of resetting the cache of current sessions on capability changes.

Summary: Front Page content shown based on role or logged in/ not logged in status
Description:
I would like to open this issue regarding the Front Page accessibility that was previously closed in the MDL-5983 issue.

I would like people who are not logged in to have a different stylized Front Page from what the logged in users would get.  Presently this is impossible to have if one wants to put a Login button or other site access information - as that does not make sense for someone already logged in to see - unless we are forced to use My Moodle which will not work if the focus is on creating a standardized learning environment that is not cluttered or made more complex by the ability of students to click around and play with various block type functionality - and thus likely resulting in more admin type of work.

The concern with using Moodle blocks is that I do not want to give my students the ability to create or use blocks - I want a tightened down standardized learning environment across all students that just focuses for logged in students on the courses to take and the actual courses themselves.

As a result, I am hoping that this can be an enhancement request to be able to better define the Front Page by role to eliminate the above issues.

Thanks in advance and keep on Moodling!

Best Regards,

Bob

Summary: improvement to context_rel table and load_user_capability()
Description:
The context_rel table is a caching table built to allow the big SQL in load_user_capability() to be able to identify the pair of contexts that are related easily, (e.g. parent/child or grandparent/child), where you have an override at a lower context level, and an assignment at the higher context level.

The current issue we have is that the number of entries in context_rel table is normally a few times larger than the context table. Working with such a large table takes quite a bit of space and can potentially cause load_user_capability() to run slower.

However, there is no point (IMHO) to store the pair of contexts in the context_rel table if
1) There is no role assignment at the higher context OR
2) There is no role override in the lower context

Currently the context_rel table is populated whenever a new context is inserted. Given that the number of contexts with any overrides is much less than the number of contexts in which we have a direct role assignment, I propose we make the following changes

1) Do not populate the context_rel table upon context creation.
2) Populate the context_rel table whenever an override is added.
3) Take out entries from context_rel if the last override is removed.
4) build_context_rel() should loop all context and only populate contexts with overrides when users upgrades. (current, for users from 1.7 and below)
5) In 1.9, drop the context_rel table and call build_context_rel().

8) Add rebuild_context_rel() to handle proper movement of courses/course categories. This is currently a bug that affects grandchild, grandparent relationships. It not related to this bug, but fixing along the way

26/Mar/20 9:42 AM;5c09c8b4b203a71cc9cb1bc1;Hi Peter,

Thanks for persisting with this issue. It would be nice to see support for this in Glossary however, stepping through it, I think there are a few things which are unclear and not deliberately handled.

*1.* The notion of 'concepts' still presents some questions which need answering.

In separate groups mode, it seems we still aren't allowing duplicate concepts, even if the concepts are defined by members of different groups. I see a 'This concept already exists' validation error if I try to define a concept that another group has already defined and I see this despite the fact I can't see that concept. It essentially makes certain concepts unusable for some groups and they don't really know until they hit a validation error. I don't know whether this is desirable but it seems counter intuitive to me.

There is no commentary on this case on the issue, so I'm just raising so we can discuss. It would be ideal to come to a conclusion on what has the most value to the end users under the different group modes and also to highlight why teachers might user separate or visible groups modes in the first place. For example, If a teacher is using separate group modes, do they expect each group to be able to enter any concepts it likes? It's hard to evaluate without this information.

Some other things we'd need to consider if we decide we want to go down this path:
 - What happens with duplicate concepts in the case of visible groups? Do we still allow members in different groups to create concepts of the same name?
 - What happens with linking when a user it in two groups both containing the concept 'cat'?

*2.* There are no testing steps covering groupings, nor discussion of it. What is the expected behaviour when I select a grouping from the select?

To be clear, I think we're pretty close with this one. The linking looks well considered and the presentation of the group selection is good. We just need to fully explore all possible cases.

I'm going to reopen this issue for further discussion of the above point and I encourage watchers to please add their 2c on the matters too.

many thanks,
 Jake

Summary: Allow viewing permissions control on database activity comments
Description:
In the database activity, improve the control of comments left against entries so that it can be set to show all (as it is currently), show to interested parties (i.e. only the submitter and recipient of the comment), or hide all. This could be done in the database settings page and apply to all entries in the database. Pseudo-code for the above would be something like:

If (user is student) then
  if (setting is 'All') then
    show all comments
  else if (setting is 'Interested') then
    if (user submitted comment) or (user owns entry) then
      show comment
    else
      hide comment
  else
    hide all comments
else (i.e. if role is teacher or administrator) then
  show all comments

This would be usedul in peer review type exercises where students are required to review each others' work but the comments should remain private between the two parties involved. Would also allow teachers to view peer reviews and maybe at a later date assess the peer reviews.

Summary: New arrangement of "published" categories in 1.9
Description:
About the new system for publishing question categories within *course* categories by Jamie Pratt, in 1.9.
This looks better than the previous possibility of publising a question category from one course to ALL other courses on a moodle site.
It's a pity that a unique term, CATEGORY, has been retained to apply to COURSE categories on the one hand and QUESTIONS category on the other.
The logic of the new system is based on the hierarchy of Course categories and sub-categories.

Example. On the site of a School, course categories are organized as follows:

CATEGORY FORM 1
-- COURSE01 -- French (teacher Joseph)
-- COURSE02 -- Maths (teacher Sinus)
-- COURSE03 -- Maths (teacher Cosinus)
...
CATEGORY FORM 2
-- COURSE03 -- French (teachers: Joseph and Nathalie)
SUBCATEGORY -- -- MATHS
-- -- COURSE04 Maths (teacher: prof Sinus)
-- -- COURSE05 Maths (teacher: profs Sinus and Cosinus)

In FORM 1, if profs Sinus and Cosinus want to share questions, they can post them to the context CATEGORY FORM 1, but then the French teachers will also view those Maths questions, for which they have no use.
In FORM 2 things are better, because a MATHS subcategory has been created, allowing profs Sinus and Cosinus to share their questions without bothering the French teachers.

Unfortunately this new publishing system does not address a problem I have expounded quite some time ago. In the above example, French teacher Joseph does not have a repository anywherewhere on the school site where to publish all his questions, to share them between ALL OF his own courses (and his own courses only).

There is of course one solution to this problem, using the present system, and that is the creation of one category per teacher for the whole site. But that is not an option, because it would destroy the "normal" arrangement of school sites, which are usually arranged by FORM LEVEL and SCHOOL SUBJECTS. In other words, what I would like to see, not instead but alongside with the present categories scheme is just one more "automatically created" category: "Courses I teach" (something similar to the _Courses I've taught_ Import option in the Course/Administration block). See attached. I have no idea whether this simple addition might entail a simple or (most probably) complex programming work...
Joseph
Comments:
13/Aug/07 10:21 AM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;Sorry, what you are asking for is almost impossible. 

What Jamie has implemented is only possible becuase it builds on the existing hierarchy in Moodle: Site -> Category -> Subcategory -> Course -> Activity - which is the same as the hierarchy used by roles and capabilites. 

Now, it is up to you how you arrange your courses into categories. Arranging them by school year does not sound very useful for me, because, as you say, it jumbles up unrelated courses.

You could get almost exactly what you want if you organised your courses so you have one category for each subject, with sub-categories for each teacher.

Or, if you trust your colleages, just give everyone a question category at the top site level, where they can put their questions. Everyone can see everyone elses, but is that really a problem?

Summary: "Total grade" for a user should use only non-empty grades in average
Description:
One of the major problems we have always had with the old gradebook was that students would have one or two assignments graded by their teacher, and then see that they had a total grade of something like 5.6% in the course. Our teachers would then get emails from students asking why they were failing the course. The fact that the total grade calculation includes non-graded assignments has caused significant confusion for both teachers and students at our schools. Our students expect to be told an average of the graded assignments only, and use that number as a measure of how they are doing in the course.

I was under the impression that the new gradebook would fix this longstanding issue, but 1.9 beta still appears to have this problem.
There is a setting to only "include non-empty grades" in averages, (as in MDL-10480, I think), but this only seems to affect column averages, not row (student "total grade") averages. 

Since that code regarding column averages is already in place, I assume that it is not too hard to add this option.
Comments: 16/Aug/07 6:01 PM;557058:04670d95-8ea4-4705-9d43-683a4fdf2d81;The last column is a TOTAL, not an average ....

16/Aug/07 6:26 PM;712020:c0f63291-bcc9-48de-8afe-7295b893b34f;I see that, but for our purposes the total is wholly irrelevant. Unless the student is exceptional, the total will never be (equivalent to) 100%, so the total is not useful for tracking course progress. Since our students work through courses at different paces, the total is not useful as a means of relative comparison. Finally, a total does not answer that basic question that graded students want answered, which is, "if I continue at this rate and level of effort, what will my final grade be?"

Thus, I was expecting an average column where the total column is. Is there an easy way that I've missed to get a course average to appear site-wide (or even course wide?) in place of the total grade (which should be hidden from students to avoid confusion)? And for that average to only include graded items?

21/Aug/07 8:50 AM;712020:99232190-cc45-465f-941a-15beba607136;My school, too, has been waiting for a running average grade for the students. We're hoping the new gradebook will finally give us this long-awaited feature!

21/Aug/07 7:34 PM;712020:31584592-4e63-4822-b0af-1fe00b101d77;Hi, if you just want an overall mean of all activities, you can put all grade items under a category, and choose "Mean of non-empty grades" as aggregation. That will create an average column. The course total does not need to get involved. Cheers, Yu

Summary: Make block add/remove and edit permissions more consistent
Description:
Blocks have methods user_can_addto and user_can_edit which let the block determine whether the current user can do certain things (perhaps via a capability check).

At the moment, user_can_addto only controls whether a user can add an instance of the block. However, a user who is not allowed to add the block can delete it. Thusn, if they made a mistake, they can't undo the action.

I want to change it so that user_can_addto controls both adding and removing.

Similarly, I want to change it so  user_can_edit controls the ability to show and hide the block, as well as the ability to access the configure instance form.

By default, both these methods return true, and no core blocks override them, so making this change should not break anything, and I think it makes the functionality more logical. Therefore, I think I am going to go ahead and check this in.

I'll post in the block and general developer forums so people know this is going on.

Summary: Conditional get support for stylesheets
Description:
Today the stylesheets generated by individual themes set an Expires header which allow them to be fetched directly from the cache until expiry. However when the cache expires they have to be refetched, even if they haven't changed. This usually means about 100kB (20kB if compressed) unneeded network traffic every ten minutes.

I've provided a patch that implements conditional get. If the stylesheets haven't been modified since they were last requested, only a 403 Not Modified response is provided.

For this to work, the style_sheet_setup function should no longer be called with time() as the first argument, from the individual styles.php-files in the themes.

Summary: The file overlib.cfg.php currently does not need to be a PHP-script
Description:
The file calendar/overlib.cfg.php does not contain any php-code.

Because it is a script it cannot be automatically cached. This means that an extra HTTP-request always must be sent when it is included.

Since this script is to be executed in the midst of page loading, before displaying the calendar, page rendering is delayed by this request. In Mozilla and KHTML based browsers, and in Opera,  this means that anything displayed after the calendar might be delayed. In MSIE6 this means that the rendering of the whole layout table might be delayed.

I suggest that as long as it contains no php-code, the overlib.cfg.php is renamed overlib.cfg.js. Then the web server may serve it together with headers that allow it to be cached.

This could be handled via param modifers to the various image rendering scripts (pluginfile.php and draftfile.php) or just to the lib/filestorage/stored_file.php file (ie. readfile method). This would allow for different sized images to be produced dynamically and saved.

Some issues to contend with:

- auto-generating images scripts do not permit any sized image to be produced as it can expose a vulnerability
- html resizing can be used to 'trigger' the image generation, with considerations to previous point
- typically this feature is most useful within the context of the htmleditor and should likely be performed when a user requests a lighter image be produced.
- system-wide defaults can be established so that administrators have control over the general size of images being produced and whether the default is to produce a lighter image, nevertheless the ability to opt-out is also available.
