10/Mar/08 2:39 PM;70121:d701ab32-f09d-436b-b7f4-ea87829df75d;John:

Let's see where we might have consensus on this and where there might be a difference that needs to be worked out:

1.  From previous versions of Moodle to the present, teachers have valued the ability, within a course, to go in as a particular student and see their view of the gradebook, to post an assignment for the student that might have been sent by email (etc.), to close quizzes that the student might have failed to close, and to generally see the course from the perspective of a that student.  It would be nice if that were retained (it was one of the first features we added back when we went to 1.9).  I am not as competent on the algebra of roles as you are, but a course context makes at least some sense as these things are the types of things a teacher does in the context of administering their course (without dismissing that this is a particular user within the course context).
2.  The loginass is disabled to teachers by default in 1.9 and the warning icons correctly indicate the danger.  This default should remain so that assigning this capability requires affirmative action by one with that ability.
3.  The actions that a teacher can do have at least many limitations that make sense.  For example, a teacher can not go in as that student into another course and see their grades, make posts, etc.  It seems that at least a partial solution is to see when these restriction's don't make practical sense.
4.  A teacher should probably not be able to send a message from that student and that feature should be eliminated from the bundle of capabilities with loginas.
5.  We probably disagree about the importance of changing user profiles.  As a practical matter, teachers might do this when a student changes his name to something like "Batman".   I don't personally find this a problem as part of the bundle of capabilities when someone is allowed to loginas -- that is one of the reasons for giving the role.  Recommended solution:  Require that a teacher also has the ability to Edit user profile in the course context.
6.  We might need to explore where there is some middle ground in terms of the practical aspects of assigning capabilities.  From a pragmatic standpoint, if we make it too difficult to give teachers the features they need (like needing to have an admin assign roles one by one and restricted to the course level for each student teacher pair), then they may "solve" the problem by giving every teacher sweeping roles beyond the current arrangement.  And that would be bad.

So, I would suggest starting by addressing #4 and then #5.  And I would wonder next if there is a creative solution to #6 that still gives us this very valued feature, or as an alternative consider that sometimes practical solutions trump ideal theoretical solutions to real world problems -- something I regularly discuss with my math students:)

10/Mar/08 8:14 PM;712020:ad2b5cc1-3b42-4b54-a8b7-54d6da0ce992;Gary, 
Once again, thank you for a clear and concise presentation of the issues.  I agree 100% with the practical necessity of allowing teachers to login as students.  I don't have a problem with teachers changing student profiles, or even sending messages as students.  I just want it to be done using the roles system in a clean way, and with greater security

By the way, congratulations on your use of the term "algebra of roles," a term that I have often wanted to use, but hesitated because I knew not everyone would understand what I meant by it.  I'm glad that there is someone else who does, who appreciates the need for such an algebra, and who can therefore appreciate my discomfort with loginas, since it breaks the rules of the algebra.  You get a permission (loginas) in context A (course) which magically gives you the ability to do things in another context B (user); yet A and B are disjoint contexts!  It is as if addition weren't commutative when adding certain 'special' numbers.   So when you say (in 5) "Require that a teacher also has the ability to Edit user profile in the course context" it makes my head spin.  The user profile is in the user context, not the course context.  Do we really want to add another "special case" to the "algebra of roles?"

Here's a proposal that partially solve the problem.

Propose a new capability moodle/COURSE:loginas (note: COURSE, not user) defined as "the ability to login as a student in a course."  This capability would be useful in a course context and would enable the user (typically a teacher) to login as any participant in the course, but be effectively jailed in the course context.  If you have moodle/COURSE:loginas = Allow, the "Login as" buttons would appear in the Participants list, not on users' profile pages.  Moodle/course:loginas would NOT give the user the ability to do anything in the user context  (e.g.,edit the profile, send message, make blog entries, create user events, etc.).   To do such things would require permissions in the user's personal user context.  

I would feel comfortable giving any teacher moodle/course:loginas because it gives her control over precisely things she already has responsibility for.  If the teacher wants to edit the student's profile, she needs to have the appropriate permissions in the user's personal User context.  I believe that capabilities for such actions already exist separately, so they could be chosen buffet style.  Yes, there would be a moodle/USER:loginas.  If you have it, you see a "Login as" button on the user's profile page, and if you press it you get a full login.

Anyway, that's how I think roles are supposed to work: separate permissions are needed to do things in separate contexts. 

Of course the problems you identify in #6 remain: how do we give teachers those permissions in the user context in an efficient way (the same issue as with Parent).

Re your #2: Any teacher who can override at least one role can give herself any permission she wants, including loginas.  There's no need to trouble the admin.  This is a basic security flaw in Moodle, not specific to loginas.

Summary: Moodle doesn't log file downloads via file.php
Description:
(I did this locally, tim requested it for core.)

As far as I can tell, file downloads (file.php) are not logged unless it comes through a resource link. For example, if you make an html page and you link to a bunch of resources, these are not logged. If you put an mp3 file online and use the multimedia filter to link to it, this is not logged... etc.

File.php is also used for image downloads. Logging these might cause performance problems, however it should be ok to log downloads of other file types.

I attach a patch to file.php that makes it log all downloads except:

1) jpg, gif, png
2) byteserved files (except for first chunk)

They are logged with module 'file', action 'download', and info equal to the filesize in bytes. This is useful when calculating statistics.

This change works independently but requires me to do MDL-13761 in order for the links in log screen to work.
Comments: 11/Mar/08 11:49 AM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;The result would not be accurate due to lifetime, right? :-(

11/Mar/08 11:57 AM;712020:6b88c3ef-8cf9-460d-8340-b589a07a8543;If you mean that it won't correctly log if the same person downloads the file twice then you are right yes. But for different people downloading the file, generally it would log each one (except in rare cases where ISP caches it etc).

You can also use this log data to track bandwidth consumption of particular files (we are) which is why I put filesize in the info field. Obviously in that case it is appropriate to only count things that the server actually has to deliver. I haven't done a UI for this. Summary: Gradebook does not consider group members only functionality
Description:
When using groupings, new functionality lets a teacher assign resources and activities to groupings, thus making them only available to certain groups of users.

This is not reflected in the gradebook - 

Create a few groups and at least one grouping, then assign one of the groups to the grouping.  Create a graded activity and assign it to the grouping.
When you look at the gradebook, the activity is listed under all the group views, and if you edit the category and uncheck 'Aggregate only non-empty grades', then this item will be counted as a zero for students that are not in the grouping.

I think the best answer is that items assigned to grouping need to have some sort of visual indicator that they are assigned to a grouping, editing on that item should be disabled for students not in the grouping, and there needs to be a check of some sort so that activities assigned to groupings are only included in any grade calculations if the student is part of that grouping.

Not sure if the gradebook should change according to the group display - or if this may need to be an option.  It makes sense to NOT display the grouping activity if you are looking at a group that isn't part of the grouping, but that may lead to confusion if you're trying to line up gradebooks for different groups and forget that it's a grouping-specific activity.

Summary: database module renaming
Description:
I propose the following renaming of this module (see forum discussion http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=91480):

Entry -> Record

Tab renaming:

Short version: List - Record - New - Formats - Fields - Templates 
Long version: View list - View record - New record - Edit formats - Define fields - Import/Export 

In the long version of the tab naming, the form "Upload entries from a file" should pass to the last tab, and should be expanded. In its present place, most of the users have trouble to find it. 

I can reformulate the http://docs.moodle.org/en/Database_module according with these names, after they are done.

11/Mar/08 11:52 AM;557058:aefadb44-443a-4323-97b5-367d90764f30;I thought about this some more. I believe that we should have all tabs either a single word, a noun only, or two words, with action word. That is

List - Single - New - Formats - Fields - Templates

or

View list - View single - Add entry - Edit Formats - Define Fields - Import/Export

While the former is more compact, I tend to believe that the latter will be more self-explanatory for more users and will likely translate better into other languages. 

Field and column are used mostly interchangably. Entry is indeed ambigous since it may refer to a whole line but also to a content of a single field. Using rows (in parallel to column) or records (in parallel to fields) makes more sense. 

Replacing Templates with Formats, I believe, would add a lot to understanding of the module. As discussed in the forum, those things have to do with formatting the data for viewing. In some sense, one can refer to that as templates, one it is not so clear and can be easily misconstrued.

I am less certain about replacing Presets with Templates. However, preset has for me more connotation with properties rather than fields and formats. Database template is more clearly referring to basic database configuration, all except field content.

Naming the last tab import/export would allow moving the batch import of records from under the "Add entry" tab, where it is hidden for only those in the know. It would further allow to cleanly add the export records function, which is for some reason missing. Having two separate tabs, ´Templates and Import/export, one handling templates and another handling records, would be an alternative, in some ways even better than having all under a single tab.

Summary: Course sub-pages
Description:
There should be a way to organize course resources/activities into course sub-pages. A course sub-page would include the basic course interface with the sidebars and topic outline boxes, but the topic contents would be unique to that sub-page. The sub-pages would seamlessly inherit all of the course's roles/enrollments and groups by using the same course ID as the main course page.

I tried using meta courses to pull this off, but it just wasn't a complete solution, since groups weren't inherited and grades were inconveniently separated. The sub-pages would simply be extra pages of topics within the same course, with no need for duplication in the database. It would allow more organizational freedom for courses with a lot of content.

A bit of background: I'm developing the Moodle site that will run the official prep course for the California High School Exit Exam (CAHSEE). This site targets students who are having difficulty passing the exam. Many of these students also have difficulty using computers and get overwhelmed by the giant page of course materials. The course creators strongly wish for the ability to create separate pages of course materials for each section of the course, since each section also contains several topics, each with its own resources and activities. This is all too much to reasonably fit into a single course page, yet the meta course system isn't adequate to address our needs. A course sub-page system would be a much more elegant solution, and I believe others would equally find it useful for very large courses.

26/Jun/19 3:10 AM;712020:1da72c25-8b36-4d92-b796-3886276dac6c;I agree that it would be better to keep this functionality separate from a course format. Flexible Sections is destructive to section contents and ordering, so many sites are reluctant to allow it, as even trying it once permanently alters the course data in ways that have to be manually repaired if one returns to the previous course format. Additionally, Flexible Sections doesn't work on Moodle Mobile, isn't updated for new versions of Moodle very quickly (as it is a third party plugin), and is missing some commonly requested functionality, e.g. the ability for students to expand and collapse sections (only the teacher can expand/collapse).

The problem is most evident in fully-online courses lasting a semester or more. The "Collapsed Topics" format with "weeks" parameter is very useful in these courses, as it automatically arranges sections by weeks and allows a student to focus on the activities for a specific week, but within that week, there may be several sets of related activities that would benefit from being grouped together. For example, when I taught statistics, I often had two major sub-week components: a set of videos and references about the week's topic, and then a group consisting of an Assignment, a sample spreadsheet File, a "Quiz" that served as a self-check rubric, and a forum to discuss the assignment. I grouped these together by indenting them, but students sometimes found the list of links per week somewhat overwhelming. In "intensive" summer courses, the problem was more extreme. The problem is also exacerbated on smaller screens.

A general interface change could address this by adding two features:
 * Add expand/collapse controls on the <ol> and <ul> list CSS, so all indentations in the course page automatically become subsections that can be collapsed
 * Add a "view this in separate page" control to <ol> and <ul> so the user can choose to view any level of the course tree on its own page.

These controls could then be leveraged by all course formats and could be addressed consistently across themes.

In particular, this would help to minimize clutter in "Section 0," which always displays at the top of the course, even if one is using "view one topic per page." Section 0 is often the natural location for documents such as the syllabus or course policies that may be accessed rarely after the course begins, yet still take up space at the top of the page for the rest of the course. 17/May/18 3:37 PM;712020:1da72c25-8b36-4d92-b796-3886276dac6c;One of my first tasks at Moodle was to summarize the types of plugins in the database. There are *many* different 3rd party plugins for helping to administer group membership:
 * Group Choice (the one we use in the MOOC and MEC, allows students to self-select into an existing group using a Choice-like activity)
 * Fair Allocation (more sophisticated than Group Choice in that it tries to optimise selection, but doesn't assign to groups automatically)
 * Team Builder (assigns to groups based on responses to multiple questions, may be abandoned)
 * Group self-selection (lets students create as well as select groups)
 * Grouptool (provides a waiting list feature, can automatically make n-person groups, etc.)
 * Groupoverview (makes groups and groupings visible to students)
 * Groups and Groupings (makes groups and groupings visible to students)
 * Group Members (makes groups and groupings visible to students, facilitates messaging)
 * Auto Group (assigns to groups based on user profile info)
 * Group formation (assigns based on a pre-defined questionnaire)
 * Group Management (students can create as well as self-subscribe to groups)
 * Automatic enrolment in groups (abandoned)
 * CSV group import (probably abandoned, but one of several plugins that try to provide an "easier" interface to administering groups and groupings)

There are probably even more plugins that I have missed. To me, this says that we need better group management tools in Core. Based on the list above, I would suggest starting from Grouptool, as it has most of the features in the different plugins, though it could be valuable to add the ability for students to create groups (e.g. Group self-selection, Group Management) as well as the profile features of Auto Group (e.g. assigning to groups based on a student's major field of study or department in an organization). If we also allow assignment to groups based on gradebook scores, we would be able to use a "[quiz with subscores|https://docs.moodle.org/34/en/Quiz_Subscores]"  (or even just a quiz or activity result to make lots of content visibility based on membership in a "needs remediation" group).

31/Aug/09 12:35 PM;557058:ad4396bc-c0c2-4271-b0a9-df80010113dc;Daniele - I am finally getting back to this issue. I am thinking that the ability to import pictures should be part of the normal import. The first challenge comes from the fact that importing is usually via a csv file. Currently something like:

 name,height,weight
  Kai,180cm,80kg
  Kim,170cm,60kg
  Koo,190cm,20kg


I think that we should be able to do something like biggestlosers.csv:

 name,height,startweight, finalweight,beforepic,afterpic
  Kai,180cm,160kg, 80kg,kaibefore.jpg,kaiafter.jpg
  Kim,170cm,100kg, 60kg,kimbefore.gif,kimafter.gif
  Koo,190cm,30kg, 20kg, koobefore.png, kooafter.png

In terms of implementation I would say that if there are image files we allow that the csv file also be a zip file. The zip file would be processed as follows:
If it only contains one csv file then unzip and process it
If it contains multiple csv files then unzip them and process them reporting all errors found but continuing on to the next one (do not halt on errors)
I think all of the images should be stored in an image or pix folder with the name of the csv file being a subpath - in order to keep pictures separated from each other. 
As the csv file is processed, if it comes across a field like beforepic which is a picture type field, then it will attempt find the picture for example /pix/biggestlosers/kaibefore.jpg (I think it should look for all of the standard picture types jpg, gif, png) and use the first one that it finds. 

The next question I have is how to handle alternate text. Should that be a separate field? If so, how do we indicate it and differentiate from the other fields or do we simply make it space. 

  Kai,180cm,160kg, 80kg,kaibefore.jpg Kai's before pic,kaiafter.jpg Kai's after pic

Personally I like enclosing the fields with double quotes:

  "Kim","170cm","100kg","60kg","kimbefore.gif Kim's before picture","kimafter.gif Kim's after picture"

But it may be clearer if we do something special to separate the image name from the alternate text.

  Koo,190cm,30kg, 20kg, koobefore.png (Koo's before picture), kooafter.png (Koo's after picture)

I deliberately used the apostrophe and raise the question of enclosing the fields as a reminder that we will have to be careful as filenames might contain spaces or other characters, alternate text may contain quotes from parents writing things like: My "little" darling, etc. 

I also think that if we get import working this way then we should also get export to work this way so that it dumps the image files and creates a zip file. 

I realize this may be getting a little bit away from what you were hoping, namely, just having a bunch of images that get inserted but ultimately I think this will better suit the needs of those using database activity module. Thanks for helping me to sort out what this should look like and how to handle these issues. Once we have a clearer idea of how we want this to work then I can begin playing with code. Let me know what you think of these ideas and of course if you have some ideas and suggestions of your own please add them. 

Peace - Anthony

Summary: download_file_content $timeout option is only a connect timeout in url mode
Description:
download_file_content has a $timeout parameter. When in emulation (Snoopy) mode, this is the 'read timeout', but in Curl mode it only sets CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT, the connection timeout, and not CURLOPT_TIMEOUT, the hard timeout.

I have made a patch. Some notes about it:

1) I made the current timeout parameter control the read timeout. This makes Snoopy/curl behaviour consistent (changing curl to do what snoopy did).

2) I changed the default to 5 minutes (300) in case people are using it to download largeish files.

3) I added an extra 'connect timeout' which defaults to 20.

The reason for making the normal, first timeout parameter the read timeout one is that (i) you probably won't need to change the connect timeout unless you want to make things really short e.g. link checker, (ii) current code probably expects the timeout parameter to work, which it won't in many cases at present.

Connect timeout doesn't do anything if using a proxy (well unless your proxy is down), this is documented. [Another reason for focusing on 'real' timeout.]

I'd suggest fixing this in 1.9x if possible.

I forgot to note above that I also made the connect timeout work (as a connect timeout) in snoopy (by setting an otherwise-unused private variable) although I haven't been able to actually test this.

If somebody gives me permission to put it into 1.9 (or just head if you like) I'll do so.

Summary: Split edit tag and manage tag capabilities better
Description:
We had a complaint from our QA people that the "edit tag" link was only available from tags on your user profile, not for other sorts of tags.  This is more visible because we've got the course tagging installed already.  

I've given my users the tag:edit capability but not the tag: manage capability, and the code displaying the link does this:

(has_capability('moodle/tag:edit', $systemcontext) && (tag_record_tagged_with('user', $USER->id, $tag_object->name) ||                has_capability('moodle/tag:manage', $systemcontext))

What I think we need really is a better split between what edit and manage capabilities control. Summary: General Improvements to Quiz Reports
Description:
The quiz reports have not been substantially revised since at least Moodle 1.6. This means the conversion to roles and capabilites was somewhat superficial, and the interface has not been converted to formslib. Elsewhere in Moodle there have been improvements that these reports could benefit from, for example the moodle_url class, and some of the features implemented for the new gradebook reports in 1.9.

Bringing the quiz reports up to the standard expected in Moodle 1.9/2.0 would greatly simplify long-term maintenance of these reports, and so reduce costs long term. The will also mean that people who learn how to write Gradebook reports will then easily be able to write Quiz reports, and vice versa.

Summary: Quiz: Allow individual exceptions for date/time and time limits on quizzes (extended time)
Description:
The ability to provide extended time for particular students or to provide scheduling exceptions for particular students has been echoed at various times in the forums. This will likely require some changes to the database; however, I think it would be well worth it given the frequency with which this topic arises.

 I have categorized this as a both belonging to Quiz and Accessibility since the addition of this feature would allow for teachers to better meet the needs of their students whether it be students with accessibility issues or from working in a second language. As such, I have prioritized this as major.

There are many reasons why a teacher might like to provide exceptions for a quiz. I would envision a special interface that would allow the teacher to manage time exceptions. They are able to select the student(s) and set alternative dates/times and/or time limits. For example, student3 should be given 15 minutes on a 10 minute time limited quiz. Student 2 should be allowed to open and close the quiz a day later than the default for the other students. There are various scenarios that I think could be handled by this and it would then simply be a matter of checking for exceptions when the student goes to start the attempt. I know that Tim had done some work a little while back on cleaning up the code for attempts. I would be interested in comments, suggestions, etc. 

Peace - Anthony

09/Jul/08 8:14 AM;712020:6b88c3ef-8cf9-460d-8340-b589a07a8543;Anthony - I take your point that this may be more general than quiz but I don't think this belongs in conditional activities plan. Conditional activities has two parts:

1) A mechanism for determining whether an activity counts as 'complete'. [This is implemented but waiting approval for checkin.]

2) A mechanism for showing or hiding activities based on conditions (which can include whether another activity is complete, also other things such as date). [This is not yet implemented but there is a design.]

It doesn't have any effect on close dates or durations of activities. So this doesn't seem to have a relation to the conditional activities system.

(Conditional activities does relate to quiz in other ways! E.g. you might want conditions 'score 30% or lower then show this special revision activity', or 'score 90% and show this certificate', and submitting a quiz may count as 'completing' it and might show a pass/fail indicator.)


I think a general system (outside quiz) that handles overriding close date is as follows:

1) Table to store the overridden/extended dates e.g. mdl_course_modules_extensions (cmid, userid, newdeadline)

2) UI for teachers to add to/remove from this table, i.e. select a student, select an activity, enter a new date.

3) Existing code that uses close dates (in quiz or whatever) changed to call a special function like:

get_effective_deadline($whatquizthinksitis,$userid=0)

ie when checking deadline, you get the quiz's close date as before ($whatquizthinksitis above), but pass it to this function, which substitutes in the extended date if necessary. For performance reasons extended dates for a student could be cached in session.

Note this does not provide a 'proportional' way to do it i.e. you can't say 'give one student 1.5x the time' or 'give one student 2 weeks extra on every event'. Those are much harder to achieve and probably not worth effort.

Maybe this would be a good feature for Moodle 2.1. But I'm pretty sure it's not part of the conditional activities system :)

Summary: Minor improvements to add_to_log()
Description:
Was playing with MDL-14257 when I saw some things that could be slightly improved in the add_to_log() current incarnation:

1) The update of lastip and lastaccess (user table): The query es executed ALWAYS, no matter if it finally ends updating the record or no. Proposal: perform the ( $timenow - lastaccess > 60) condition in PHP (using the $USER->lastaccess) variable. And, of course updating it if the record is updated.

2) The update of timeaccess (user_lastaccess table): We always perform one query + one update, no matter if the update finally changes anything or no. Proposal: Fetch also the timeaccess in the query and then perform the ($timenow - timeaccess > 60) condition in PHP.

That way we'll save TWO updates per add_to_log() call, that is, indeed, a lot!

My only concern is about to update $USER->lastaccess continuosly. Not sure if if affects recent activity and so (I guess no and lastlogin is used instead). But better to confirm it.

Ciao :-)

PS: Feel free to reassign to me if you think it's ok and you want me to implement.

Summary: Make it possible to add conditions (IF) to grade calculations
Description:
I understand that when calculating the grade for a category or total grade in moodle 1.9, it is possible to use various formulas:

http://moodle.org/help.php?module=grade&file=calculation.html

However, it does not appear to be possible to use an IF formula (condition) as can be done in Excel.

It would be very useful to be able to calculate the total of x number of graded activities, but not include the scores of those activities that are less than a certain %.

So for example, if there are three graded activities for which students must get 50% or more, the formula in Excel would be as follows:

=SUM((IF(A1>=50,A1,0))+IF(B1>=50,B1,0)+IF(C1>=50,C1,0))

where A1, B1, & C1 are the three graded activities. Here, A1, A2 & A3 are added together, but if the score of any one activity falls below 50%, it is treated as 0%.

For example:

   student1
	activityA1: 30
	activityA2: 80
	activityA3: 70
	Total: 150 (Not 180)

the total for student1 is only 150 (not 180) because his score for quizA1 is less than 50, and so is treated as zero, so 0+80+70=150

I know it's possible to indicate a "Grade to pass" for any item or category, but this seems to only change the background colour of a score: green for pass, red for fail. It does not effect the category score to which that item belongs.

So, I can see three possible ways of achieving this goal:
1) make it possible to use the 'IF' function in the gradebook as in Excel
2) make it possible to remove from the total calculation any grade that falls below the designated 'Grade to pass": this should be an option, not automatic
3) make it possible  for each activity module to return 0% to the gradebook if the score falls below a specified amount - probably the least practical solution

Why would this  feature be useful?
Short answer = motivation
In activities that students can do (i.e. submit) more than once, they would be 'encouraged' to achieve more than a bare minimum. For example, in a course in which there were many quizzes, it would be possible for a student to pass by doing very well in just a few quizzes, and then doing lots of other quizzes badly. Yes, their average  would be pulled down, but because they had done a few very well, their average may still be high enough to pass. Allowing the teacher to specify a grade below which certain activities must not fall will assist teachers to motivate their students.

11/May/09 11:29 PM;712020:d1749269-36e4-4686-a1f9-549e1379b852;Nicolas,

Thanks for your comment on this issue.

Yes, I agree that solution 2 makes most sense. It allows teachers to convert low scoring assignments to 0%, so that students are penalized for performing badly. Also, it doesn't require teachers to learn the various IF equations associated with the Excel IF formulas.

That said, including IF calculations in version 2 would be welcome, since this would make the Gradebook even more useful, i.e. a teacher could use the conditional formula to do many more things, not just convert less that x% scores to 0%.


Note to other people coming to this "New Feature" suggestion: In the Moodle Gradebook it is already possible to remove low scoring activities from total scores so that students are NOT penalized for x number of lowest scores. 

The original suggestion here is to make it possible to make conditional calculations (using IF formulas). Just one of the advantages of this is that it would be possible to penalize students that had underperformed. Or, put more positively, 'incentivize' students to perform well, by encouraging them to get at lest x%.

A workaround for the issue Otakar Prdlik raised is:
if a = grade in percent form
then let x = min(1,round(a,33))  => if a<33 then x= min(1,0)=0.  if 32>a<66 then x=min(1,1)=1.  if a>65 then x=min(1,2)=1.

My issue that brought me here, which was to see if there was an IF statement that I could use as for Prdlik but taking into account that I have groups in my course as well... well that was unresolved... but I have a work around for that too for anyone else who needs it:

Issue: groups with different grading calculations in the same class (worked around by having assignments with different codes for each group then adding all the grades) combined with need to have overall course grade of fail if one important assignment is failed.

Workaround:
let g1a(i) = grade of group 1 for ith assignment, g2a(i) = grade of group 2 for ith assignment
g1x(i)=round( g1a(i),50 ); g2x(i)=round( g2a(i),50 )
Then final score = (sum over all i( g1a(i)*weighting(i) + g2a(i)*weighting(i)) ) * (product over all i( max(g1x(i),g2x(i)) )

Summary: Provide triggers that cause automatic role assignment when a user enters a context
Description:
It would be nice if Moodle provided triggers that admins could set in any context, which would cause a specified role to be automatically assigned when a user with certain characteristics entered the context. For example, one of the characteristic could be authentication method.  This role could be in addition to a default role (e.g., Auth user, on entry to System, Student on entry to course), or in addition to a default role.

See the following discussion for a use case 
http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=92537
Comments:
08/May/08 5:47 PM;712020:f4aad3ea-cbec-4935-8843-3d55aac0a669;Assigning to Martin Dougimas... for his consideration.

Thanks for the report, John!

07/Jul/08 8:14 AM;712020:ad2b5cc1-3b42-4b54-a8b7-54d6da0ce992;Ger Tielmans provides another compelling use case for this feature in http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=70539.  Ger wants to control Block visibility on the MyMoodle page so that parents see only the Mentees block.  In his scheme (which automates parent account creation and Parent role assignment), parents are distinguished from other users by their usernames, which are of the form parent_<child> where <child> is the child's username.  A trigger that matched the username with the R.E. parent_* could be used to assign a role in the System context that allowed parents to be distinguished from other users.   Currently, all logged in users are Authenticated users in System, and there is no way to distinguish them.

09/Jul/08 6:07 AM;712020:ad2b5cc1-3b42-4b54-a8b7-54d6da0ce992;Another use case for this feature can be found in http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=100873. An administrator wants to prevent students from creating blog entries, but allow teachers to do so.  There is currently no way to do it automatically, and there are no good workarounds.

26/Jul/08 9:24 AM;712020:ad2b5cc1-3b42-4b54-a8b7-54d6da0ce992;Maybe "trigger" is an unfortunate term.  If I filed the issue today, I might call it "user defined user policies"

Imagine a third tab in the roles user interface in each context (Locally assigned roles,Override permissions, **User policies**).   In this tab you could specify one or more (predicate, role) pairs.  The interpretation of each pair is:

if <predicate> is true, assign <role> to the user

It must be possible to evaluate predicates when the user logs in so the information can be loaded into the USER->access structure.  Here are some useful predicates:

* RE matches user name
* RE matches specified field in user profile
* user has a particular role

Like standard user policies, the user may have to log out and log back in for a user-defined user policy to take effect (for example, if the user changes a field in his profile).

The third example above (user has a particular role) is particularly valuable, since it makes assignment a viable alternative to overriding.  For example, I can define a user-defined user policy in a Forum context "If user has the Student role, assign the ForumModerator role."  This is particularly valuable in System, where there is no override (we have many use cases for this).

Summary: The course category hierarchy should be reflected in CSS classes on the body tag
Description:
If a course is within a category, that should be reflected in the CSS classes to allow it to be styled appropriately. The category id number could be used, combined with some text e.g. "category-1" and added as a class to the body tag.

If a course is nested within one or more categories, then all of them should be added to the body tag as classes. To ensure that the CSS cascade works properly the designer should ensure that the CSS for the lower level categories comes later than the higher categories (assuming that you wish them to override).

This would make it much easier to make subtle style changes via categories. We're currently trying to theme over a hundred departments, which mostly involves just changing a prominent header image and have implemented something similar just by adding PHP code to the header.

Summary: Put 400x200 pixel "screenshot.jpg" files in all standard Moodle theme folders.
Description:
== The Suggestion ==

I suggest that you use 400x200 pixel screenshot.jpg files for all the themes that are in the standard Moodle package.

== The Reason Why ==

1. The "theme selector" will load faster if there is a "screenshot.jpg" file in each theme's folder.
2. You can more easily see how themes compare, if the screenshots are all taken from given course.
3. You can completely see the theme without needing to scroll horizontally and vertically within the page. (The page is optimized for 400x200 pixel images, otherwise scroll bars appear.)

== Attachment: The "screenshot.jpg" files already done ==

I've attached a zip pack with 400x200 screenshots already made for each theme that comes with Moodle.

You may use them "as is" or just use them to see how effective this suggestion is.

Or use them all now with the idea that you may want to replace them with other screenshots in the future.

Perhaps the only one that you might not want to use is "chameleon" since it is a theme meant to not always be the same so having its appearance generated each time may be better.

== Also Attached: A Screenshot of How the "Theme Selector" Will Then Look ==

This is a screenshot of how the "theme selector" will look when all screenshot.jpg files are 400x200 pixels.

Summary: Centralize output to browsers to prevent timeouts...
Description:
Browsers, after some period of inactivity (i.e. not receiving data from server) use to timeout, dropping the connection. This applies to practically all browsers with different timeout periods.

Some Moodle operations (backup, restore, upgrade...) are really long operations and it's undesired to allow the browser to stop in the middle of the process.

For backup & restore one basic backup_flush() was implemented, adding some output and flushing buffers. This has worked since ages ago.

So, I think we should have some sort of function like:

browser_keepalive($seconds=10)

to be inserted within long processes. 

That function will be responsible to output 300 whitespaces + \n (linefeed) each $seconds seconds. And flush them.

Having it centralised will be better and consistent for future improvements (weblib sounds like a good destination).

Ciao :-)

Summary: Switch standard icons to Tango-based icons
Description:
The Tango icon library proposes both an interesting naming scheme and a coherent iconset.

First ... I like the iconset, but it's distributed under a cc-by-sa-2.5 license, so I sent an email to the FSF "licensing hotline" to ask if it could be included in Moodle.  I was just told there is no problem including icons under this license in Moodle.  So, good news for themers : we can use Tango icons.  The iconset comes with 16x16, 22x22, 32x32 and scalable images.

Second, the Tango naming scheme is now used in xfce, gnome and kde.  If we used the same naming scheme, we could (easily?) use icons made for these frameworks (among others - openoffice, pidgin, gimp and others also use either the same icons or the naming scheme). This would require significant work to move/rename each icon (there are 229 icons in Moodle 1.9).

Tango project: http://tango.freedesktop.org/Tango_Desktop_Project 
The iconset can be seen on http://tango.freedesktop.org/Tango_Icon_Library (files are available by cvs)

Summary: Update userid field of mdl_data_records table on each record edit
Description:
In the current Moodle 1.9+, we have the template tags ##timeadded## and ##timemodified##, but only ##user## and nothing like ##usermodified##. That is no problem as long as ##user## corresponds to the user who last modified the entry, but currently it always returns only the user who originally added the entry.

A code such like
"Record last updated at ##timemodified## by ##user##"
would thus not work as expected in a template like the singletemplate.

This is a problem for me, since I (as the site admin) import many existing records through a CSV file, which cause all records to be "owned" by me. Users with the role Teacher can edit all entries, but it doesn't get saved which user made the last edit. Thus, I propose to change the user ID in the appropriate SQL table (mdl_data_records -> userid) on every update.

Summary: Fake block HTML is not consistent, making it more difficult to create themes
Description:
There are two issues with fake blocks:

1) Calendar has fake blocks, but doesn't even use the print_sideblock function which is supposed to ensure consistent display.

2) print_sideblock does not ensure consistent display. Real blocks always have <h2><div class="title"> around the heading text. print_sideblock relies on users to pass this in, however all uses (except by the 'real' blocks) do not. [This is also a minor accessibility issue, since headings should be marked as headings.]

My solution for 2.0 is:

1) Change calendar to use print_sideblock

2) Change print_sideblock so that if you pass it plaintext (something without a div tag) for $heading then it automatically adds the HTML above around the $heading. However, if you pass complex HTML (as is sometimes required, for example when a genuine block displays its control icons or already has the above styling) the behaviour is unchanged.

3) Make minor changes to some themes so the calendar styling isn't broken after this change

Summary: Replace table layout with div
Description:
Currently Moodle uses tables to generate the page layout. While they do appear to work, tables are not intended for page layout, and divs offer more flexibility and customization with the evolving web standards.

The proposed solution is to replace the layout table with floating divs.
A container div is required, with margins on both sides set to the block width (these margins can be optional based on whether there are blocks on the page or not). The left column would be stored as a floating div, followed by the right column, followed by the actual content for the centre.

This system has already been tested with 1.9 on our production site: http://www.thomashaney.ca/

The main issues are that it would require a rewrite of many themes. With that in mind, it would be best to mark it for 2.0 rather than 1.9.x so as to not break existing themes.

I can provide a patch for the standard theme .css files and the index.php as an example.

Summary: Allow the user  to enter a Description when making an override
Description:
When defining a new role, the user can enter a description.  However overriding a role, there is no description text box.  I think one is needed.

I have a use case for it.  It is one that should become common when users understand roles better.

Administrator creates ten dummy roles Dummy1 ... Dummy10 having all capabilities Not set, and grants ability to assign and override these roles to selected teachers (10 is not a magic number, but it should be enough so that no new dummy roles ever need to be created).

If a single activity needs N variants of student behavior , where N < 10, the teacher can override N Dummy roles to effectively create N new roles that can be assigned in the activity context.  

Example: Suppose you want to set up a Choice activity such that

students in group 1: can Record choices but not View choices
students in group 2: can Record choices and View choices
students in group 3: can View choices but not Record choices
students in group 4: can neither Record choices nor View choices

You will need 4 dummy roles.  You will override Dummy1 ... Dummy4 in the Choice context

Dummy1: mod/choice:record = Allow, mod/choice:view = Prevent
Dummy2: mod/choice:record = Allow, mod/choice:view = Allow
Dummy3: mod/choice:record = Prevent, mod/choice:view = Allow
Dummy4: mod/choice:record = Prevent, mod/choice:view = Prevent

In the Choice context, make the following role assignments:

to students in group 1: assign Dummy1
to students in group 2: assign Dummy2
to students in group 3: assign Dummy3
to students in group 4:  assign Dummy4

Without a description, it will be difficult for the teacher to keep track of the variants.  The descriptions would read:

Dummy1: can Record choices but not View choices
Dummy2: can Record choices and View choices
Dummy3: can View choices but not Record choices
Dummy4: can neither Record choices nor View choices

Where should these descriptions be displayed?  The current table in the override roles tab displays the role Name, Description, and #Overrides.  I would replace the #Overrides (which is not very useful) by the override description.

it's about social constructionism.  http://docs.moodle.org/en/Pedagogy

Basically any open discussion that is related to the subject is :

   - an opportunity for others to learn all kinds of things just by watching that discussion
   - an opportunity for saying things once instead of many times  (saving time for more interaction)
   - an opportunity (for students) to reflect more deeply before posting questions that could waste the teacher's time (because they know other students will see it).

So you miss out on all these network effects.  Many teachers coming from an offline world may not even realise the power of well-used forums.

Summary: Capability to select default formating when HTML editor is disabled
Description:
Very often people with disabilities (and even people without disabilities :-) ) disables the HTML editor, which currently does not is fully compliant with accessibility guidelines. This way people can use markdown, HTML or plain text format according to the selection made on the drop down menu appearing just below the editing text area.

However, it is needed to select the preferred format each time a text is entered. Would be really useful, especially for people with disabilities, to have a setting in the user profile were the preferred format can be selected once the editor is disabled.

Probably the current User profile drop down list "When editing text" could be used to specify the preferred format:

Use HTML Editor
Use Standard Web form - Plain text
Use Standard Web form - Markdown
Use Standard Web form - HTML
Use Standard Web form - Moodle Format

Once selected, when editing text the default format will always be preset accordingly. However, user can select other format in case of need.

Summary: Consistent Navigation for Moodle 2.0
Description:
(I think Tim Hunt came up with this idea originally some months ago, but I really like it and want to see it 2.0.)

The idea is to move all the "modes" for a module into consistent tabs that are visible all the time (assuming you have permissions).  This way we could make roles much easier to get to, and we'd also remove some of the inconsistent buttons and links we have.

So for example, the Assignment module would have a consistent top row of tabs all the time:

  - View
  - Submissions
  - Update activity
  - Assign roles 
  - Override permissions

Quiz module top row:
  - Info
  - Results
  - Preview
  - Edit
  - Update activity
  - Assign roles 
  - Override permissions

Thoughts?   Votes?

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

06/May/08 3:23 PM;557058:7e1bfbd6-11e7-4915-81fc-98f57783686a;As I'm working on for french MoodleMoot 2008, writing a conference on how to develop an activity module, I was categorizing modules in two main ranges : 

The first one I call sequential modules, where activity is proceeded by phase of actvity as linear process or maybe a more complex workflow. The second one I call it "sub application", which has rather a parallel access or tree-organisation just as a Web site. 

Maybe the design of a sequential module may not have need of tabs, as only one screen of the module might be available at the same time for one user class. Of course more complex modules should merge both approaches, having a major sequential design but with accessories that might be accessed all the time. 

In my older devs, Techproject was typically a sub-application, with very little workflow activity. Brainstorm (unpublished yet, but largely reviewed) was typically offering both, configuration selectable. This is the typical example of switch where tabs are required and help a lot usability when all phases of brainstorming may be accessed simultaneously, but where a teacher might choose to use it as a full sequential process. Tracker is such a sub-application, as was logical for that kind of function. Flashcard is getting rather a sequential module switching between two action screens for the student, and becoming a more parallel device for the teacher that has to access to status screens. 

Usually, as a module is reviewed and enhanced, gaining in complexity, there are IMO very few situation where a pure sequential or pure parallel access may survive. We should quite always need both, even if the major behaviour of a module twicks to one or the other side.

Question : what would we do with a single tab bar, when functional design concludes we do not need more ?

Anyway, I vote in favour !!

I think this feature should be in all Moodle pages where tabs are used. 09/Aug/08 2:58 PM;712020:08373fc8-9132-4753-b7fe-5f615d31546d;I also think it is a good idea to 
a) keep navigation across modules as consistent as possible (as long as it does not interfere with each module's specific use cases) 
b) have configuration in a more obvious place than it is now (with a more obvious label than "update this [modulename]")
c) do something about the fact that quiz configuration now has a set of tabs of its own (there is no clear return route for users from those tabs to the main quiz set of tabs, or communication about the relationship between the two different sets of tabs).

This change seems to have a chance to solve the above. However, I do think that deciding to just "add tabs" as a means to improve usability is very superficial. There are big issues in the configuration screens, which will not be solved by this change. If a major change is introduced (the configuration is moved to another location), it would be best to take a good look at the configuration screens so that major changes need not be introduced in many subsequent versions. With the following, my intention is not to bash others' valuable work, but to demonstrate the fact that a superficial decision of whether configuration should be a tab or a button might not address the actual issues.

Expressed in another way, there seems to be no notion here of taking the actual usage scenarios into account, although this is an UI-level change. Moving functionality into tabs may help, adding consistency probably will, but unless you look at these changes in the context of the use cases and more broadly, the actual usage scenarios, you don't even know if this is really that relevant to users or not. Of course some kind of a personal context is -- to some degree -- in the heads of everybody discussing here. However, knowing whether or not that is representative of real users  would require communicating the actual scenarios and use cases affected by the current state or the proposed change. 

That said, what comes to my mind quickly are that the different options should be analyzed throughly and it should be determined with real users. To get a bit deeper, different information gathering methods can be used to:

Summary: Activity Module: Allow modname to contain an underscore (_)
Description:
I was working with the ILP project which contains two modules that I had suggested be renamed to ilp_target and ilp_concern; however, then we discovered that it chokes with /course/mod.php because the variable must be a PARAM_ALPHA which excludes the underscore (_). For consistency, it would be good if modules could have the underscore. Tablenames, blocks, function names all allow the use of the underscore so this issue caught me by surprise. 

I'm filing this under course since that is where I found it but it may be more far reaching. Since Petr indicated that the issue is not trivial and that we may be able to address it in 2.0 I am initially assigning to him.
Comments: 08/May/08 10:16 PM;557058:ad4396bc-c0c2-4271-b0a9-df80010113dc;Working with the ilp project, I initially thought it would be helpful to add a prefix to the module name similar to how we do with blocks; however, I was not aware that the underscores were stripped away. We have since renamed but the hope is that using the underscore for a module name will be allowed in Moodle 2.0 to be consistent with Moodle naming conventions. In other words, since the underscore is used in tablenames, blocks, etc. it makes sense that a module should also be able to use it (IMHO). Peace - Anthony

17/Dec/10 10:51 PM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;Hello, I am sorry, modules will never be allowed to contain '_' because we need this for BC.

Petr

18/Dec/10 3:37 AM;557058:ad4396bc-c0c2-4271-b0a9-df80010113dc;Petr - For consistency, would it helpful to not allow any plugin (blocks, filters, authentication types, etc.) to contain underscores? Even if we do not prevent the underscore in the code for all plugins, should we consider making that a recommendation when naming or does it make sense to just not allow the underscore for activity modules? Peace - Anthony

18/Dec/10 5:02 AM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;The problem is that the 'mod_' is option for modules, when normalising the component names we look for '_', if it is there the stuff before the first '_' is type of plugin and the rest is plugin name. If there is no component it is either core component or module, allowing '_' in modules would break it completely, that is why it can not be allowed.

I would vote to forbidding '_' in all plugins but it is already in multiple official blocks and other plugins, upgrade would be painful, the contrib is full of plugins with '_' too.

Petr

18/Dec/10 10:43 AM;557058:ad4396bc-c0c2-4271-b0a9-df80010113dc;Thanks Petr - It sounds like we live in an imperfect world. Perhaps we could just make a recommendation to avoid the underscore in plugins with the understanding that it will not work with activity modules. It sounds like trying to fix the existing stuff would be more work with no significant benefits other than theoretically being more consistent. I'm certainly OK with leaving things as they are. Happy Holidays. Peace - Anthony
18/Dec/10 10:50 AM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;I am personally recommending no underscores in plugin names for many years. Thanks for your attention to details like this!
18/Dec/10 10:50 AM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;Merry Christmas to you too.

Checks UTF8 back links
Fixes an UTF8 issue in querylib.php avoiding searches with special utf8 chars to match

Summary: Add 'Update External: On Update' option to the Username field and the Password field in External Database User Authentication
Description:
Would like to have the option of both the Username field and Password field being updated in the External Database when the user changes them in their profile from within Moodle. Perhaps add the "Update External: On Update or Never" option as setup in the Data Mapping section of External DB Auth.

FURTHER EXPLANATION:
I have an e-commerce site that sells a course, and after payment is confirmed, it populates a database with required info that Moodle needs to create a user and enrol them in a course.

Upon testing this method (external db auth), it turns out that a user that is added this way CANNOT change their own password (even when ChangeOwnPassword is set to Allow). Even if an Admin tries to change their password from their profile page, it appears to be changed (no erros or warnings), but the password is not saved in the mdl_user table or in the extrernal db. That means that every time a user wants to change their password, they would have to request the admin to do it, and the admin would have to make the change directly to the external database. Very time consuming and unecessary for admin, when it could be accomplished completely by the user.

Currently, in Moodle 1.9, it does not appear that a user can even change their own username (I will be filling another issue with a request for this feature). If the admin tries to change their username from their profile page, you get and error that says the external db can not be updated, and their username is not changed. Once again, this would require an admin to make the change directly to the external db. Again, very time consuming and unecessary for admin, when it could be accomplished completely by the user.

Summary: Allow YUI files to be loaded from Yahoo directly
Description:

Summary: Add 'Overridable' option for grade items
Description:
Category and course grades can be overridden easily, but reverting to a calculated grade is not obvious for the average user.  Having an 'overridable' option, default to false, for category and course grade items would prevent accidentally overriding these grades (which normally should not be overridden), but would allow instructors to override those grades if there were special circumstances.

At a minimum, this would require:
Adding an 'overridable' field to the grade_items table, tinyint(1), default 0
Modifying the grade_item->is_overridable() function to look at that value when the grade item is a course or category grade
Modifying the form for grade items to have an 'overridable' check box if the grade item is a course or category grade
Adding help, localization strings, etc.

Comments:
10/May/08 2:31 PM;712020:7bece4c6-79e9-4e60-84a1-ecfd85016866;The attached patch allows specifying a number (integer >= 0) of decimal digits a number should be displayed with. The number of decimals can be specified within the "preset.xml" file (which is part of a "preset.zip" preset), as "param1".  For example, to define a number field for a Moisture in % with 2 decimals, we can use:

<field>
<type>number</type>
<name>Moisture</name>
<description>Moisture (in %)</description>
<param1>2</param1>
</field>

For example, a stored number of 0.999 will be displayed as 1.00 and 0.002 will be displayed as 0.00.

Summary: Add CSS class to blocks with editing controls so that these can be themed differently
Description:
When creating themes it is sometimes necessary to know whether a block contains editing controls. Unfortunately there is no way for a theme to tell (apart from literally the existence of the 'controls' div, which is fine, but you might need to make changes at the level above).

A potential mistake (which I made) is to assume that the .editing class on BODY provides this information but it does not. This class is only reliable on course view pages. Everywhere else it may or may not coincide with editing status of blocks.

I have attached a trivial patch (affects one line of code, uses existing logic) which adds the 'block_with_controls' class to existing classes if a block contains editing controls. Effect on generated html is as follows:

1) If block does not have editing controls - no change

2) If block does have editing controls - 

Before patch:
<div id="inst21" class="block_html sideblock">

After patch:
<div id="inst21" class="block_html block_with_controls sideblock">

Summary: Packaging assignment module for better documentation structure
Description:
Assignment as a core module should be reviewed for phpdoc generation correct packaging : 

all module root level php files should present a :

/**
* file description
*
* @package mod-assignment
* @category mod
* @author initial author if known (optional)
* @contributors list of known contributors (optional)  
* @license http://www.gnu.org/copyleft/gpl.html GNU Public License (unless other licensing)
*/

/**
* Defines and requires
*/

Subplugins such as assignment types should have an additional @subpackage tag

/**
* file description
*
* @package mod-assignment
* @category mod
* @subpackage assignmenttype (example)
* @author initial author if known (optional)
* @contributors list of known contributors (optional)  
* @license http://www.gnu.org/copyleft/gpl.html GNU Public License (unless other licensing)
*/

If some code use MVC pattern, we have added an @usecase tag that could be used to list all handled use cases (UML meaning).

These blocks MUST be first block of comment just under <?php opening line.

If the first code construction that follows is a class or a function, it should have its own comment block.

The form :

function afunction($parm){
/// some comments
}

should be deprecated, using phpblocks instead : 

/**
*
* @param type $parm description
*/
function afunction($parm){
}

Thanks for helping improving documentation structure.

Note1 : that all php files should be headed, not only lib ot locallib. This ensures all local function or structure defines will be correctly packed inthe phpdoc.

Note2 : please all packaging should be at least commited for 1.9 and HEAD branches.

To summarise the situation for anyone arriving here:

There are three things that affect login instructions:
# $CFG->logininstructions
# $CFG->registerauth
# The "none" authentication type

This simplified code should explain what happens:
{code}
if auth plugin is enabled then
    [loginstepsnone,moodle] is shown
else if $CFG->registerauth = email then
    if $CFG->logininstructions is set then
        $CFG->logininstructions is shown
    else
        [loginsteps,moodle] is shown
else if $CFG->registerauth is set to anything
    $CFG->logininstructions is shown
else
    $CFG->logininstructions is shown
{code}

So that could be considered some what complex, but it does allow for the instructions to always be customised either by setting logininstructions OR by customising the language string.

I have not doubt this area could be improved, however doing so would be blocked by first tiding up the login code in Moodle.

Summary: Proposal for improving Moodle Forums
Description:
Currently Moodle's forum allows a very simple moderation of discussions. In a constructive environment, where forum is one of the most important instrument for confrontation and collaborative construction of knowledge, this represents a very relevant problem: currently, off-topic messages can not be moved to more appropriate (already existing) ones and if they have in their hierarchy some other in-topic messages, there is no possibility of separating the first and conserving the others in the original topic. Moreover, Moodle's forum lacks of some forum tools (for example, "sticky" discussions) that usually give moderators more possibilities to organise and manage discussions in an easiest and profitable way.

We would like to transform Moodle's forum in a more usable and complete instrument, in accordance with constructivist ideas and satisfying teachers/moderators needs to manage communication in a collaborative community of students. 

Our proposal is to increase moderator's power by adding some features to his role, including the possibility of intervening on the hierarchical order of discussions (and between different discussions, too). This would allow to freely move a single message.

In the case this goal appears to be technically unviable, a simpler option would be to develop these features on a chronologically ordered forum. In this way course managers can choose from two types of forum: a hierarchical forum, characterized by more rigid structure, and a chronological one, more flexible and adaptable to moderators needs.

Changes specifications

Student role:
The same capabilities students has now with the addition of a quotation system (students can quote the message of someone else to answer in a more detailed way, without losing the context).

Teacher role:
The same capabilities Teacher has now with following additions:
He can move a single message from a discussion to another that already exists, without having to decide if messages under it are to be erased or taken all to the new discussion. He can manage messages in the hierarchy changing their level and dependence.
He can make sticky some discussions (they will be always displayed at the top of the discussion list). The sticky attribute can be added or removed in any moment.
He can decide to close a discussion: students cannot add other messages if a discussion is closed. This attribute can be added or removed in any moment.

Non-editor teacher role:
He can move messages, make discussions sticky and close them, but he can't edit nor erase messages.

Forum properties:
Under the avatar and the name of the user, in the left side, should appear also his role in that forum: student, teacher, etc.
A discussion may be erased (if there is only one message in it  - to erase a discussion you must first erase or move all its messages).
Confirmation check on erasing and editing.

Capabilities to be added for forum roles:
Edit messages (and messages' subjects)
Erase messages
Move messages
Move discussions
Erase discussions
Close discussions
Make discussions sticky

Summary: Quiz Autosaving Feature
Description:
As the name describes, this is an autosave feature that should silently save the student's answers per interval. This is to protect the students attempts in case of interruptions such as power outages, etc..

Olli Savolainen made an interim solution for this one using Prototype but there are bugs encountered. Here's the link: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=74710

25/Sep/08 1:56 PM;557058:b7c950df-9ed7-4280-88ce-d2250178a711;We have had people writing quizzes from dial-up in remote locations, we have also had students writing quizes and final exams using the quiz module, some of these quizzes span multiple hours.

20/Feb/09 1:06 AM;6164fac872f6970069bb7701;This would be great for Forum posts, assignments, etc. We did add this feature our assessment module (http://development.moodlerooms.com/mod/resource/view.php?id=210&subdir=/Assessment_Module_for_1.9 ) and the code works quite well -I've requested this be a GSCO code project to add auto-save in other places.

18/Mar/13 10:17 PM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;We are hoping to implement this in time for Moodle 2.5. There are actualy two ways we could do this:

1. Client-side, using the DOM Storage API (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/DOM/Storage) from HTML 5. Since this is all client side, it does not add to server-load, and we can auto-save every few seconds when students have changed something.

2. Server-side, by making and Ajax call to the Moodle server. This does add to server-load, but is better protection for the student, becuase the data is on the server, and they can continue their quiz attempt from any computer without dataloss.

Our plan is to do both, because each approach has its own advantages.

I am about to create two sub-tasks for these two things.

Summary: Patch fixing various HTMLarea issues
Description:
This patch fixes an issue with pasting in HTMLarea, in addition to a few other bugfixes.

1. Unnesting block tags

When pasting multiple-paragraph text into HTMLarea in MSIE, HTML blocks may be nested. This is usually a problem when paragraphs are pasted into a heading, which is often the case when attempting to paste at the beginning of a document. It is non-trivial to circumvent the problem or fix the formatting, without resorting to html-mode.

This patch adds unnesting of block tags to the word html-cleaner.

Mozilla does not have this problem, as it doesn't allow nesting as a result of pasting.

2. </><//>-style garbage removed. (MDL-13451)

Issues with getHTML (the innerHTML-replacement) of HTMLarea combined with nasty behaviour of MSIEs tag soup parser may generate garbage that doubles in length each time the text is saved (or html-mode is entered).

The problem is, MSIE won't parse unknown tags as content tags, for example <foo></foo> will be two empty nodes in the DOM, which will be considered content-tags and each will be closed in the generated HTML. By only closing tags that are recognized by MSIE, the problem will no longer occur. Also old tags generated by the byg looking like </>, <//>, or <//foo> are removed.

3. Ctrl+rightarrow keybinding removed (MDL-13451)

The input handling of HTMLarea is screwed up. The same function handles both keydown and keypress events, not taking into consideration that the generated keyCode varies depending on the event type. (See http://unixpapa.com/js/key.html for a description of the mess that is javascript keyboard handling.)

A simple fix is provided by commenting out this keybinding (which is supposed to be Ctrl+').

4. <personname> tags are now removed by the Word cleaner

Empty <personname> tags are sometimes produced by Word, and are a common cause for the symptoms of MDL-10657.

   if (file_exists($basedir) && filetype($basedir) == 'dir') {

Summary: Improve the quick grade GUI in assignment module - popup window navigation GUI and pull-down grading menu
Description:
OK, the proposed improvement was initially caused by changes to assignment module to correct the problem caused by using the "Gradebook Plus v2" (GBPv2)..

The GBPv2 gradebook allow users to change a grade to whatever they want (no error checking). If you put in grade of 555 (out of max 100), it still takes it, and then when you go to assignment, you won't see any grade (it would show "NO GRADE").

To fix that we (SFSU) changed the grading in assignment to use text fields (originally it was pull-down menu allow from 0-100). Our instructor also provided some feedback that they LIKE the "text fields" better (for entering grades). However, because the assignment module was not originally designed for text fields, so we must now do error checking. So grading in assignments is limited to 0 - 999. If assignment uses scales, then the scales dropdown will appear.

We also changed the behavior of each of the buttons available in the popup menu. (again based on feedback from our users and support team). See attached screenshots for "BEFORE AND AFTER"

[New GUI have these buttons:]
Previous - New button that saves changes and moves to the previous student to grade
Save Changes - Used to save and close the window. Now just saves the data and refreshes the window with feedback
Cancel - Closes the window
Next - Saves changes and moves to the next student to grade 

Thoughts or comments? I have also included a quick and dirty patch (originally designed for 1.8.2), which probably need some rework for moodle 1.9.x. Note that we also added a help button right next tot he navigation GUI...(not included in the uploaded diff)

Summary: Forum module review of comments headers for better phpdocs documentation structure
Description:
Hi Martin !! your turn !! ;-)

Forum as a core module should be reviewed for phpdoc generation correct packaging : 

all module root level php files should present a : 

/** 
* file description 
* 
* @package mod-forum
* @category mod 
* @author martin dougiamas (and others)
* @contributors list of known contributors (optional) 
* @license http://www.gnu.org/copyleft/gpl.html GNU Public License (unless other licensing) 
*/ 

/** 
* Defines and requires 
*/ 

There are no subpackage concerns for forum
If there are in other module, we try to resolve them as follows : 

Subplugins should have an additional @subpackage (e.g. assigmenttype) "or something like that" tag 

/** 
* file description 
* 
* @package mod-assigment 
* @category mod 
* @subpackage assigmenttype (example) 
* @author initial author if known (optional) 
* @contributors list of known contributors (optional) 
* @license http://www.gnu.org/copyleft/gpl.html GNU Public License (unless other licensing) 
*/ 

If some code use MVC pattern, we have added an @usecase tag that could be used to list all handled use cases (UML meaning). 

These above docblocks MUST be first block of comment just under <?php opening line. 

If the first code construction that follows is a class or a function, it should have its own comment block. 

The form : 

function afunction($parm){ 
/// some comments 
} 

should be deprecated, using phpblocks instead : 

/** 
* 
* @param type $parm description 
*/ 
function afunction($parm){ 
} 

Message for all people I added in other posts :

Many thanks for helping improving documentation structure. 

Note1 : that all php files should be headed, not only lib ot locallib. This ensures all local function or structure defines will be correctly packed in the right phpdoc subsection. 

Note 2 : please all packaging should be at least commited for 1.9 and HEAD branches. 

Cheers.

Summary: assign tool
Description:
Dear Moodle-Team:
An idea for a new feature for moodle 1.9:

What I´d really like to see in moodle is a tool to assign different tasks from a list to different pupils.
For example: The class has to do a research and represent its results. There are 10 different topics for a class of 28 pupils  The pupils are allowed a certain choice of topic.

In reality it may work like this:
-Version 1 of assignment: Let the pupils do it themselves: Result:  all 28 pupils choose the same topic (or at least something very near to that outcome).
Version 2: Distributing the topics (teacher and class): Result: Equal distribution of topics, but using a long time during the course.
- Version 3: Giving out the directive: max 3 pupils per topic and letting them enter their chosen topic in a forum. Result: it takes a long time for the students to  chose their topic, the distribution of topics is better than in version 1, but some pupils don´t read the entries in the forum properly and so some topics aren´t chosen at all or pupils choose a topic but don´t enter it in the forum.

What I´d like is a tool with the following features:
- Teacher can enter a list of topics
- Teacher can specify the number of times each topic may be chosen
- pupil (or group) sees the list of topics and chooses one
- Each chosen topic disappears from the list, so that other pupils can only chose the remaining topics (that aren´t yet taken)

Even better: 
- Teacher can specify topics that must neccessarily be distributed in class and topics that may be distributed, but aren´t necessary for examinations. The last type of topic is only seen by the pupils, when the "neccessary ones" already have been chosen.
- Topic, that are "given back" reappear in the list

Best regards

Andi

25/Jun/10 6:06 AM;712020:3fe0319b-8b17-4c50-82af-457e665ef9b6;> It's interesting that it's complaining about a SQL Server 2008 Native Client ODBC Driver. What is this?
> And why is it looking for a MSSQL 2008 driver when I'm running MSSQL 2005?
Our drivers, SQLSRV and PDO_SQLSRV, are designed to be built on top of SQL Server Native Access (SNAC) ODBC API. See our v2.0 CTP2 announcement blog post that provides some details on the architecture: http://blogs.msdn.com/b/sqlphp/archive/2010/04/19/sql-server-driver-for-php-2-0-ctp-adds-php-s-pdo-style-data-access-for-sql-server.aspx

SNAC is our unmanaged code (C/C++) library implementing ODBC, it is a very robust & performant connectivity option for SQL Server, and it is designed to support N & N-1 versions of SQL Server. Meaning, SNAC 2008 will support SQL Server 2008 and SQL Server 2005. At this point it will be good to note that "R2" releases don't change major version number, so SNAC 2008 R2 can also be used with our drivers. This provides my team to link to the "right" version of SNAC ("right" being influenced by several factors) to best support our PHP community.

This is why we linked to it in the commit comments too, and on our v1.1 & v2.0 CTP2 download pages. Arguably, we could include the SNAC driver with our package but it is best for the DBA/developer to decide which one best fits their needs.

And, as Eloy correctly says, the drivers (SNAC & SQLSRV/PDO_SQLSRV) always need to be installed on the machine/vm where PHP is installed.

BTW, our drivers also support connecting to SQL Azure - it's just s small connection string change. I wasn't sure how Moodle 2.0 is being positioned for the "cloud", so I didn't push for this support in this patch. Let me know if you all are interested in the SQL Azure option in Moodle 2.0 installation.

Ashay

Summary: Provide standardised way for modules to indicate their support for Moodle features
Description:
It would be nice to have a standardised way to indicate whether modules support certain features. At the moment, generally this is done by checking whether a function exists, which is not a great way to do it (and, for new module developers, can be prone to error).

I threw some code together  for the attached patch - this patch is for 1.9 just because, obviously there is no intention this would ever go into 1.9, also I'm not sure about the sketchy exception usage. So I'm not really expecting this would be checked into anything as-is, but if you think it's a good idea, I can put it into 2.0 later as part of the completion-tracking (conditional activities) work.

Basically you call

plugin_supports('mod','quiz',FEATURE_COMPLETION_TRACKS_VIEWS)

then that opens quiz/lib.php and calls

quiz_supports(FEATURE_COMPLETION_TRACKS_VIEWS)

which can then return true or false. (Some features might be defined to have values instead so could also return something other than plain true.)

If the function doesn't exist [legacy support] it returns false. 

We could also add extra legacy support if features are added eg FEATURE_CRON that could be checked the 'old' way without having to change modules, I have indicated where this would go inside the plugin_supports code.


If it was decided to make modules entirely OOP for 2.0 then this approach would not be appropriate and we would probably be better off using interfaces or something.
