Summary: Add new capability for restricting activities
Description:
At the moment, the 'restrict activities' feature of Moodle allows an Admin to restrict activities at a site-wide level, and then override this at a course level, which is good.

From what I can see though, the ability to override this requires the 'doanything' capability to be allocated to the user in the appropriate context, meaning you give them everything or nothing. What would be nice would be to create a specific capability called overrideactivityrestriction or something that allowed users to be given this priviledge at the course context.

The use case for this is to allow teachers to initially be given access to the restricted (and allegedly less overwhelming) set of activities while they are getting up to speed with using Moodle, and then when they 'graduate' to being 'advanced users' then they can override the restrictions and use all available tools. At the moment this can't be done without giving the teacher complete Admin control over the course.

Happy to hear of better ways of achieving this too :)

Summary: Hide result of hidden assignments in calendar and in "My Courses"
Description:
In many Moodle installations, there is a certain group of users ("Inspectors", "Surveyors", "Exams officers", "Administrative staff", etc.) who have the following requirements.

* They need access to all courses, or a large set of courses, at least for reading.
* They are however not students, teachers, or other "usual" course members in most of these courses - access may be very infrequent.
* They are not supposed to be Moodle administrators (no "doanything" capability).

This can currently be realized by assigning them a certain role as a "hidden" role assignment, either globally or in a course category.

HOWEVER, currently all their hidden "memberships" will show up in their personal calendar and in their "My courses" list. These can be hundreds of courses (in our case) so that the list becomes virtually unusable, and they can't find the courses that they actually teach.

To solve this, my request is that hidden assignments should be excluded from the Moodle calendar and from the "My courses" list (and corresponding blocks).

For further details, see these forum discussions:

http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=141501
http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=143571

I have made the changes listed on my site and it works well. Users my page and mycourses block only shows their course:participate courses whereas when they go to the course list they can enter any course on the list. Users also do not see course calendar events where they do not have the course:participate capability.

As for forums my inspector role has forum:initialsubscription not set as is common to admin roles to prevent emails from courses where they are not part of, how does course:view interact with forum:initialsubscription? If I want the inspectors to have forum emails (such is with my "staff information" course) I use an override on the course to allow forum:initialsubscription, as it stands the inspector can move into any course they are not course:participate in and subscribe to the forums as they see fit should they want to have forum notifications. The inspector is not prevented from doing this by the role settings.

Unsure about patch creation so here is the raw code change:

1) in moodle DB table "capabilities" insert a new record with the values (without the quotes for values of course):
id = autonumber
name = "moodle/course:participate"
captype = "read"
contextlevel = "50"
component = "moodle"
riskbitmask = "0"

2) moodle\lib\db\access.php,v 1.75.2.23 2009/12/30 17:17:09 stronk7 Exp $
After line 550 (end of moodle/course:view) add:

    'moodle/course:participate' => array(

        'captype' => 'read',
        'contextlevel' => CONTEXT_COURSE,
        'legacy' => array(
            'student' => CAP_ALLOW,
            'teacher' => CAP_ALLOW,
            'editingteacher' => CAP_ALLOW
        )
    ),

3) moodle\lang\role.php,v 1.47.2.22 2009/12/30 17:17:10 stronk7 Exp $
After line 51 (course:view lang string) add:

$string['course:participate'] = 'Participate in courses';

4) In site administration->users->permissions->define roles edit teacher, non-editing teacher and student roles (or roles if you have more custom roles which are equivalent to teachers and students who work in the courses) and set course:participate to ALLOW. Other roles are left as unset, unsure of the effect of setting this to prevent or prohibit, it may cause issues so unset works fine.

5) moodle\lib\datalib.php (version from same release as access.php above)
After line 929 (end of "Non-cached - get accessinfo" if / else statement) replace:

$courses = get_user_courses_bycap($userid, 'moodle/course:view', $accessinfo, $doanything, $sort, $fields, $limit);

with:

$courses = get_user_courses_bycap($userid, 'moodle/course:participate', $accessinfo, $doanything, $sort, $fields, $limit);

-----------------------------------------------------------------

Summary: allow blacklist auth plugins
Description:
Without this patch, it is not possible to write an authentication plugin that prevents certain users from logging in under certain conditions, if there is another authentication plugin that will authenticate them. This patch adds a pre-authentication hook during the login process, so an auth plugin can return AUTH_DENIED at that point and prevent any further possibility of login via another plugin.

This patch also introduces a class named auth_status, and uses it to return the state of authentication (currently just status, message, errorcode) from the pre-authentication hook and then keep it all in one place. Since this patch is intended for the stable release, the changes are minimized and this isn't being used extensively. But auth_status could be expanded to include more information, and it could be used throughout the login process in order to simplify login/index.php by not relying variously on $frm, $user, and $errormsg at different points.

I've also attached a very simple demo blacklist plugin that denies all authentication for a user named 'test1'.

Summary: The hard-coded raise_memory_limit("96M") in /lib/setup.php and potential issues
Description:
In some rare occasions (especially for 64 bit systems), when log in as instructor and access the "edit course settings" page, all the modified values will NOT be saved correctly, and Moodle will generate a error message:

Fatal error: Allowed memory size of 100663296 bytes exhausted (tried to allocate 81 bytes) in /var/www/xxxxx/lib/dmllib.php on line 761

When this happened, our system administrator looked into the system logs, and didn't find a spike of server memory load (for both DB server and Apache server).

The system was set to use 128MB in the $CFG->extramemorylimit and in the php.ini. However, the Fatal error was pointing to memory size of 100663296 bytes, which is 96M. This is set in the /lib/setup.php by a hard-coded value. This probably should be improved by changing this value to be controlled by $CFG->extramemorylimit (so that system administrators could change this value on the fly through the UI), or refactor the codes a little bit to avoid this inflexibility. The core issue that would trigger this memory overload still remain unknown, which would be nice if that could be figured out somehow.

This ticket was originated from this discussion:
http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=143936

And is slightly related to ticket MDL-20168.

18/Feb/10 4:42 PM;557058:49d96837-3095-4b42-acc4-4776e0c583f8;While I think this does need some attention, those values are very low and likely a hangover from previous versions of PHP where memory usage was different for whatever reason..

You can totally mitigate this issue by setting 'memory_limit' in your php.ini file to a sane value, as raise_memory_limit()' DOES pay attention to what memory_limit is currently set to, and if it's already higher it does not overwrite it.

However, having the ability to change this on the fly however is possibly a wise addition, so modifications to raise_memory_limit() to implement it is probably a good idea.

18/Feb/10 5:13 PM;712020:f4aad3ea-cbec-4935-8843-3d55aac0a669;The idea beyond $CFG->extramemorylimit was to be able to increment memory on the fly for certain operations (backup/restore mainly, also used by another script, if I'm not wrong) without having to set php.ini to one big value for all the scripts. Perhaps we we could, easily, follow this way:

# Default for all scripts, defined by setup.php = 96M
# Can be raised by optional $CFG->memorylimit for *all* scripts
# Can be raised by optional $CFG->extramemorylimit for scripts deciding to use it

Both 1 & 3 are currently implemented exactly that way and only 2 (new setting to raise *all* scripts) should be added (it just provides one "moodle way" alternative to edit php settings in any case).

Also, perhaps, instead of using "low-level" raise_memory_limit($value) calls, we should simply expose something like:

raise_memory_normal()
raise_memory_extra()

and make those functions to work, automatically and exclusively with the 1, 2, 3 settings above, i.e. forbid completely arbitrary use of harcoded values.

Another thing is, obviously, why the course edit page can need > 96MB of memory, something is definitively wrong in PHP/Moodle IMO if that's happening.

29/Mar/10 1:44 PM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;Change log (updated to match latest code):
* capability "moodle/course:view" redefined - means user may enter course without being enrolled, also is not visible, this capability is removed from the guest role finally
* new capability "moodle/course:participate" - user enrolled and visible in course
* "administrator" role removed - instead admins are list in $CFG->siteadmins
* simplified use of $doanything parameters - now available only in has_capability(), not necessary anywhere else
* hidden role assignments replaced by inspect capability and concept of enrolment and profile roles list
* new "manager" role created, all original admins at lower levels assigned this role
* new role archetypes replace old capability capabilities
* negative guest capability removed - obsoleted by inspect capability and enforced restrictions in has_capability()
* hardcoded restrictions in has_capability() for guest user account - no write access or risky capabilities (no need to use isguestuser() in so many places for security reasons)
* new $CFG->profiteroles list - those are the roles visible in the profile and participants page
* improved handling of $CFG->coursemanager roles - it is now used instead of isteacherinaanycourse()
* new API - is_enrolled(), is_inspecting(), get_enrolled_sql() - major performance boost
* undeprecated API - isguest($context) - course visitors + real guest account
* fixed group assignment code - now allows assignment for roles only for enrolled users
* fixed survey and choice - only for enrolled users
* only enrolled users are visible in online users list - it is possible to add new capability to see all users including inspectors and visitors

Definition os some terms:
Enrolled user - participant in the course, those are usually students+teachers.
Manager - somebody with full access that does not actually teach in course and does not interact with students
Visitor - somebody with a temporary guest access into course, the access is granted in require_login() depending on the course settings
Administrator - somebody administering server, has_capability() always returns true, get_user_by_capability() and get_enroleld_users() does not return them (with the exception of frontpage)

Short list of benefits:
1/ the api is compatible with future changes in enrolments (the new tables instead of course:participate capability) - it should not be necessary to modify SQL or PHP code in capabilities
2/ simplified UI - no hidden role assignments that were working only in some areas
3/ no problems with unintended modifications of admin role
4/ much better performance - finally we may query who is enrolled in course

Note: more info and explanation coming into wiki soon....

Summary: Gravatar integration
Description:
I don't know if you guys have heard of Gravatar, but I think it's a very cool idea. If you haven't heard of it, check out http://www.gravatar.com/.

I've attached a very small patch that will add a "Enable Gravatar for profile pictures" setting to the "Site Administration > Miscellaneous > Experimental" page. When the check box is checked, if a user has not uploaded a profile picture yet, Moodle will try to display a Gravatar image for that user. If no Gravatar image is found, the default profile picture is displayed.

I decided NOT to add this to the "Modules and plugins" on moodle.org, because if it's added as a setting that's disabled by default, there's no reason not to simply add it to Moodle.

Some of the credit for this should go to Piotr Majewski. He originally suggested it in http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=135968

Summary: Deny reset of forgotten passwords
Description:
Attached is a patch that allows a list of usernames to be forbidden from resetting their password via the forgot password form.  This is an added security measure to protect sensitive accounts (e.g. admin).

The list of usernames can be added to an array variable $CFG->denyforgottenpassword in config.php.  When a lost password request comes in, the patch will check if the requested username exists in the array and if found, silently reject the lost password request giving the default generic message:

"If you supplied a correct username or email address then an email should have been sent to you.

It contains easy instructions to confirm and complete this password change. If you continue to have difficulty, please contact the site administrator."

If this feature is accepted, we are willing to develop it further by moving the config variable to the database and adding a way to select users via the UI.

To enable this patch:
# In the moodle src directory:
 patch -p0 < path/to/denyforgottenpassword.patch
# Add the following to config.php
 $CFG->denyforgottenpassword = array('admin'); // Add any usernames to block to this array

Summary: Activity setting 'Available for group members only' should be added also to the course settings to enhance access control in the course level
Description:
Both groups modes, 'visible groups' and 'separate groups', include a virtual 'all participants' group which allows access to activities even to those who are not assigned to any group. While the 'all participants' access may be limited it may still be undesirable under some circumstances. The 'Available for group members only' allows for preventing any access to activities/resources without being assigned to a group. When this setting is checked  without selecting a grouping it effectively hides the activity from anyone who is not explicitly assigned to a group in the course. While this behavior may be just an insignificant side-effect of the grouping feature, it is in fact an important enhancement of activity access control. 

Adding the 'Available for group members only' to the course level may allow setting the default behavior of the course to hide activities/resources from users who are not assigned to any group. This may be useful in sites which allow self-enrollment or have auto enrollment and yet require that members be assigned to specific groups so as to control access to the activities/resources.

Summary: A progressive form of the online text activity would be very helpful
Description: In my face to face workshops, I use a worksheet where a student  decides on an issue they want to work on from their career and then answers four questions about it in essay form. i have them answer the first question, then there is some feedback and discussion, and then they go on to the next. When answering later questions on the worksheet, it's important for them to easily refer to their choice of issue and also their answers to the first questions on the sheet. I find Moodle incapable of doing this well. There are workarounds, but none of them are very effective. Online text seems to be the closest activity. So my suggestion is that there be a progressive online text variant. In that variant, the online text activity would have sections that were completed as separate activities. And for each one, the student saw what the earlier questions were and what their answers were. Another way to do this would be to permit grouping online text activities in a way that when you were working on one of them, you could easily see your responses to the earlier ones. The idea is to mimic the worksheet, which I have found very effective. I've attached a sample worksheet so you can see what I'm talking about.

Summary: Gradebook incorrectly rounds grades, including calculation of completion
Description:
The MOODLE gradebook allows the teacher to specify the number of decimal points to display for each grade. According to MOODLE Docs, this setting has no effect on grade calculations, which are made with an accuracy of 5 decimal places.  Some teachers choose to round.  If they display grades with 0 decimal points, the number will display as if it was rounded.  If  grades are displayed as both real and letter, there are situations where the grade the student sees does not match what they are expecting to see.
EXAMPLE :
Suppose 90.0000 is set as the lower bound for an A-
Suppose the 1st quarter average was calculated to be 89.5412
Average displayed when teacher chooses to display 1 decimal would be 89.5 (B+)
Average displayed when teacher chooses to display  0 decimals would be 90 (B+)
This appears as a discrepancy to the student even though it is not..

The problem is compounded as grades are used in multiple calculations. Example: 1st quarter, 2nd quarter and mid-term grades are averaged to produce the 1st semester average.  3rd quarter, 4th quarter and final are averaged to produce the 2nd semester average.  The 1st semester average is averaged with a 2nd semester average to produce the course average.  The grade with the 5 decimals was used in all calculations, but a grade that appears rounded is what the student sees leading to apparent discrepancies.

While it is true that a teacher who wants to round can override the 89.5 to a 90, this is very time consuming.

Proposed improvement:
Provide teachers with the option to specify that grades should or should not be rounded and the ability to specify the number of decimals for rounding.  This will allow them to control the precision of the numbers used in calculations in the same way that the Excel ROUND function does.

As a temporary alternative for those who need to round grades before this ticket is solved, you can do so by manually entering a formula into the COURSE TOTAL (Gradebook > Categories and Items > little calculator icon). For example, if I have two grade items, each worth 50 points, ID numbers are Assignment 1 and Assignment 2. Formula would be =ROUND(Assignment 1 + Assignment 2). If a student got 45 on Assignment 1 and 44.5 on Assignment #2, total would be 89.5 but the ROUND function would round that to a 90.

03/May/16 7:54 PM;5d5f788c3aee330d4323c9d0;All possible solutions were discussed between myself and all of the developers here at HQ. We have tried to provide a solution that while not perfect, will keep most people happy. 

Possible solutions - 

* Adjusting completion status by the decimal display setting.
** Not an accurate display of the student's real grade.
** The changes are extremely complex.
** The changes required would have to extend into activity completion code and we can only reach core activities.
** The changes for regression are extremely high.
** The upgrade path would take a long time to complete for large institutions as every grade would have to be considered.
** This new behaviour may catch teachers by surprise and we were not considering adding a setting to turn this behaviour on or off.
* Truncating the display to the decimal display setting.
** No need to change any activity code.
** Situations where completion show a rounded up number that is the same as the completion mark would be avoided.
** Changes are less complex.
** Chances of regression are reduced.
** The actual grades of students are not affected.
** We were not considering adding a setting to turn this behaviour on or off either.
*** Each grade item needs to be considered in the upgrade step, could lead to a long upgrade for large institutions.
* Adding a setting to switch between rounding the grade up or rounding the grade down.
** The general rule here at HQ is that adding more settings is a bad thing and should be avoided if possible.
** Each institution can decide if they want to keep the old behaviour or go with the new behaviour.
** The upgrade is greatly reduced and would only be looking for courses affected by the 57 letter boundary problem.
** Does not solve every possible situation.
* Flagging grades that have been rounded to a grade boundary.
** Totally different solution that has no chance of being included in Moodle 3.1
** Needs more discussion as to what the actual behaviour would be (Do we show this flag to students or not? Should the raw grade be shown or not?)
** Shouldn't require an upgrade step.
** The actual grades of students are not affected.
** Extending this flag to course and activity completion could be problematic.
** Requires discussion about whether this needs to be a setting or not.

Ideally we would like to have a consensus, but in this situation we seem to have no complete agreement on which solution to implement. Consequently we have decided to go with the current solution of providing a Site wide setting to display grades either rounded up or down.

1) Whenever a letter or completion is shown, if the number of display decimals is not enough (<=) to cover the number of decimals in the scale/completion rule... show something, an asterisk, note, hover... indicating that display rounding may be affecting perceived information
2) If possible, when such a "lack of decimals happen" (the <= above), show the corresponding grade with a bigger (>) number of decimals. Straight. That should kill any misinterpretation.

And those are my thoughts about this issue, again, let's fix a bug if there is a bug, but only if there is a bug. Summary: Change Lesson interface on Teacher Edit tab
Description:
Change the edit tab view to one that is similar to GoogleDocs, OOImpress or PPT.

While 1.9.7 edit tab view with collapased and expanded view is a huge improvement, it is not teacher friendly.

I cobbled up a screenshot using GoogleDocs to demonstrate the concept..  There is a left column and a larger center or right column, with a menu at the top.

The menu could be the current combination of icons and pulldowns.  Copy/paste would be a new feature and located on the menu.  The menu works on the context or insertion point in the left column.   

The current move function could be done via a cut/past (new icons on menu, or via drag and drop.    

The left column contains thumbnails of the pages.  This would include navigation pages such as end of branch.  Optionally consider theme outline colors for navigation (pages not seen by a student)  and/or perhaps different colors for question and branch tables (I vote to change this name to content pages).   

The left column should be able to switch views from thumbnails to an outline view, similar to collapsed view in 1.9.7 (without menu icons which now are above).  This would be more like outline view in PPT.  The left column needs to have a hide and reveal function.

The right or largest column shows the page that has been selected in the left column.  Essentially, it would be the current page edit view.  The place the teacher gives details to the content area, jumps, scores, feedbacks.  Initially I would leave the HTML tool bar just like it is in 1.9.7, above every field that needs it.  However, in the future why not put it above the right column, so that it's context is in the field which has been selected.  This would compact the view for the teacher.

That is it in a nutshell.   I am sure a massive project.

Summary: Change the name of a branch table  to Content page, impacts Quiz Description page?
Description:
The world of Lesson according to Chris, has two kinds of pages for a teacher.  Those seen by students and those not seen.  Since the ultimate user is a student,  the generic name for what a student sees should include the word  "page".   IMO, a "Content Page" is a better name than a "Branch Table".  

There is basically no difference between a multiple choice question and a so called branch table, except a "branch"  has no feedback and is never graded.   For all intents and purposes, a branch table is similar in function to a "description" question in Quiz.  In short, it is a page the student sees and is not graded.  The branch table function is to provided non-graded content with choices and jumps associated with the choice.   Thus the name "Content" page seems logical, just as we have Multiple Choice Question pages, Short Answer Question pages and so on.    For menu purposes these can be called Content, Multiple Choice, Short Answer  etc. 

As an aside, I wonder if Quiz would consider renaming the "Description" question type, to "Content" .    And this raises the concept if a Description "question" can be exported from Quiz and imported in a Lesson.  Or created in a GIFT format for import into either Lesson or Quiz.   I have never tried that , which would be a solution to something I have been squawking about for years :)

At the moment I do not have any brilliant name alternatives for what I think of as "navigation pages", such as Start Cluster or End of Branch .   I was thinking of navigation  "marks" or  "posts", or"blazes" or "cairns" or "flags" or "trip wires", anything but "pages".  

Just an idea, probably been thought of before using a different name.   And of course this name change would have a profound impact upon the documentation and help screens.  If Lesson is going to have a major make over, I would add this to the list. 

Best to all  Chris

12/Jun/10 7:23 AM;557058:04670d95-8ea4-4705-9d43-683a4fdf2d81;The key confusion is between the "Assigned roles" and the "Manual enrolments", obviously, mostly because they are independent, and the 'Assigned roles' screen contains people who are both participants and non-participants.

My GUI idea is that we get rid of the generic assigned roles screen totally, and change the distinction to enrolled participants and non-enrolled participants, with separate pages.

A. ENROLLED PEOPLE

The manual enrolment screen should be changed to a name like "Active course participants", which is all the people who are actively involved and seen in the course.  It could even be integrated with the under/index.php page but doesn't have to be.   Basically it's a table with paging and firstname/lastname selectors.  Columns are: profile image, name, email etc, enrolment method, and roles.  

A selector box (like the right hand of the old assign roles screen) lets you manually assign lots of people to this page, and there are X icons to remove them (as well as checkboxes for multiselect). 

The enrolment column lists names of ALL the enrolment methods that led to a user being here.  Of course, any added with the selector box here would be "manual" or "added by teacher".  If a non-manual method is active for any user then you would not be allowed to remove them here.

The roles column would work like the roles column does on the permissions screen.  You can add/remove roles here easily with an AJAX popup menu.


B. NON-ENROLLED PEOPLE

Since these are less common, and likely to be very few people, we can have a separate page for them.  It's a paged table similar to the above, except it will be very clear that these people are not enrolled no matter what permissions they have.  It would make sense to go here to add an observer teacher, or a supervisor, for example.

We can show inherited users from higher contexts here too, with information about exactly what context they are enrolled in.


C. MENU STRUCTURE AND OTHER STUFF

I think it's best for the manual enrolment to be integrated in the main overview as above, rather than appear as a plugin like all the other ones.  It's special.  We do still need to have configuration pages for all the other plugins, of course.  However, these are not things you visit often, so don't need to be so prominent.

We can also move the settings from the course settings screen to settings menu.  (I'm not sure about this, because I do like your forms there, but it's also good to keep this all clear in the menus with less mega-forms).

Course Administration
Enrolments 
- Participants   (---> A)
- Other people   (---->B)
- Enrolment methods   (menu)
- - Manage enrolment methods (enable/disable any of them, plus settings links to below)
- - Manual enrolments (-> page to set default role etc)
- - Guest access (-> page to set password etc)
- - Self enrolment (-> page to set password, role, days etc)
- - Cohort enrolment 
- - etc

Summary: Unit Testing in Moodle 2.0
Description:
I have some questions about unit testing in Moodle 2.0:

1. we spoke sometime ago about using PHPUnit instead Simpletest:
* is there a document about that? 
* how long does it take to be ported?
* what are the advantages to use PHPUnit? (supported by IDE, PHPUnit project still alive,...)
* what are the disadvantages? (except the fact that is going to be ported)

2. impact of Unit Testing on other part of the code:
For example: I want to test a function calling a library function. I don't want to test/run the library function. I want the library function call to return a defined result.
Problem: the library function is not in a class or is static. => I cannot Mock the library function (I cannot find a way to override the call xxxx::library_function())
Solution: I resolved this problem by creating a "manager" class, where I put my library functions. This mean that anytime I want to call a library function I need to create an instance of the manager.
* is it right? We have documentation for Mocking the global $DB (http://docs.moodle.org/en/Development:Unit_tests#Unit_testing_in_2.0) it is easy and clear, but not for library functions.
* is there other design implication about creating unit test? Do we have rules about them?

3. Code coverage
Coverage is linked to Unit Testing (http://docs.moodle.org/en/Development:Unit_tests#Code_coverage_analysis). I could see on some tracker issue that Eloy did quite some work on it :) 
* I would like to have another advertising/guidance/teaching about Unit Testing and test coverage, maybe a meeting? (Are they mandatory, how to "feel" the need to use them, what does it implicate if we don't write them,...)
* Do we expect a percentage of code coverage for Moodle 2.0?
* If we write code coverage for simpletest, is it going to work with PHPunit?

15/Mar/10 8:01 PM;557058:04670d95-8ea4-4705-9d43-683a4fdf2d81;To clarify:

If the widget feature is a very simple core feature with no GUI scripts (like formslib) then:

- lib/widgetlib.php 

Any supporting files for this can go in lib/widget/

If the feature has some GUI scripts it has its own directory (eg like blog, comment, mod/forum, local/widget etc) and then this is always applies:

- widget/locallib.php - for functions and classes that will only be used by scripts in widget directory.  No capability checks.
- widget/lib.php - for functions required by core code.  Minimal capability checks.
- widget/externallib.php - for functions and classes implementing external interface for use by other modules and web services.  Full capability checking.

Summary: Listing a course in multiple categories
Description:
A several users of Moodle need to list a same course in multiple categories. This is a strong necessary feature. Take the engineering courses for exemple: there are a lot of unit classes that match to different kinds of engineering courses and is insane to duplicate the unit classes for several engineering courses.

Is a better way to have only one unit class(called "course" in Moodle) that is related to several course categories.

So,  to compose a course categorie i can just select  the courses (unit classes) available from a list, without the need to duplicate some of then to create a new categorie.

Duplicate a course(unit class) isn't adminstrative worth.

P.S. in all dicussions about this, i think the misunderstanding resides on the terms. For Moodle a Course Categorie is composed by complete courses with all of their units inside on it. But the reality is that we have a lot of unit classes in Moodle that we want to organize to compose distinct Course Categories, without duplicating this units.

Project: Moodle

Issue Type: New feature

Summary: In-place translation (or click-to-translate)

Description:

This feature is about allowing users with language editing capabilities to click on untranslated or mistranslated strings in order to edit them.

There is a very old proposed patch about it in this issue: [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-21880|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-21880]

This blog post describes how it works: [http://abautu.blogspot.com/2010/03/click-to-translate-feature-for-moodle.html|http://abautu.blogspot.com/2010/03/click-to-translate-feature-for-moodle.html]

Another way to implement this feature may be like this:

# Modify the function `get_string()` to track all the strings used at the current page and their translations.
# Append all these strings and translations at the end of to the current page, maybe in a hidden form.
# Add a link at the footer of the page (or on the menu) that says "Edit translations on this page".
# When this link is clicked, a form or JS overlay can appear which allows to edit the translations of the strings appearing on this page.
# When changes are saved, they are stored as local modifications of the translation, on the directory *moodledata/lang/xx_local/* (where *xx* is the code of the language). For more details about local language customisations see: [https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Language_customisation|https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Language_customisation]
# After changes are saved, the page should be refreshed and the new translations should appear on it.
# The files of local language customizations (on *moodledata/lang/xx_local/*) can be uploaded to [https://lang.moodle.org/|https://lang.moodle.org/] . On "AMOS -> Stage" there is an option that says "Import translated strings from file" which allows to import these files. It is also possible to upload all the files at ones, if they are ZIP-ed.

Some other discussions related to this issue:

* [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=383289#p1547591|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=383289#p1547591]
* [https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=347843#p1463017|https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=347843#p1463017]

This project can also be seen as an extension or improvement of the [language customization|https://docs.moodle.org/36/en/Language_customisation] feature, or maybe it can borrow some code from it (for example the part that saves translations on local translation files).

 

Affects Version/s: DEV backlog, Future Dev

Component/s: Language, Translation

Summary: Allow unlimited attempts to a lesson
Description:
Where students are allowed to retake a lesson, the drop-down list on the lesson settings page allows up to 10 retakes. Because the lesson structure allows such a number of branches and learning points, in some situations (I have a few) students may want to return time and time again, especially if it is ungraded and thus a totally formative experience.

I would like to add the option 'unlimited' to the list to cater for such situations. Indeed, to me any practice lesson would default to unlimited since it has no effect on grades.

I currently work on a fix where we can select '0' in the lesson settings page and this defaults to unlimited (but only remembers one earlier attempt). Will upload the code for everyone when we have tested it a bit more.

Understandably this would clog up a database if we had to remember hundreds of attempts by students!

Do vote if you like the idea, or comment if you don't.

20/Sep/13 12:28 AM;557058:4af356f1-8e9d-44d4-81f1-2a75726709c1;I just did a quick look because of your request in the chat.

Seems sane.

The only thing I wonder is if a username get recycled before old user with the new username logs in - or the similar case: user leaves institution and loses username. New user eventually gets same username, and logs in. Gets old users Moodle account.

Might it make sense to always do a callback to the auth plugin and give it the opportunity to replace the $user object wholesale?

20/Sep/13 4:15 PM;712020:0ca3a761-806b-4d9e-b9ca-1e835a799f7b;Responding to Eric's point (and a couple of others raised elsewhere).

Currently:
1. User authenticates with Moodle
2. External system changes username
3. User logs in to Moodle + gets assigned a new account on Moodle
4. External system re-allocates username
5. New user logs in to Moodle + gets old user's account

Under my proposal:
1. User authenticates with Moodle
2. External system changes username
3. User logs in to Moodle + gets their existing Moodle account renamed
4. External system re-allocates username
5. New user logs in to Moodle + gets new account set up for them

If the old user never logs in to their Moodle account inbetween their username being changed and being allocated to a new user then we are in no worse a situation than there was before (and really, any external system should probably prevent the recycling of old usernames anyway ...).

As for replacing the $user object wholesale - if the account already exists, then the authentication plugin already gets a chance to overwrite all the existing user information (as controlled by the settings for each authentication plugin).

Duplication of usernames is not possible, as the Moodle code checks for the existence of a user with the given username and only asks the authentication plugin to search for an existing user if there is no matching username found (as a final check before creating a brand new user).

Unit tests - these will be difficult to write, as this code provides a hook to be used by addon authentication plugins, but which is not used by any of the core authentication plugins. The best test would be if it does not break any of the existing unit tests (although I cannot see any authentication unit tests that test for creating a new user when authentication succeeds).

What is not certain to me is why the plugin can't already achieve the same thing in user_login() itself and i'm not sure how exactly the plugin would reconcile it in find_renamed_user().  Also i'm not sure what impact this could have in a multi-auth situation.

01/Oct/13 3:38 PM;712020:0ca3a761-806b-4d9e-b9ca-1e835a799f7b;Dan,

The current flow of the code (after the user has entered their username + password) is:

# Moodle loads the database record that matches that username
# Moodle asks each auth plugin in turn to authenticate the user
# Once the user has been authenticated, either log in the existing user (if found in step 1), or create a new user (if not found in step 1).

Some external authentication systems allow the user to change their username (especially true if the username is an email address), but keep the user consistent by using some other unique ID for the user (which might be stored in the ID Number, might be stored in a custom profile field or, in one case I've seen, stored in a custom extra field added to the mdl_user table).

The auth plugin could look this up during the user_login function call, but the problem is that the return value from this is either 'true' (authenticated) or 'false' (not authenticated). By this point Moodle has already loaded the user object from the database (or failed to load the user object). The best the auth plugin can currently do is to authenticate the user and then allow a new, unrelated, user account to be created.

Of my code, the only line that can't be worked around at the moment is the line 4315: $user = $existinguser; (i.e. tell Moodle that the user does already exist, even though they weren't found when searching by username). The rest of the lines of code are really just for convenience (it would be quite possible for the auth plugin to change the username in memory + in the database, but as all auth plugins supporting this feature will need to do the same steps, they may as well be in core code).

An example of how an auth plugin would operate within the find_renamed_user function would be:
# look up the user details using the username against the external system
# retrieve the unique user ID from these details
# look up this unique user ID within Moodle (wherever it has been stored)
# return the database record for this unique user ID, or return false if not found (so a new user record can be created)

Note that this function would only ever be called in situations where: 
a) the given auth plugin has already authenticated the username + password combination
b) the Moodle has not found a record with matching username

Summary: Quiz Reporting by Standards or Objectives
Description:
With NCLB and so many standards floating around and being tracked, it would be a game changer at my school district if the questions in Moodle could be tagged according to different standards and then tracked in the quiz grade and gradebook.

For example, a student might take a quiz that involves 2 different standards (read a line graph; read a bar graph).  The questions will be randomly ordered, but after submitting her answers she and the teacher would be able to see he score broken down according to the two standards.  Is she getting all the bar graphs right but getting all the line graphs wrong?  Even for teachers in a non-standard based environment, this would still be a great tool to identify weaknesses.

On a grand scale, it would be amazing if it could actually track across multiple quizzes.  So after taking the 10 quizzes of the quarter, the reporting module would be able to say overall scores in different standards as well.

Finally, being able to see class trends overall would be the nail in the coffin.  What percentage of students are getting the line graph questions wrong?

It think this has a lot of potential :)

Summary: Addition of mathematical operators to the Filter(s) in Bulk User Actions (operators are <, <=, >, >=)
Description:
I suggest the addition of the ability to apply mathematical filters to be used with numeric data.  The filters suggested are "greater than", "greater than or equal to", "less than", and "less that or equal to".  Filters have been added only to the custom user profile field filtering option.

I modified the code in 

/lang/en_utf8/filters.php
/users/filters/profilefield.php

All modifications are commented with "filter added".

The ability to perform such filtering within Moodle allows a school to perform administrative tasks based upon data stored in custom user profile fields.  The method utilized however, may not be the most efficient.
Comments: 30/Mar/10 9:05 PM;557058:ad4396bc-c0c2-4271-b0a9-df80010113dc;Jason - In order to help the developers see what all is being changed, I am attaching a patch file off of 1.9. It looks to be pretty straight forward and I could see some benefit. I have not tested and unfortunately do not have time at the moment but like the idea. Could you provide a couple of actual use cases that would highlight or demonstrate the utility of what you are proposing. It is not hard to imagine but I figured your examples would probably be better than mine. Peace - Anthony

31/Mar/10 2:30 PM;712020:6e3118c6-79dd-4b65-b453-468b49fdbcb7;Anthony,

Thank you for looking at this and for creating the patch.  As for uses, here are a couple that we intend to use it for:

1. We store proficiency test and placement test scores in the user profile fields (we have them locked but visible to individual users) and would like to be able to filter based upon the value in those fields.  We can combine a series of filters to "drill down" to the exact group that we want and then export as a CSV or Excel file.  For example, we use university issued student numbers as all students usernames and the student number contains information about their department so we can filter based on department and then, with these added operators, filter out, for example, all students who got a score equal to or higher than a 60 on a specific test.  This information is used by other offices on our campus so we are asked to provide it from time to time.  Being able to generate it via this type of filter is fast and easy for our administrative staff.

2. We store other types of numeric data in the fields that is occasionally used as a criteria to aggregate groups of students into lists.  Since we store almost all of the information that is needed, and are working to store all of it, in the  Moodle database, the ability to filter it all within Moodle greatly increases our efficiency.

As for the greater than, greater than or equal to etc. filters, I have noticed that they seem to put a fairly heavy load on the server.  Creating an SQL query to retrieve the data desired may be faster but that would mean modifying the query every time the numeric value(s) needed to be changed and thus isn't practical considering the numerous various queries we would have to set up.

Jason

Summary: Clean up get_sql_sort in tablelib
Description:
At the moment, flexible_table::get_sql_sort can either be called as an instance method, or as a static method, but that last option is only used in one place in the assignment module.

Also, it does several things in one place, namely getting the list of sort columns, and then building the SQL from them. In the quiz report, we have some code that wants a list of columns, so it does get_sql_sort, and then explodes it. That is a bit silly. It would be better to have a separate method to get the list of columns as an array.

So, I am going to do a bit of refactoring to split this into separate methods. And change assignment, so the static method can be separate from the instance method.
Comments:
02/Apr/10 5:10 AM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;So, the only API changes are:

1. you can no longer call get_sql_sort as a static method.

2. in the past, if you called get_sql_sort before calling setup, you just got an empty string returned. Now, you get a coding_exception. I thing that is an improvement.

Other than that, the changes should be backwards-compatible.

Summary: stand-alone file name and permissions "sanitizer" script
Description:
I am the general moodle server maintainer at my school.  The Technology Integrator and I were brainstorming the other day about some alternative uses of Moodle.

One thought that he had was to be able to grant FTP access to the ./moodledata folder for teachers, r/w permissions based on the courses that they have access to (context: teacher) so that they could upload a semester's worth of assets in one shot- and then link to the appropriate resources as needed thoughout the semester.

This would also help us to have the administrative secretary be able to upload school-related forms.  The idea is that the user can set the FTP to sync to the folder, and when they change a file locally it will sync to the MoodleData folder- and it will have the latest revision.

I shot down the idea for the teachers because the bulk-uploader module works beautifully, and we have users upload up to 64Mb per upload.

However, for a select group of administrators (the second example) it could be a VERY useful feature.

anyways- that's all doable currently.  The problem is, when we created a test course and played around with it, we noticed one very glaring problem quickly.  Lack of access to the files API results in file names and permissions not be "sanitized" and references not being added to the database for the proper file name.

I'm sure you've seen how moodle works with improperly named files: it doesn't.

so the request is this: make a standalone php script that can be run called "sanitize.php" or something similar, that recursively scans the moodledata folder and files and does the following:

1) sanitize file names
2) add references in the database for correct file names
3) update references in courses/site files
4) fix permissions

I realize that depending on the size of the moodle instance this could be a fairly burdensome script- that's why I'm not requesting it to be added to CRON, but be standalone like replace.php- use it just when you need to.

I feel like this + a short guide for users on appropriate file names could allow this to be done.  And the ability to check for bad file names/permissions through Moodle would be a nice feature on its own.

I will resume how the default end date works from the lowest level to the higher one:
# At database level the default value is 0 (no course end date)
#* Any other default value that this would be wrong as the end date always depends on the course start date.
# At Moodle API level create_course() (and testing/development callers - data_generator::create_course()/tool_generator_course_backend::create_course) the default is no course end date as well.
#* This default is good for backwards compatibility and third parties
# At UI level Moodle admins create new courses using Moodle's UI through "Site admin" > "Courses" > "Manage courses and categories" > "Create new course". Here, by default, we enable the "Course end date" setting and we set the default value to a calculated value that depends on the default course format
#* Course creators can always disable the end date
#* We encourage people to set the value if an end date make sense for them

It is important to note that only a portion of all courses are created using Moodle UI, sites with many courses have synchronization processes to create courses automatically from external information systems. In those cases courses are created through create_course (defaults to no end date)

All this is the rationale behind the current design, although it is not perfect because:
# Data generators should mimic default moodle values as much as possible. Testing uses Moodle APIs to create courses, which defaults to end date disabled. In behat case this is less ideal than when writing phpunit tests because we want the elements (courses, users...) created using a data generator to be as close as possible to a course created manually by a user
# We would like to encourage people to set the end date, even if they create the course through an automatic sync process

IMO the current design has a good balance between backwards compatibility (we shouldn't annoy 3rd parties with a new setting when there is no real benefit on setting it yet) and encouraging people to set the end date for reporting purposes and all my doubts could be resumed in "Should behat data generator set a default course end date or not?"

20/Oct/10 3:56 AM;712020:eed5dc5a-21ca-43bf-ac0a-0519d4291ed4;Hi Bruno,

right now we don't quote the bind user distinguished name (DN) using the syntax mandated by RFC 2253 (we do in other parts). We have two options here:

1.- Use the RFC 2253 quoting in your setting. If the spaces are the real problem (they should work ok with Windows 2003, I have just tested it), you can encode them as \20. I.e., you should use:

{code}
    OU=Name\20-\20ORG,DC=com,DC=br
{code} 

(i.e., you need to use a single backslash, not forward slashes).

2.- We can quote the bind user DN following RFC 2253 rules when we save the settings. This is a bit more work and we can get in trouble if the admin specifies the DN already quoted (we would double-quote it, as it is a bit difficult to tell an already quoted DN apart from a non-quoted one). If we go this way, and expect admins to always use non-quoted DNs, then at least one case would be problematic: when we have a ',' in a RDN (a single piece of the DN), as the comma is the RDN separator.

I wouldn't with go option 2 unless we have to. Most people won't need it and the possible pitfalls don't offset the benefits, IMHO.

Saludos.
Iñaki.

Summary: Possible confusion for the new UI in Moodle 2.0 quiz
Description:
One thing that I have noticed in Moodle 2.0 dev is that now by default, the "Close the quiz" (timeclose) is "disabled", thus it make sense for the "After the quiz is closed" (closedoptionsgrp) to be grayed out. However, here is a possible use case:

1. The instructor click on the "Enable" checkbox of "Close the quiz" to specify a quiz close date (timeclose), which then will re-enable the whole closedoptionsgrp. Now that he selectively check (and uncheck) some individual items in this group (e.g. check "Scores" and "Feedback" only)... later on if the instructor sort of change his/her mind, and unchecked the "Enable" checkbox of "Close the quiz", this will then disable the closedoptionsgrp, but still LEAVES the "Feedback" and "Scores" checked (in the closedoptionsgrp group), which can be a bit confusing. Again not really a big issue, but just want to point this out as a possible improvement.

The current "disabledIf" in formslib doesn't support disabling checkbox AND resetting the values at the same time, so maybe this would require some work in the formslib level..

Summary: Improve unit test failure display
Description:
Suppose, to organise your unit tests, you make a helper function, like $this->check_current_output(...), that does a whole bunch of asserts, and which you call from a number of different test methods.

At the moment, the failure message will point to the line of code in the check_current_output method, which is not very helpful.


The attached patch tries to do more helpful output by displaying the stack-trace of where the failure occurred.

However, when running simple-tests the full stack trace is very long, with lots of simple-test related stuff in it.

Therefore, this code strips all the irrelevant bits out of the stack trace, so that only your code remains. Then the trace is only displayed if more than one bit remains.


(The patch is for 2.0. In 1.9, we can't use format_backtrace. There, I will just use print_object.)

When students can make multiple submissions for an assignment it is useful to know when files were submitted and when responses were uploaded (e.g. to see which response was for which submission).  [We prefer that students do not delete any submission once it has been marked, so 'obsolete' submissions and responses will remain visible; hence the need to distinguish between them].

This patch simply displays the filesystem timestamp (date) for each file immediately after the filename on the 'Grade' popup (and anywhere else that uses the affected routines).

Affects two routines (print_user_files & print_responsefiles) in mod/assignment/type/upload/assignment.class.php.

Summary: Forced download files to use Content-Disposition header to force the browser to save rather than open the file.
Description:
When a user clicks on a file resource that has the 'force download' set they are given the option to open or save the file.  If they open it and work on it, saving as they go, the file is saved to the temporary area that the web browser uses, as soon as they close the browser they potentially lose the location of the file and have no access to it.  When in fact they should have selected the 'save' option on the dialog box.  This should not happen and the user should be forced to save the file.

In looking at a solution - http://blogs.msdn.com/mapo/archive/2007/11/12/remove-the-open-button-from-the-file-download-dialog-box-in-internet-explorer.aspx & http://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/ms533689(VS.85).aspx - suggest use of the Meta tag to remove the open button from the download dialog, however, this will not work with all browsers.  Example 1 of http://php.net/manual/en/function.header.php suggests use of 'Content-Disposition' to indicate to the browser to save, not open the file.

Looking at /mod/resource/type/file/resource.class.php,v 1.71.2.31 - line 720 there is a call to 'redirect()' in lib/weblib.php where in fact there could be a call to send_file (line 654) in /lib/filelib.php,v 1.50.2.32 to send the file to the browser with the right headers if 'forcedownload' was contained in the url created in display() - line 195 of  /mod/resource/type/file/resource.class.php,v 1.71.2.31 with the right mime type.

The only sure-fire way to force the filename to be something reasonable is to make the URL end in that filename.

The only sure-fire way to force a download is Content-type: application/octet-stream

02/Jan/13 3:26 PM;712020:58b5d64a-e4a6-4658-ab55-6335c7197083;As I'm looking to the file upload issue in core_course_create_module(), I wanted to share my thoughts.

Status
------
At the moment we can send files throught:
web service with the core_file_upload() => it is sent in base64. The base64 encoding is really slow on mobile device + the encoded file could be way bigger to send.
with the webservice/upload.php => it is currently limited to private file area.

Objectif
--------
being able to send any files to any draft file area in Moodle.

Solutions
---------
I think the best and easiest way to send a file for client is by http with $_FILES. Exactly like in webservice/upload.php
I see two solutions:
a) the client send the files by HTTP. They get store in Moodle (we can implement some limitation, a user could send 10 files max). Moodle returns their "temp file id" as JSON string. Then the client call a moodle web service functions including their "temp file id" as parameter.
b) the client calls a web service function. The web service function prepare and return a "waiting for file id". The client sends its file with the "waiting for file id". At this moment the web service code logic is executed and moodle returns some JSON response.
I prefer solution a). It's easy, can be controlled/limited and support all protocols.

Some references to web service file upload:
[http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Web_services_files_handling#File_upload|http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Web_services_files_handling#File_upload]
[https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-37148|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-37148]
[https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-22236|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-22236]
[https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-31864|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-31864]

A is reasonably close to how file upload works with the picker - files go in a draft area until the form is submitted and then restrictions like file size and number of files are checked. It may be useful to put a global limit on the size of all the files in a users draft areas as part of this change.

How it should work:

(If you can, look at how Wikipedia notifies you when someone adds a comment to your talk page, that is where I saw this done right.)

1. When you have unread messages, a div is output, perhaps at the top of the page, telling you you have unread messages, with two links "Go to messages" and "Thanks, I'll look later". The Div should be styled so that it is very noticeable, without being completely distracting.

2. The "Go to messages" link is a normal link to the messaging UI.

3. When JavaScript is disabled, the "Thanks, I'll look later" link is a link back to the current page ($PAGE->url), with an extra param unreadmessagesseen={timestamp} to indicate that messages have been seen (and sesskey too, of course). The timestamp is the page containing the link loaded.

4. Whenever the unreadmessagesseen param is present in the URL, we set a user-preference, called something like "unreadmessagesacknowledged" to that timestamp.

5. When JavaScript is enable, the "Thanks, I'll look later" link is converted to into an ajax-y link, which sets the user_preference and hides the div without reloading the current page.

6. I suggest the following logic for whether to display the notifications div:
a. either, the user has unread messages posted after the time set in the unreadmessagesseen pref.
b. or, the user has any unread messges, and the unreadmessagesseen is more than one hour in the past.

For safetys sake I think I'd prefer to stick with setting the user last notified timestamp on the initial page load.


"or, the user has any unread messges, and the unreadmessagesseen is more than one hour in the past."

That's a good idea. Handy and reduces the impact if the user doesn't notice the first notification. If its over an hour since your last notification and you still have new messages you get re-notified.


I've also made it so that if you have only a single new message the notification tells you who the message is from.


There was a hard coded 30 second limit between notifications. This made sense for a popup but I don't think it does for an overlay in the corner so I've removed it. If you have a new message since the last notification or you have new messages and its been an hour since your last notification you get notified.

I've moved the notification overlay to the bottom right corner. It would be good if it was attached to the bottom of the browser as it looks funny when you scroll. Figuring out how to make that happen now.

Note also that if youre testing this it can be handy to comment out line 8973 of lib/moodlelib.php
$USER->message_lastpopup = time();
Without that line you'll get notified every page load after you receive a new message. Handy for testing.

Comments, ratings and tags are independent sub-systems in Moodle. For instance, to determine what tags have been associated with a wiki page, we ask the tagging system, rather than asking the wiki module. So it is not possible to maintain a history of tags, comments and ratings with the history of wiki page content.

If we wanted to keep a history of comments, ratings and tags, this would require an architectural change to these three sub-systems. As this is almost exclusively necessary in wiki pages, and for informational purposes only, I don't see that this idea will be implemented soon, if at all.

Summary: Glossary: teacher search for glossary terms across category or whole site
Description:
Basically the idea is, a global glossary search for teachers which they can use to find definitions in other courses on the site, that might be relevant to their own course (ie so they can copy/paste it).

The intention is, let's say you are working on a science course and you are about to write a glossary definition for 'photosynthesis', then you think, hang on, we've done loads of other courses, I bet somebody already wrote one. So you search across the whole site or across the Science category, you find one, you copy it, then just add a new glossary entry as usual, paste it in, and maybe tweak it a bit to be more relevant to your course.

So there would be a link from the glossary to a 'search across glossaries' page. You would then be able to choose to search all glossaries across all courses in (a) the current category, or (b) any parent category, or (c) the whole site.

    * The search would just be on the glossary term (wildcards permitted, so you could search for 'photosy*' if you're lazy or if you think other teachers probably misspelt it), and not a full text search.
    * Results would be shown as normal paged results 10 at a time or whatever, you could click on them to go to the glossary entry or just copy/paste it straight from the page if desired.
    * There might be a button you could click next to a glossary entry to add it to your own glossary, this would just open up the glossary add form, with the text from the existing entry filled in, so you could edit it and hit save.
    * I haven't figured out quite how permissions should work, but presumably it would only include results from glossaries you are allowed to actually see. The link itself would appear to anyone who's allowed to add entries in the current glossary.

I can code this thing locally just for us, but if there is an interest in having this in Moodle 2 core (and if I can agree it with Martin etc) then it would be nice to add it to that. Seems to me it might be useful to other sites.

Summary: Convert the languages codes used by Moodle to ISO 693-3
Description:
Originally, Moodle used two letter ISO 693-1 codes. When we realized it was not enough, we introduced our own language codes. Due to obvious reasons, it would be nice to switch back to some standardized codes. The most reasonable seems to three letters ISO 693-3. The switch involves:

* prepare a mapping table of all current codes to the new ones
* making sure that the mapping is unique
* fixing the Moodle core code
* fixing AMOS
* fixing localized docs.mood.org URLs
* fixing contrib and 3rd tools relying on the current scheme

Once we do that, the language in Moodle will be referenced to as XXX_YYY_local where XXX is ISO 693-3 code, YYY is a code of a variant/clone of the language (for example pirate English, OpenUniversity English etc.) and _local is optional suffix for site customization.

Koen, if you get bored with renovating the house and would like to start with the mapping table, that would be great.

Current setup of moodle forces the user to get into their profile to see what are the courses he has enrolled into and com back to the home page to see what are the course available if he wants a comparison.

Scenario :

There are 10 courses in a site, a user visits the site and enrolls into 3 courses to start with.

He returns to the site after some gap, and now he/she wants a comparison on the available courses and the courses they has enrolled into.

Existing methodology :

The user is beautifully presented with a listing of all available course along with the teachers and other few details when they log into the site in the course listing page.

Now when he wants to view the course he/she has already enrolled into, they have to click their profile name at the top right to view the profile page where the enrolled courses are displayed.

And return back to the home page or open the home page in a new tab/browser window for comparison.


Proposed solution:

A small indication as such as a text saying "Enrolled" besides the course name in the course listing page would suffice and help the user to get a current stand point without shuffling back and forth.

Summary: Add a custom menu that can be configured through admin and displayed by themes
Description:
The idea here is to integrate the static drop down menu that is popular with themer's into Moodle core.

The custom menu should be implemented using the YUI3 node-menunav widget and should display (even possibly work) with JavaScript enabled or disabled.
It should be implemented through the renderer as well in order to be over-rideable encase someone would like to implement a pure CSS drop down or any other sort of drop down that is desired.
This should also be supported in the standard theme.
Comments:
10/May/10 7:52 PM;557058:800d2609-d1a6-4f60-b9d9-0edd9cbd20bd;Hello everyone,
I have added Martin and Patrick as watchers to this issue and have just attached the patch for achieve this new feature now.

The patch adds support for the custom menu into core and is implemented in the standard theme. Martin if you could please have a quick check over the code.

You can now configure a custom menu by:
# Browse to Settings: Administration > Appearance > Themes > Theme settings
# Add items into the custommenuitems setting as described (text|url|title|sort) and then save.
As long as the theme supports it this is all that needs to be done.
Once this has been commit I will post in the theme's forum about how to integrate this into a new theme as well as what needs to be done to get it all displaying correctly.

What you should both be aware of with this patch, it of course makes use of the YUI 3.1.0 menunav widget, this widget however does not support JavaScript being disabled. As such I have added a class to the root yui3-menu div _javascript-disabled_ that gets removed once the yui3 menunav widget [finally] initialises.
This class allows us to style the custom menu for both JavaScript being disabled and the delay that occurs before the widget has initialised (it is a pretty slow widget sometimes). I have put minimal CSS into base+standard themes that displays the menu nearly exactly as it is displayed by the widget, enough so that you won't notice the switch from CSS to JavaScript when it occurs.
Currently in IE6/7 it only displays when JavaScript is disabled, however I have fixed it so that with any other browser it is fully functional without JavaScript as well.

I will look in the future to write a tutorial illustrating how to override the renderer in order to achieve a pure CSS dropdown menu, I think this will be desired in the future as the more JS we load into Moodle the longer it all takes initialise and this is simply adding to the undesired performance drop.

I think continuing to have the admin page is a good idea - updating timezone information is relatively risk-free compared to updating Moodle itself, and we should IMHO enable administrators to keep Moodle's timezones up to date on as close to a similar cadence to the operating system timezone updates they're generally required to apply.

You just need to be able to specify a $CFG->cachedir, which defaults to $CFG->dataroot . '/cache' if not otherwise set.

The only difficult bit is when you want to clear the cache. Then you need to clear the cache folder on each server.

Summary: Progress bar behavior is not always desirable
Description:
Currently, the progress bar calculates a completion percentage based on the total number of pages in the lesson. If the user restarts the lesson, the progress bar doesn't reset. In other words, once the user views all the pages, the progress bar will always be completely green. In some cases, this is the desired behavior. In other cases, course designers want one of the following instead:

Progress bar represents the position of the current page in the lesson, rather than a completion percentage. For example, page 2 of 10, rather than 20%. Resetting the progress bar isn't an issue in this case.

Progress bar represents a completion percentage, but it resets when the user restarts the lesson. This may not be as important, because in this case, what they really want is probably the position, not the percentage.

Ideally, the behavior of the progress bar would be configurable within the UI. Instead of just turning the progress bar on or off, the course designer would specify a certain behavior (non-resetting completion percentage, resetting completion percentage, or page position).

This behavior comes from the lesson_print_progress_bar() function in \mod\lesson\locallib.php
The current calculation is count($viewedpageids)/count($validpages).
To show the position of the current page, it would need the position instead of count($viewedpageids). Apparently the position comes from prevpageid and nextpageid in mdl_lesson_pages.
To show a completion percentage that resets, it would perform the same calculation, but count($viewedpageids) would need to be based on the current session, not the life of the lesson.

b) if it is group centric then the first column would be the group, ordered by groups and then by users. Users in multiple groups would have multiple rows. Groups with no members would still be shown.

c) if it is grouping centric then the first column would be the grouping, second would be group, then users and sorted by grouping then group then users. Users in multiple groups / groupings would have multiple rows. Grouping with no groups, and groups with no members would still be shown.

1) move the column order so its' grouping first then group

Summary: Incorporate section name into other parts of Moodle
Description:
Moodle 2.0 provides a way to set the section name (e.g. Topic 1) to something more specific (e.g. Introduction to Calculus).  Currently the section name is included in navigation, but not anywhere else in Moodle.  Other places in Moodle refer to the section name as "Topic 1", "Week 1" or "Section 1" depending on the current course format.

It would be nice if the rest of Moodle supported section names the way navigation does.

The attached patches attempt to incorporate section name functionality into Moodle.  I've split the changes into two patches.

The first patch (get-section-name.patch):
# Modifies the {{get_section_name}} function in /course/lib.php to return the full name (e.g. Topic 1, Intro to Calculus, Week 4) instead of just the language string.
# Adds support for using navigation's {{callback_xxx_get_section_name}} callbacks in course formatters to control what section name is returned.
# Updates code references (as many as I could find) throughout Moodle to use the /course/lib.php {{get_section_name}} function.

The second patch (use-sections.patch):
# Adds support for a new function, {{course_format_uses_sections}}, in /course/lib.php.  This function returns true if the course format uses sections to display information (e.g. Topic format, Week format, but not SCORM format),  Activity modules can use this function to determine how to display information.
# By default, {{course_format_uses_sections}} returns false.  Course formats can implement a {{callback_xxx_uses_sections}} function in their lib.php file to indicate they use sections.
# Modifies several places, mainly index.php in activity modules, to use the new {{course_format_uses_sections}} function.


In my opinion, students and teachers should benefit from consistently named sections throughout Moodle.

These patches replace a lot of code that specifically looks for the topic or week course formats with more generic code.  This should make writing additional course formats a little easier.

Summary: Make the create_users() external service function return more data
Description: The utility of the create_users() external service function can be greatly enhanced if it returns some more data about the user.  At the very least, for users like us that make use of the idnumber field to uniquely & unambiguously associate Moodle users with a corresponding record in our SIS (we store our staff & students in two separate tables, for example), having the idnumber will allow us to parse out which type of user we have just created and then store their Moodle user id in the correct place.
Comments: 04/Jun/10 1:28 PM;712020:71ee14d2-3443-45c3-88c4-9602246f801b;This patch adds the idnumber to the information that is returned by the create_users() external service function

04/Jun/10 5:43 PM;712020:58b5d64a-e4a6-4658-ab55-6335c7197083;At the moment create_users ws function returns:
* id
* username
which is enough for s client. The client just need to know under which id the user has been created on the remote Moodle site.

We could add the idnumber and many other fields, I'll talk about that during our next dev meeting...

04/Jun/10 6:15 PM;557058:04670d95-8ea4-4705-9d43-683a4fdf2d81;Um, perhaps I'm missing something here Basil, but your client just passed the optional idnumber *to* the create_users function to create the user account, so you already have it.  Why would you want it passed back?

My feeling is that this API needs to be very clear, rigorous and consistent.  Either we return a minimal-needed dataset or we return all of it.

My -1 to start adding optional fields to the returned data like this.

05/Jun/10 5:35 AM;712020:71ee14d2-3443-45c3-88c4-9602246f801b;Martin, you're not missing anything.  That is true.  But what I want to do is store the Moodle user with the appropriate, associated record in our SIS.  The idnumber value that we sent over is our unambiguous way of distinguishing the type of record that the return userid applies to.  Let me provide a few more details, and you can hopefully understand our case a little better.

We have three types of users - staff (teachers, administrators, IT workers, helpdesk users, etc.), students (exactly what they sound like), and guardians (basically, users that fit the "Parent" role profile with some more extensions we've added).  We assign each of these types of users a globally-unique idnumber of the form "$usertype-$sisid".  So a staff with an id of 1234 would have the idnumber value of "staff-1234".  Students behave the same as staff.  Guardians exist on a one-to-one basis for students, so every student has a unique guardian associated with it, so the guardian for a student 5678 would have the idnumber of "guardian-5678" in the LMS.

As we store our staff & students in separate tables in our SIS, I'd have to check the returned username across two different tables (three, if we ever end-up treating guardians the same as staff & students) before finding a match, and then knowing with which record to associate the Moodle user id of the user we just created.  This step is only needed on user creation, because after that, we'll have the userid stored in our SIS and we can use that from this point on for user-related external services.

It is my understanding that the idnumber exists for exactly the kind of usage I've described, so having the idnumber returned so I can easily make a quick update to our SIS records makes sense to me.  I hope my explanation was clear.  I totally agree with sending back only the most important information, and at least in our case, the idnumber fits into that.  Having the idnumber will save me many lines of logic in our SIS that can be error prone if we have false matches to the usernames between the staff & student tables, whereas having the idnumber would completely avoid this issue.

05/Jun/10 5:38 AM;712020:71ee14d2-3443-45c3-88c4-9602246f801b;I forget to address the point that we did send the idnumber itself clearly.  Yes, we sent it over, but all we get back are a userid and a username.  Including the idnumber saves us the step of having to infer the specific record (i.e., student or staff) via just the username.

22/Jun/10 8:58 PM;712020:58b5d64a-e4a6-4658-ab55-6335c7197083;I'm not going to add more fields as you can workaround any data value on the client side. However I'll let this issue open for a while if some people wants to vote for it. Lowering the priority.
Thanks for the report Basil.

30/Jun/10 11:08 PM;557058:04670d95-8ea4-4705-9d43-683a4fdf2d81;Basil you didn't really explain about the username ... I'm not sure why you have to search three tables for it.

The username must be unique in Moodle, the idnumber does not (and it can even be NULL).  So I can see how it would help for this case but I don't think it makes sense for the API.

01/Jul/10 5:57 AM;712020:71ee14d2-3443-45c3-88c4-9602246f801b;We have to search two tables because our Moodle users are stored in two tables in our SIS.  We encode the "user type" (which maps to a table in our SIS) in the idnumber field, as opposed to the username field.  This is very implementation specific, and we have a solution.  The discrepancy comes from the fact that Moodle uses a single table for *all* users (which is not a bad idea, in my opinion).  I think it's fine to let this be for now, at least for us, I took care of the issue by handling it on the SIS.
