Summary: Outputing numbers to the UI like 0.000 is ugly and pointless
Description: Trim trailing zeros from numbers displayed in the gradebook.  For example 1.125 should be left untouched but 1.000 can be trimmed to 1
Comments: 04/Jun/10 10:05 PM;557058:c4596910-72fa-4677-8fbf-4d81abaa8214;Added a function to strip out trailing 0's. Weight, extra credit, multiplicator and offset columns make use of it.

18/Jun/10 12:14 AM;5b4e1b8cb84bc45fea9605e4;I object against trimming numbers like 1.000 to 1. It is quite common to display numbers like 1.000 or even 0.00 in statistics, engineering etc. The redundant decimals are sign of precision. If the grades in gradebook are 0.00, it implicitly means that the precision is two decimals. But of the grade is just "0" or the weight is "1" etc, one may be unsure if the value equals or was rounded.

Also, numbers alignment does not work well in columns if there are rows with 1.125 followed by 1

So, from my point of view: trimming 1.000 to 1 is ugly and pointless ;-)
18/Jun/10 3:53 AM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;I am with David. Gradebook has an explicit decimal places option. We should respect that.

18/Jun/10 10:38 PM;557058:c4596910-72fa-4677-8fbf-4d81abaa8214;Sorry, the bug report is a bit vague. Its only settings on the "categories and items" page we're talking about. Not grades themselves. This only affects aggregate coefficients (usually displayed as 'weight'), multiplicators and offsets settings. As Tim says, gradebook has a setting for the grade items themselves.

"Also, numbers alignment does not work well in columns if there are rows with 1.125 followed by 1"

While nice smooth columns of identically formatted numbers look more attractive, as a general principle, jagged columns are more user friendly. Its easier for a person to read down the list as the unevenness prevents you from losing your place and you don't get mistakes due to similar looking number like 1.000, 10.00 and 1000

I've attached two screenshots. One with trimming, one without. I put some numbers in the weight column. Having all the zeros displayed adds a lot of noise and makes it far more difficult to quickly make sense of the numbers being displayed.

18/Jun/10 11:18 PM;5b4e1b8cb84bc45fea9605e4;Thanks for the screenshots. They actually support my objection, IMHO. As by default the aggregation coefficient equals one, the number displayed in the input field will be "1" instead of current "1.0000". This has an effect in user intuitively thinks that integers only are allowed. Again - if we display "1.0000", we say that decimal numbers are expected, what the precision may be and what the decimal separator must be used (in Czech we write comma instead of dot, for example).

18/Jun/10 11:53 PM;557058:c4596910-72fa-4677-8fbf-4d81abaa8214;They only need to find out that we support decimals once but the cost of the user parsing all the numbers displayed and typing them (some will) is paid by the user every time they come to this screen. We're introducing a recurring cost to get a one time benefit.

IMO, if a user wants decimals they're likely to try to enter one, see that it works and we reach the same end point, the user knows we support decimals, without cluttering the UI. The 3 column help items should probably also let the user know decimals are allowed.

I'd prefer to err on the side of making it appear less intimidating initially then allow the user to discover more later (progressive disclosure). New users aren't going to be impressed by the degree of precision we offer but they may be put off by the volume of numbers.

What about having it trim trailing zeros to 1 decimal? ie 1.0 That expresses that decimals are supported and tells the user what decimal separator to use. It means we're outputting 2 numbers to convey 1 number worth of data but it's better than 5 :D

23/Jun/10 9:13 PM;557058:c4596910-72fa-4677-8fbf-4d81abaa8214;I'm taking silence as agreement :D I've altered format_number() to trim to between 1 and 4 decimal places. I've also added some unit tests that demonstrate its behaviour.

Katarzyna Potocka # katarzyna.potocka@elearning.tuwien.ac.at # # Vienna University of Technology # E-Learning Centre # Gusshausstrasse 28/E015 # 1040 Wien # http://elearning.tuwien.ac.at/ # --------------------------------------------------------------- # FOR Moodle 1.9.7 !!! # --------------------------------------------------------------- README.txt v.2010-03-03 Moodle 1.9.7 course overview semester sorting and MyMoodle semester sorting This is a cummulated patch for thw following two improvements: http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-18760 http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-20593 What will this patch do: This patch will give the administrator the possbility to change the layout of the course overview, either on the course overview page or on the MyMoodle site. The administrator will have the possibility to choose a different front page layout for the "My courses" display. Go to Site Administration/Front Page/Front Page settings/ (/admin/settings.php?section=frontpagesettings) for setup (see screenshots). The courses will be sorted according to the startdate set within the course settings. Additionally the administrator will have the possibility to turn on the MyMoodle site and to check the semsorting, so that the courses on the MyMoodle site will be sorted according to the startdate. The possibility to change the semsort to standard Moodle sorting is available. You can transfer courses into the next term just by adjusting the startdate. Within the attached screenshots you can see the difference between moodle-standard sorting and the novel semester sorting and the standard sorted MyMoodle site and the MyMoodle site sorted according to courses startdates. My courses: Labels of the sections will be YEAR+semester S for summer, W for winter eg 2009S or 2008W. The label of the current term will be "My current courses". MyMoodle: Labels of the sections will be "Summer term+YEAR" for summer, "Winter term+YEAR" for winter eg Summer term 2010 or Winter term 2009. Summer S = startdate IN (Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun) = (2,3,4,5,6) Winter W = startdate IN (Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec, Jan) = (7,8,9,10,11,12,1) 0) Prerequisites 1) Applying the patch 2) Add german language files (optional) 3) Add style sheet part 4) Screenshots 5) Use your new moodle enhancement, and have fun :-) 6) If something went wrong 7) Additional settings - just a little bit coding 8) Please send feedback to Follow these instructions for applying the patch: 0) Prerequisites: a) Make sure your Moodle Version is 1.9.7 b) Make a Backup of EVERYTHING (moodle, moodledata, database,...) c) Make sure you can restore your backup and the restored system works d) Make sure you can apply a unified-diff patch to your moodle source code (e.g. Eclipse) We highly recommend applying and testing the patch on a testsystem before applying it to your production system. $string['config_courseordersemester'] = 'moodle wide on/off'; $string['courseordersemester_user'] = 'Sortorder as user preference in DB'; $string['config_courseordersemester_user'] = 'Save the sortorder as an user preference in the DB (reqires 2 DB accesses per myMoodle visit), use Cookies otherwise'; $string['courseordersemester_names'] = 'Months of the winter term'; $string['config_courseordersemester_names'] = 'unselected month = month of the summer term'; $string['mymoodleadminnote'] = 'Admin note'; $string['config_mymoodleadminnote'] = 'if set, shown on any myMoodle page'; // my/index.php $string['courseordersemester_summerterm'] = 'Summer term'; $string['courseordersemester_winterterm'] = 'Winter term'; $string['courseordersemester_semester'] = 'Sortorder: standard moodle '; $string['courseordersemester_classic'] = 'Sortorder: term based'; // accessability $string['courseordersemester_access'] = 'Skip Course'; otherwise copy the my_hub.php file into your lang/en_utf8 folder 2.2) Add german language file (optional): if you already have a moodle_tuwel.php or my_hub.php language file, extend it: $string['frontpagecourselistsortedstartdate'] = 'Kursliste sortiert nach Kursstartdatum'; //kp added 17.02.2009 $string['courseoverviewsemester'] = 'Semester $a'; $string['mycoursescurrent'] = 'Meine aktuellen Kurse'; // admin/settings/appearence.php $string['courseordersemester'] = 'Kurse nach Semestern sortieren'; $string['config_courseordersemester'] = 'Instanzweit an/aus'; $string['courseordersemester_user'] = 'Sortierung pro Nutzer in DB speichern'; $string['config_courseordersemester_user'] = 'Speichert die Auswahl pro Nutzer in der DB, Session und Browser uebergreifend (2 DB Zufriffe pro Nutzer / myMoodle Aufruf notwendig), anderenfalls Cookies zum Speichern verwenden'; $string['courseordersemester_names'] = 'Monate des Wintersemesters'; $string['config_courseordersemester_names'] = 'nicht markierte Monate = Monate des Sommersemesters. Die Monate 1-6 zaehlen noch zum Wintersemester des Vorjahres'; $string['mymoodleadminnote'] = 'Adminnotiz'; $string['config_mymoodleadminnote'] = 'wenn gesetzt, wird diese Nachricht instanzweit verbindlich auf der myMoodle Seite angezeigt'; // my/index.php $string['courseordersemester_summerterm'] = 'Sommersemester'; $string['courseordersemester_winterterm'] = 'Wintersemester'; $string['courseordersemester_semester'] = 'Sortierung: moodle Standard'; $string['courseordersemester_classic'] = 'Sortierung: semesterbasiert'; // accessability $string['courseordersemester_access'] = 'Kurs überspringen'; otherwise copy the my_hub.php file into your lang/de_utf8 folder 3) Add style sheet part Add the content of the my_hub.css file to your ../theme/yourchosentheme/styles.layout.css file! 4) Screenshot: mycourses_admin.jpg mycourses_studentview.jpg mymoodle_admin_notempty.jpg mymoodle_admin_empty.jpg mymoodle_admin_before_patch.jpg mymoodle_studentview.jpg 5) Use your new moodle enhancement, and have fun :-) 6) If something went wrong :-( ... don't panic ... just make a reversion Just follow these steps (Eclipse): b) right click the project and choose Team -> Apply patch c) choose the patch file tuwienhumboldt_elzmoodle_courseoverview_mymoodle_semestersorting_patch197_20100303.diff d) select the path for applying the patch (the project you have right-clicked before) e) choose the checkbox 'Reverse patch' (this will remove all the further added changes) e) preview the reversion and click Finish 7) Additional settings - just a little bit coding 7.1) Moodle sorting or semesterbades sorting on your MyMoodle site: if you don't want to leave it to your students if they use the Moodle sorting or the semesterbased sorting on their MyMoodle site, you just have to comment out one line of code in the ../my/index.php file search for "// the sortorder switch" and add "//" in front of the following line: echo '
'.get_string('courseordersemester_semester', 'my_hub').'
'; so that it looks like: //echo '
'.get_string('courseordersemester_semester', 'my_hub').'
'; 7.2) Different term settings: if your institution has different term settings than summer term: February, March, April, May, June and winter term: July, August, September, October, November, December, January than you have the possibility to change this within the admin settings of your Moodle Site. If you want to change this additionally within the code you have to change following lines within 2 php files (../course/lib.php and ../my/index.php): $SS = array(2,3,4,5,6); $WS = array(1,10,11,12,7,8,9); 8) Please send feedback to: katarzyna.potocka@elearning.tuwien.ac.at andreas.hruska@elearning.tuwien.ac.at See als

Summary: Allow 'locking' of Database fields so that only teachers can edit them
Description:
These patches add a new "lock field for editing" checkbox at the bottom of each field editing form. If you tick this box, then the field is only editable by users with the mod/data:manageentries permission.

The point being that a student adding a new record can complete all fields except the 'locked' ones. Then a teacher can edit that same record and add extra information in the locked fields. It's the equivalent of the "for admin use only" part of a paper form.

Note that this code uses the spare 'param9' field in the mdl_data_fields table to mark the locked fields. There are 10 spare fields, of which ony the first 3, appear to be in use. I have used param9 to hopefully future proof against coming official extensions to Database functionality.

Summary: Improve contact/message search to limit potential server load
Description:
The function message_search() in message/lib.php could do with some enhancements.

1) It doesn't seem to limit the maximum number of search results that will be retrieved. Either implement paging and show say 20 records at a time or simply cap the results returned to 100 or so. Either way pass the limits in to $DB->get_records_sql() to limit the size of the result set at the database level.

2) Also, single letter search terms are culled from the array of conditions. This is to exclude search terms that may bring in bogus matches. For example "a brown dog" will be split into "brown" and "dog" with the letter "a" being discarded. This has the side effect that if the only search term is a single letter it is discarded and the following default where clause is constructed.

m.fullmessage like %

This will match every message which probably isn't intended behaviour. I'm guessing that if the search term consists of only a single letter we should still be searching for it even though that will return a lot of results.
Comments:
07/Jul/10 11:53 PM;557058:c4596910-72fa-4677-8fbf-4d81abaa8214;Fix committed. Note that I've capped message search results to 200. If you do a search which produces the maximum number of search results you get a message telling you to refine your search. 200 will limit database load due to a too general search but is still enough that it should be more than a person will want to read through, hopefully prompting them to search again with more specific search terms.

Also, if only single letter search terms are supplied then they are not stripped out. Even a single letter search term is better than matching everything (I think). If there is a multi-letter search term present then single letter search terms are stripped out as per normal.

Summary: Allow teachers to move students between options in a Choice
Description:
If, as a teacher, I want to change a student's choice, I either have to ask them to do it, or else modify the Moodle database directly. It would be useful to be able to do this, especially where Choice is being used to allow students to select seminar groups.

This patch will allow a teacher (or anyone who has mod/choice:deleteresponses capability) to select one or more users in the results table, and change their choice. If the users are in the 'unanswered' column, then they get assigned to the new option. The last-modified time is unchanged by this operation.

If the target option is already full, this will be indicated in the drop-down, but if you attempt to move the user anyway, nothing will happen.

If you attempt to delete a user from the "unanswered" column, nothing will happen.

Summary: Qualifications expiry and notifications (or reminders)
Description:
I'm investigating the possibility of implementing qualification expiry and notifications / reminders in Moodle.

For example if a person completes a training for a given qualification, and that qualification is valid for 12-months, is there a way in Moodle to send notifications to the person (say at intervals of 1, 2, or 3 months before the expiry of the qualification) to re-qualify by completing another instance of the course?

A possible of implementing it would be to have an 'expiry period' field in the grade_items table and that field can be used in reports and notifications.

This may not make it into a 1.9 release, so I'm suggesting it for 2.0.

Summary: Kill Typo3 UTF-8 libraries and rewrap our textlib against own code
Description:
Since Moodle 2.0 iconv is required by Moodle installations.

This give us the opportunity to end using some Typo3 libraries we have been using since Moodle 1.6 in order to provide UTF-8 string operations. Typo3 has been really useful as it provided one nice fallback between iconv/mbstring/custom unicode handling, but as far as we know that iconv is always available, we should be able to switch to own library.

Proposal:

- Complete testing coverage of current textlib.php
- Implement new unicodelib for all those operations
- Make textlib wrapper to use the new unicodelib by default (keeping typo3 there available controlled by CFG setting "just in case" problems arrive).
- Ensure all tests pass both using unicodelib and typo3
- Release (2.1.x)
- After 2.1.x+3 without problems reported, if typo3 isn't necessary anymore... drop it. Thanks Typo3!

Summary: Perform natural sort on groups and groupings
Description:
Groups and groupings are currently sorted using a basic alphanumeric sort (as the sorting is done by the DBMS), which fails to sort names with numbers in them correctly when the number of digits differs.  For example, if you use the auto-create groups feature to create 20 groups using the naming scheme "Group #" it'll create "Group 1" through "Group 20" - but they'll appear in lists in the order "Group 1, Group 10, Group 11, ..., Group 19, Group 2, Group 20, Group 3, ..." which isn't ideal.

I've attached patches against Moodle 1.9.9 and Moodle 2.0 (cvshead from git.moodle.org/moodle.git) which implement natural sorting on groups and groupings.  I may have missed any places that they're listed outside the groups/groupings admin area, as I haven't done an exhaustive search of Moodle for lists of groups/groupings).

Note that you won't be able to get to the Groupings or Overview tabs on 2.0 until MDL-22903 is resolved (unless you manually patch it), and that the list of groups assigned to the selected member in the group assignment list will not appear on 2.0 until MDL-22935 is resolved.  These features will all still be sorted correctly by the attached patch.

29/Jun/10 1:56 PM;70121:31a3541a-98d0-40cf-83fa-c58c1f5a1106;Good point, Petr - but making the auto-create groups system add leading zeroes doesn't seem like the "nicest" (from a user's perspective) way to fix it, especially if you have 100+ groups - and it won't affect existing groups.

Perhaps what we need to do is simply add a new (numeric) column which gets populated automatically by the auto-create groups system, and sort by that first and the group name second?  It could be exposed as an advanced option in the group also, so that the sort order of manually-created groups can be tweaked if necessary.  The field could be left null (or set to 0, to achieve more consistent results on different DMBSes - I think some may sort nulls before all else and others after all else) for manually-created groups without sort orders specified, and the auto-create system could then grab the maximum sort for groups in the relevant context and start at the next index.

While this approach wouldn't necessarily result in all groups being sorted (auto-created groups would be in one block after all manual groups with no explicit sort order set), it would resolve the issue for auto-created groups, which are the primary issue.  It also would not break any 3rd-party blocks/modules which list groups, since they'd just continue to sort in the existing manner if not updated.  Groupings could simply have an advanced setting for sort order - that might be nice to add either way, to give a little more control.


Alternatively, the auto-create system could be tweaked to use two columns - a (string) "prefix" stored in the existing group name column, and an integer index stored in a separate column for groups auto-created using the "#" placeholder (those using "@" for letters could still be stored as the group name only).  Groups could then be sorted by name followed by index.  It does, however, mean that the check for group name uniqueness would need to be modified to check the suffix as well as the name, since you'd end up with several groups with the same name but unique indexes.  The # denoting the position of the number within the group name could remain in the database, so the number goes into the correct spot.

This approach does require post-processing of the results in order to replace the placeholders, which may cause some performance degradation, though, and will require changes anywhere that groups are fetched/listed (preferably to use a library function to fetch groups which handles this).  Such a change would probably be best done in 2.0 only, since it could easily break existing functionality in 3rd-party blocks/modules (they'd end up showing a bunch of "Group #" items).

* move mod/folder stuff back to own renderer

* etc.

Because SVG images are resolution-independent, the image can be resized or altered without degrading the image quality. SVG supports animation - see endless debates SVG versus Flash. You can animate individual objects within an SVG file as well as the vast majority of the properties and attributes that these objects possess, such as their color, size, orientation, opacity, and visibility. SVG has a number of other advantages over other graphics standards. It uses a "color profile" to render colors more accurately, regardless of browser and monitor differences (even rendering accurately to devices such as PDAs and cell phones). Text-based SVG can be edited with text editor, it is open source, written in XML, an official W3C graphics standard, accessible for people with visual disabilities, searchable, dynamic and updateable, supports filters, transformations, clipping, and masking, supports transparency, can be used for print as well as Web graphics...

Details are:

1df11d7.
I've added a function to force the usesvg property to either true or false. I've then used that method within theme_config::post_process (the function responsible for processing those image URL's) to force the use of svg when available to off. This means that we never serve SVG images through CSS. The reason for this decision is that support of SVG in CSS across browsers is sketchy and at best quirky. This will I imagine lead to a situation of a further feature request in the future to support SVG in CSS, however I think that is a bridge best crossed later when we both know people want it, and support of it is more consistent.

0d966ed.
I found a bug in the way things happened if the user who first requested an image was using a browser that didn't support SVG. In this situation a PNG (or equiv) would be cached and all future requests for that image would result in the PNG being served regardless of the users browser supporting it or not. This was happening because any candidate image already exists for subsequent requests.
The solution is to always ensure we cache an SVG copy when caching & serving an image for someone that does not support SVG.
This will of course only happen once so while it does introduce more work it should not be significant.

Summary: Hub settings: add check for reCaptcha activated
Language - Critical review of English language files to improve consistency and clarity especially regarding permissions
Description:
I originally began thinking about this because of a recent commit that caught my attention but realized that the issue is actually much larger than a particular string. Considering that 2.0 is such a major release, it seems worthwhile to do a good review of the English language pack to ensure that we are being as consistent and clear as possible. I'll start with the string that first caught my attention and then explain and summarize at the end.

Consider the following string:

$string['cannotsearchcommunity'] = 'Sorry, you don\'t have the right permissions to see this page';

Is 'right' is the best word? Would sufficient be better? Do we really need a qualifier. Permissions are pretty specific and are tied to a particular capability within a particular context. The right permissions makes it sound like it is a matter of right and wrong. I think we are looking for a measurement of sufficiency rather than right or wrong. Yet, we seen to be using a variety of words to convey the same basic message. Some of the other words used are required permissions, needed permissions, a simple statement that they do not have permission to do/perform x (which I like even more than sufficient).

So perhaps the string could be improved by changing it to: 

'Sorry, you do not have permission to view this page' (I prefer view to see since we cannot literally determine what a person sees or not). But perhaps 'this page' is not clear enough - should it say you do not have permission to search perform a community search? I believe the more clear we can be about the permission and context the better folks will be able to understand the way that roles, capabilities, and contexts are used throughout Moodle which will greatly enhance the usability.  

$string['nopermissiontodelentry'] = 'You can\'t delete other people\'s entries!'; - should this be 'You do not have permission to delete other people\'s entries'? I do not like simply telling someone they cannot do something. any user can delete other people's entries if they have the capability in the particular context. 

$string['nopermissiontohide'] = 'No permission to hide!'; - should this be 'You do not have permission to hide!' (if so, I would like to see some object - what is being hidden. Context is important so I want to make sure we are communicating what is happening. 

$string['nopermissions'] = 'Sorry, but you do not currently have permissions to do that ({$a})'; - does 'currently' add anything? why are we apologizing? I think a simple statement of 'You do not have sufficient/necessary/required/needed permissions ({$a})'. We should pick a formula for expressing insufficient permissions and stick with it.

$string['nopermissiontorate'] = 'Rating of items not allowed!'; - technically speaking this is incorrect. The rating of items is allowed, just not by a particular user with particular permissions. This is why I like personalizing by saying 'You do not have permission to rate items'. Should we mention context by saying 'these items' since they could rate other items?

$string['nopermissiontoviewletergrade'] = 'Missing permission to view letter grades'; - I would avoid using the phrase 'missing permission' - the permission is not missing, the user just does not have that particular permission in that particular context . 

$string['wscouldnotcreateecoursenopermission'] = 'WS - Could not create course - No permission'; - this seems choppy. I do not like unnecessary abbreviations - what is WS? (web services I suppose). Again, the formula here is choppy. 'You do not have permission to create courses with web services'. 

In summary, at the very least I think we should look at the language strings that contain the word permission. In 2.0 there are 158 matches in 25 files. 

1) We should be more consistent about how we express not having permission
2) I would advocate for not using contractions ("can't, don't, etc). in the language files. I think this keeps the language files easier to read and since Moodle is an educational tool and contractions are not encouraged in academic writing it makes sense to avoid them by default.
3) Remove unnecessary words. For example words like 'currently', 'sorry', etc. Since a user is getting the message, it is obvious that it is the current state. I think it may even imply that something might change on its own so that the user should try again later. Remove the word 'sorry' as there is no need to apologize. Permissions are setup to prevent particular users from being able to do things. There is no need to apologize. In fact, I would advocate for removing 'Sorry' altogether (61 matches in 17 files) and simply state the fact. Sites that want to give it a more sympathetic or personalized feel can always add in their apologies. 

Once we come up with a standard of how we want to express insufficient permissions, then I would be happy to prepare a patch.

Peace - Anthony

17/Aug/13 4:40 AM;712020:51693c1c-5828-4e14-8282-3d44625fdfbf;Proposed solution:

h4. Required Code Changes

h5. Create a new admin setting
* Create a new admin settings class that extends the 'admin_setting_configtext' class.  The new setting class will override the validate() method to ensure the user enters an integer that is greater than 0 but less than or equal to 10000
** A hard coded maximum of 10000 will be enforced by the admin setting
** The default value will be 100

* Modify admin/settings/grades.php by adding the new admin settings field, to allow the user to enter a site wide imposed grade point maximum.{quote}
*Example 1*
* User goes into Site Administration -> Grades -> General settings
* User scolls to the 'Grade point maximum' setting
* User enters a value of 600
* User clicks 'Save changes' button
* Site wide grade point maximum is now 600

*Example 2*
* User goes into Site Administration -> Grades -> General settings
* User scolls to the 'Grade point maximum' setting
* User enters a value of 20000
* User clicks 'Save changes' button
* The admin setting code notifies the user of the 10000 point limit

*Example 3*
* User goes into Site Administration -> Grades -> General settings
* User scolls to the 'Grade point maximum' setting
* User enters a value of 0
* User clicks 'Save changes' button
* The admin setting code notifies the user that the value must be greater 0 but less than 10000

*Example 4*
* User goes into Site Administration -> Grades -> General settings
* User scolls to the 'Grade point maximum' setting
* User leaves the field blank
* User clicks 'Save changes' button
* Site wide grade point maximum is now 100 (the default value)

*Example 5*
* User goes into Site Administration -> Grades -> General settings
* User scolls to the 'Grade point maximum' setting
* User enters a non-numeric value or negative number
* User clicks 'Save changes' button
* The admin setting code notifies the user that the value must be greater 0 but less than 10000
{quote}

h5. Create a new formslib element

* Create a new form definition for displaying the grading elements (defined as an instance of MoodleQuickForm_group).
* In expotValue() the selected options must be analyized such that one value is returned instead of 3 (one for each grading element).  The reason for this is that all graded activities currently use one column, in the module table, to store the grade value.  A grade value of '- x' denotes a scale where '-' tells the module a grade scale is to be used and 'x' is the id of the scale selected.  Where as a grade value of 'x' denotes a grade point is to be used and 'x' is any positive number.
{quote}
*Example 1*
User adds a graded activity and selects the following:
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 900
- Grade Type - 'point'
- Scale - disabled because Grade Type is not 'scale'
- Grade Point - 600

The user submits the form and the value stored in the grade column of the module's table is 600.

*Example 2*
User adds a graded activity and selects the following:
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 900
- Grade Type = 'scale'
- Scale - Scale value
- Grade Point - automatically disabled because Grade Type is not 'point'

The user submits the form and the value stored in the grade column of the module's table is a negative integer.

*Example 3*
User adds a graded activity and selects the following:
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 900
- Grade Type = 'No grade'
- Scale - disabled because Grade Type is not 'scale'
- Grade Point - disabled because Grade Type is not 'point'

The user submits the form and the value stored in the grade column of the module's table is 0.

*Example 4*
User adds a graded activity and selects the following:
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 900
- Grade Type = 'Point'
- Scale - disabled because Grade Type is not 'scale'
- Grade Point - 20000

The user submits the form and validation code returns an error highlighting that the grade point entered is higher than the site imposed maximum.

{quote}

* In onQuickFormEvent() in the 'updaveValue' event the values passed to the formslib definition can be used to initialize the state of the 3 grade elements.
{quote}
*Example 1*
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 900
- User updates a graded activity that is using a grade point value of 600
- The value is analyzed
- The Grade Type dropdown value is set to 'Point'
- The Scale dropdown is disabled
- The Grade Point text field is populated with 600

*Example 2*
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 900
- User updates a graded activity that is using a grade point value of 0
- The value is analyzed
- The Grade Type dropdown value is set to 'No grade'
- The Scale dropdown is disabled
- The Grade Point text field is disabled

*Example 3*
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 900
- User updates a graded activity that is using a scale value of -1
- The value is analyzed
- The Grade Type dropdown value is set to 'Scale'
- The Scale dropdown value is set to the '-1' entry
- The Grade Point text field is disabled

*Example 4*
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 100
- User updates a graded activity that is using a grade point value of 600
- The value is analyzed
- The Grade Type dropdown value is set to 'Point'
- The Scale dropdown is disabled
- The Grade Point text field is populated with 600

The user submits the form and validation code returns an error highlighting that the grade point entered is higher than the site imposed maximum.

{quote}


h5. Backup and restore usecases

*Example 1*
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 1000
- User creates a graded activity
- Grade Type = 'Point'
- Scale - disabled because Grade Type is not 'scale'
- Grade Point - 1000
- Saves the form
- Creates a backup of the course, activities and user data
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 100
- User restores the backuped course with activities and user data
- User edits the graded activity
- The grade value is analyzed
- The Grade Type dropdown value is set to 'Point'
- The Scale dropdown is disabled
- The Grade Point text field is populated with 1000

The user submits the form and validation code returns an error highlighting that the grade point entered is higher than the site imposed maximum.


*Example 2*
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 1000
- User creates a graded activity
- Grade Type = 'Point'
- Scale - disabled because Grade Type is not 'scale'
- Grade Point - 30
- Saves the form
- Creates a backup of the course, activities and user data
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 100
- User restores the backuped course with activities and user data
- User edits the graded activity
- The grade value is analyzed
- The Grade Type dropdown value is set to 'Point'
- The Scale dropdown is disabled
- The Grade Point text field is populated with 30

The user submits the form and the value stored in the grade column of the module's table is 30.

*Example 3*
- Site wide grade point maximum is set to 1000
- User creates a graded activity
- Grade Type = 'scale'
- Scale - Scale value
- Grade Point - automatically disabled because Grade Type is not 'point'
- Saves the form
- Creates a backup of the course, activities and user data
- The scale used in the graded activity is removed
- User restores the backuped course with activities and user data
- User edits the graded activity
- The grade value is analyzed
- The Grade Type dropdown value is set to 'Scale'
- The Scale defaults to the "standard scale value" of -1
- The Grade Point text field is disabled

The user submits the form and the value stored in the grade column of the module's table is -1.


h5. Modify moodleform_mod.php to use new grading formslib element

Two areas in this file require modification.  The first is in the standard_grade_coursemodule_element(), the second is in the standard_coursemodule_elements.

The standard_grade_coursemodule_element() first checks to see if the module does *not* support a rating grade.  Then adds the standard grading element to the page.

The standard_coursemodule_elements() first checks to see if the modules does support a rating grade.  Adds the standard grading element to the page, but sets the grade element to disabled if the user selects 'No Ratings' for the Aggregate type

Both of these areas will have to be modified to call the newly created grade element.

h5. Inconsistencies in graded module tables

For lesson module's table, the grade column is defined as a smallint(3) datatype.  Other modules, except the quiz, store the grade column as a int(10).  The quiz module stores the grade as a decimal(10, 5).

The problem here being that the lesson module can't accept grade point values greater than 32767.  Where as other modules could accept grade point values as high as 2147483647.  In the case of the quiz module it could go beyond 2147483647.

The gradebook table has a grade value defined as a decimal(10, 5).

11/Oct/13 12:43 AM;712020:7275f6a3-a6cd-4c0c-b932-f5f1906c7b72;Hi Andrew,

- I've updated the language strings and the parameter descriptions.
- The idea behind using "data === ''" rather than empty() is to show a validation error when the user enters "0" - indicating that the entry must be between 1 and 10000. Changing this to used empty() causes the default value to be used when "0" is entered.
- For "((string)(int)$data === (string)$data", the purpose here is to validate a string that contains an integer. $data is going to be a string, so is_int() won't work here, and double-casting and strict-comparing ensures that the string $data contains only a valid integer. (For example, "123abc" would fail this test). This is the same idea for "$isintlike = ((string)(int)$val === $val) ? true : false;".
- Main reason for not updating modgrade is that it is used in at least one other place not covered by this issue (/mod/workshop/form/accumulative/edit_form.php), and didn't want to break anything else (plugins, etc) that might be using it.

Summary: Gradebook calculations when all input grades are null
Description:
At the moment, the code for computing calculated grades (The method use_formula in lib/grade/grade_item.php) replaces any missing/null input grades with 0 before applying the formula.

Based on our usage here at the Open University, we would like to propose a small change to this behaviour. What we would like is:
1. If ALL the input grades to a calculation are missing/null, then the result of the calculation is null.
2. Otherwise, the result is calculated as at present, with any missing grades treated as 0.

The attached patch implements this change.

I know everyone is busy with Moodle 2.0 at the moment, but I would be grateful for any consideration you can give this. (The patch should apply to 1.9 or 2.0.)

Summary: SCORM player makes width and height of new window a percentage if either value set to 100
Description:
When scos are set to launch in a new window it seems like the width and height settings are interpreted as percentages *only* when they're 100. w: 100, h: 100 = maximised window
w: 100, h: 101 = very wide, short window

Summary: Allow hub admin to customize subject fields
Description:
The issue was brought on this forum topic: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=153853

Hopefully Moodle 2.0.1 will support Hub Global Searches. Moodle user will be able to search quickly in one click on any public hub. But it is possible. The global search engine could search on the higher level subject. Say a hub administrator creates 'veterinary for dogs only' subject under the original 'Veterinary' subject.  Say his 'Veterinary' hub allows global search.

Note that at the moment, a publisher cannot select anything else than third level subject. So this solution cannot be implemented yet without being able to publish on first or second level.

About removing a subject from the list, it is a bit similar but easier. It's a matter for a registered site to request the subjects list from a hub.

Summary: Capability (or setting) for viewing performance info
Description: Administrators may wish to see performance info on a production environment, but not show it to teachers or students.  The obvious solution to me would be to create a capability for viewing performance info, and only set MDL_PERFTOFOOT etc. if the user has that capability (and the performance info setting is enabled).  An alternative solution would be to change the setting (or add a new one) to allow you to choose whether non-admin users can view performance info - but capabilities seems like a cleaner approach as it also allows you to use user-specific overrides to allow an individual user to view performance info when their role doesn't normally allow it.

Summary: Allow usage of dvipng in Tex filter
Description: As I understand the current flow of the core Tex filter (http://cvs.moodle.org/moodle/filter/tex/latex.php?revision=1.12&view=markup) we convert to postscript and then to png.  However,  current versions of Tex (http://www.tug.org/texlive/doc/texlive-en/texlive-en.html) have contained the "new" dvipng binary for some time (dvipng has been available on its own since 2002). For Tex Live documentation see: http://www.tug.org/texlive/Contents/live/texmf/doc/dvipng/dvipng.html. Should the filter be tweaked to determine if dvipng is available, and to use same instead of convert and dvips? I've had a brief look at this and I'd like to note that Ubuntu (10.04) doesn't install dvipng when you install LaTeX (Ubuntu uses texlive too). You have dvipng in a separate package. Hardly a problem, but it seems that not all Linux distros install the whole LaTeX features by default.

That little "problem" aside, I'd say the rest of the feature shouldn't be hard to implement. My only concern is about the user interface. How to make it clear that you can/should either use dvipng or dvips + convert, and which one we use in case the user specified the path for all the executables. 08/Sep/10 12:30 PM;712020:273645be-1bff-4312-83c9-c0622a9c8a05;Thanks for taking a look at this Iñaki

As to Ubuntu,  I assume that when you say that it doesn't install dvipng when you install TexLive you talking about using Ubuntu rpms for TexLIve, as opposed to doing a TexLive installation? My initial response would be that we would have to leave download of all the appropriate texLive packages for the user (with a note in Moodle docs about dvipng as an option)  However,  if one does the  TexLive install via install-ti  one also gets the tlmgr, and that may be a handy tool to have available to moodle users (as well as anyone else use to managing perl). Using tlmgr also means one does not need to be root to manage tex,  another point that may help moodle users (and it has a GUI,  which would be of value to windows users...)

I had initially thought that some additional settings in the config page  that would add a  location for dvipng and explain in small print that dvipng does the work of dvips +convert and of course we would need to tweak texdebug. If present the latex page would default to using that and if not if would fall back to current behavior. It really would not effect Moodle if the user had convert and dvips installed if the user also had dvipng installed as tweak to latex.php would use only dvipng if it was present.  In other words, not to worry if things work.  If they don't work then texdebug can explain that one needs one or the two others....

As I mentioned we could also add some settings to alter the behavior of dvipng (for example to output gifs, etc) but this is part and parcel of the choice between redoing the tex filter (which is needed) or just doing a quicky tweak to keep so many people from having to mess with obtaining and properly locating convert.

Summary: File picker defaults to current course in hierarchy for Server Files tab
Description:
The file management in Moodle 2.0 will be an area that users of previous versions will have a lot of difficulty with. To ease this transition, and to provide a more familiar environment for choosing and managing files, this Issue proposes that upon opening the file picker in Moodle 2+:
1. Opens with the Server Files tab active (if available)
2. Viewing the course level in the hierarchy as a starting point, with the ability to navigate up or down the hierarchy as required.
3. This behaviour is set as a user preference, defaulted to true.

This is also likely to be more convenient, based on the assumption that an existing file is more likely to be in the course hierarchy than anywhere else. Screen shot attached.

Summary: Add revision and caching support for Moodle YUI modules [Patch]
Description:
MDL-22920 added support for easily loading custom YUI modules (aka Moodle YUI modules) via the new yui_module function.  This function causes these modules to get loaded via yui_combo.php (regardless of the useexternalyui or yuicomboloading settings).

Currently, yui_combo.php does not support caching or revisions.  Originally this wasn't necessary as YUI and YUI Galleries (the only JS previously loaded by yui_combo) had their own versioning.  Moodle YUI modules need to be versioned so they can be cached effectively and still updated when purging caches.

The attached patch adds support for including $CFG->jsrev in the yui_combo URLs for Moodle YUI modules.  The $CFG->cachejs setting is also supported.

I did not add cachejs or jsrev support to YUI modules as it has its own built in versioning.  Similarly I didn't modify YUI Galleries as yui_module already supports gallery versions.  This means that if cachejs is off, YUI modules and YUI Galleries will still be far-future cached.  Only Moodle YUI modules will not be cached if cachejs is off.  I think this is what *should* happen because YUI modules should only be changed upstream.

Please see the forum post: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=154359

Summary: {prefix}context path index is pretty much useless
Description:
If a PostgreSQL Moodle database is running with UTF-8 encoding/locale settings, then the default index on the {prefix}context table's path column is mostly useless, as the majority of queries on that column use a LIKE operator. My understanding is that UTF-8 databases are either required or strongly recommended for Moodle, so this will pretty much impact all PostgreSQL Moodle instances.

To enable this index to work as (I assume) expected, the index should be created with explicit use of the varchar_pattern_ops opclass. The relevant PostgreSQL syntax is:

CREATE INDEX mdl_con_pat_ix_patternops ON mdl_context (path varchar_pattern_ops);

I suggest that the original index, without the pattern op class, is not really required and would provide more overhead than performance benefit so should probably be replaced rather than running both.
Comments:
22/Jul/10 1:22 PM;5a0119b6c24efb3c4ed42802;On postgres 8.3 and 8.4 with a UTF8 db the index does appear to be used, what version of Postgres are you using?

EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM mdl_context WHERE path LIKE '/1/34%';
                                       QUERY PLAN                                       
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Index Scan using mdl_cont_pat_ix on mdl_context  (cost=0.00..8.36 rows=54 width=42)
   Index Cond: (((path)::text ~>=~ '/1/34'::text) AND ((path)::text ~<~ '/1/35'::text))
   Filter: ((path)::text ~~ '/1/34%'::text

22/Jul/10 1:54 PM;557058:5958070b-3655-4561-9f4a-793b7dadc823;I'm testing on an 8.3.9 instance.

Was your PostgreSQL cluster created with a C locale? You can use pg_controldata to check:

# pg_controldata /var/lib/pgsql/data | grep LC
LC_COLLATE:                           en_US.UTF-8
LC_CTYPE:                             en_US.UTF-8

Without a pattern ops index, I get a seq scan and with the pattern ops index I get an index scan. I'm aware that this could be due to other influencing factors, but my understanding of PostgreSQL's btree indexes is that they do not apply to LIKE or ~ comparators unless your cluster was initdb'd with locale = "C" [1][2]. Example follows.

# explain analyze SELECT ctx.*
                             FROM mdl_context ctx
                             WHERE ctx.path LIKE '/1/42848/223267/268362/%';
                                                   QUERY PLAN                                                    
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Seq Scan on mdl_context ctx  (cost=0.00..1264.68 rows=6 width=38) (actual time=239.613..239.613 rows=0 loops=1)
   Filter: ((path)::text ~~ '/1/42848/223267/268362/%'::text)
 Total runtime: 239.637 ms
(3 rows)

# create index mdl_con_pat_ix_patternops on mdl_context (path varchar_pattern_ops);
CREATE INDEX
# explain analyze SELECT ctx.*
                             FROM mdl_context ctx

                                                                 QUERY PLAN                                                                 
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Index Scan using mdl_con_pat_ix_patternops on mdl_context ctx  (cost=0.00..8.28 rows=6 width=38) (actual time=0.139..0.139 rows=0 loops=1)
   Index Cond: (((path)::text ~>=~ '/1/42848/223267/268362/'::text) AND ((path)::text ~<~ '/1/42848/223267/2683620'::text))
   Filter: ((path)::text ~~ '/1/42848/223267/268362/%'::text)
 Total runtime: 0.186 ms
(4 rows)

# rollback;
ROLLBACK

Summary: Additional features for forum activity
Description:
New features for forum:

Set forum to read only.  This is available by role changes, but this option is only available for admins in standard configuration. It should be an option for teachers to change forum settings to read only for a forum that is inactive now.

Mark a forum topic as answered. The author of initial post or trainer should be able to mark a forum topic as finalised/closed or answered. If a forum is used for question it should be possible to say 'this is finally answered".  The status should be marked in the overview of  topics for a forum
Comments:
26/Jul/10 12:14 PM;70121:c59fa592-e4e0-4800-ad5a-9045fe034c92;I thought I saw somewhere some significant forum developments down for 2.1, but I cannot find the reference.   I am in favour of both these enhancements in this request.  Some comments follow.

Comment 1: From the second part of this post: 
"Mark a forum topic as answered. The author of initial post or trainer should be able to mark a forum topic as finalised/closed or answered. If a forum is used for question it should be possible to say 'this is finally answered". The status should be marked in the overview of topics for a forum"

This brings the coding down to the thread level.  Another request is for subscriptions at the thread/discussion level.  However the implementations of this have been critised for being too resource intensive.  Obvious really: it's just a lot of work to manage many thread's activity. (one example of technical comment here: http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=118619)  As a non-coder, I am unable to really tell the status of this discussions-subscription enhancement.

Comment 2: This coding at the thread level has probably been behind the continued bug in the Q and A format of the forum where student CAN check other posts, then edit their own, defeating the purpose of using this forum format.  http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-9376

Comment 3: The problem with this added power is it will introduce complexity to the interface and in any of these options there is also hidden complexity.  In this present discussion one request  "Close a forum topic as answered" - I presume this means discussion.  OK.  Does this allow further posts or not?  What about a nice post in the discussion that is off topic?  Does it close it as well to further replies as well as marking it as 'answered', or leave it open to further replies and marking it 'answered'?

ALSO: Students DO have problems if we set up a forum in a different way anyway.  I like being able to give power to posters (like 'the initial poster" above) but I'd like to see things still well designed to be simple as possible.  Ramble over.

I believe adding in some extra power to forums could really help with using Moodle in the teaching and learning process.

28/Jul/10 12:02 AM;712020:75420ce8-d01a-4460-b964-f3d67bd25460;Andrew,

Many thanks for having implemented this new look overlay glossary autolinker. Much better than the former obsolete popup window!

I have some comments.

0.- If we consider that glossary definitions are a kind of help, it might be more coherent to make their overlay windows look more lie help items, and with a close *X* rather than an OK button. But please keep the background of the definition text white, not gray (for the sake of legibility).

1.-  There is no reason why the text of the definition should be displayed centered. It should normally be displayed *left-aligned* (or, I suppose, right-aligned for RTL languages).

2.- It should not be possible to display more than one glossary overlay at the same time (on top of one another!). Clicking on a second hyperlink in the text should *automatically close* the currently displayed overlay. _But see #5 below._

3.- The glossary overlays are displayed right in the middle of the current course window. It _might_ be more user-friendly to display them - when possible - next to the glossary word that has been clicked in the text (same behavior at the help overlays).
Of course it would be very convenient if the student could *move* the glossary window to anywhere they wanted (inside the current main window), as is now possible with the windows such as the File picker...

4- In 1.9, glossary popup windows display (amongst a lot of unwanted stuff) the glossary's *name*. I think that might be a useful information to display (discreetly) somewhere in the newlook overlay glossary window.

5.- It can happen that the same word has beeen entered in 2 (or more) different glossaries. When clicking on the hyperlinked word in a text, in 1.9 the definitions from those 2 (or more) glossaries were displayed in the same popup window, one at the top and the other below the first, etc..
In current newlook overlay window, those 2 entries are displayed in 2 separate overlay windows, on top of one another. The overlay window at the back is displayed when the front window is dismissed. I'm not sure this is the best display for the end-user, but it might be difficult to implement it otherwise?

Summary: Moodle XML import/export doesn't save category description
Description:
When question category descriptions were added Moodle XML import/export format missed this...
So it saves only name of the category.
Should be easy to fix thought....
Comments:
12/Aug/10 11:53 AM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;Actually, this is not quite as simple as all that.

The problem is that the category is stored in the file as a path, like

Category Top/Category sub

Suppose you import that into an empty course. There is no place to put the description of Category Top.

So, we could only export the description of categories that contain questions.

Then, there is the problem that the questions are written to the file ordered by qtype, name, you cannot even guarantee that all the question from the same category are together, or that any the questions from the top category come before questions from the subcategory.

So, if you first encounter a question from Category sub, you create 
Category Top with no description, and then later when you get to a question from 
Category Top, you might be able to go back and add the description to the category top you created before, but that is not easy. (When importing into an existing course, you don't want to overwrite existing category descriptions.)

The other option is to re-order the export, so it exports in the order of the category tree. That is probably the best thing, but would require more substantial changes to the code.

So, this is not as easy to fix as we thought, so it will have to wait until after 2.0. Sorry.

16/Aug/18 7:29 PM;5c09c8b4b203a71cc9cb1bc1;Hi John,

Thanks for taking over this issue and moving it along, and thanks to the others here for their great work on getting this issue to where it is now. This is a big improvement on import/export of categories!

I've run through the code and testing steps, and have a few suggestions to make, mostly minor things but there is one fairly important thing in point 1.

*1.* When running through the human testing on an unpatched master branch (for reference as I usually do), I noticed that after the import of the apple/banana/carrot tree example, the apple category wasn't created at the correct position, and in fact, I have 2 apple categories (I'll attach a screenshot of the post-import view). One contains a question, one does not. This is a problem only with the import, as an import of the same export file (created on unpatched master) creates incorrect/correct categories depending on whether the patch is applied.

Category descriptions aside, this is a legitimate bug, and it's only present in 35 and master because of some recent changes to the way 'top' categories were represented (---MDL-61132---). Thanks to [~accountid:62b96026fa171a27239c3e14] for discussion around this one. The interesting thing, however, is that your patch fixes this bug.

I think right now the best course of action is to hold off on landing this issue in it's current form (as an improvement), and first revisit which code in the patch fixes this 'top' bug. Then, we'll separate that out into another MDL (I've created MDL-63165 and assigned you there) for this. This issue could then be blocked by this bug fix if need be, but I'll leave that up to you to resolve.

*2.* Please change the commit component name to either 'question' or 'core_question'. I.e. lose the caps. We don't need 'Moodle' in there either.

*3.* This is an improvement, and as such will only land in master. The 'question/format/upgrade.txt' changes should reflect 3.6, not 3.4.

*4.* It seems the $displayprogress instance var, was added solely to allow switching off output during testing. I dislike this because it's adding something to a class to ONLY be used during testing. I would prefer to see this handled another way. Either:
 – In phpunit, via expectOutputString() (not ideal, imo) or;
 – Change the qformat_default class to require use a progress_trace type object (see subclasses in weblib), and then create the qformat_xml object using a null_progress_trace when using phpunit, thus generating no output.

*5.* Please keep in mind to typehint params and returns for any new functions you've added given we're now on php 7+:
 – [this one|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/compare/master...Beedell:wip-MDL-23545-master#diff-a22f7fcc9a0c5e983df0ac8d96aaf5e7R1495]
 – [this one|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/compare/master...Beedell:wip-MDL-23545-master#diff-f51db7f1fc039f54de7ebcce35e522f3R963]

 *6.* Why is [this function|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/compare/master...Beedell:wip-MDL-23545-master#diff-f51db7f1fc039f54de7ebcce35e522f3R963] publicly scoped? I can't see this being used anywhere else, and I don't foresee that it will be. Please make it protected.

*7.* According to the comments, [this case|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/compare/master...Beedell:wip-MDL-23545-master#diff-f51db7f1fc039f54de7ebcce35e522f3R577] should not occur, but we're not throwing an exception and instead just blindly continuing. Surely, if it's exceptional/unexpected behaviour, we're better off throwing an appropriate exception so we know it failed.

*8.* The global function 'question_categorylist_parents' should be unit tested.

+Other minor points:+
 *9.* We should try to be consistent with syntax for arrays - see [here|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/compare/master...Beedell:wip-MDL-23545-master#diff-f51db7f1fc039f54de7ebcce35e522f3R844] and [here|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/compare/master...Beedell:wip-MDL-23545-master#diff-f51db7f1fc039f54de7ebcce35e522f3R869]. Please pick one style and stick with it. I prefer [], but either one is fine.

*10.* Comments like [this one|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/compare/master...Beedell:wip-MDL-23545-master#diff-a22f7fcc9a0c5e983df0ac8d96aaf5e7R1516] really don't add a lot to the code as anyone can see what that call is doing. Instead, we should explain the reason for reversing the array, making it clear why the output needs to be in some certain order. If there's a defined order, then we should also document this in the docblock for that function.
 – Ditto, [here|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/compare/master...Beedell:wip-MDL-23545-master#diff-f51db7f1fc039f54de7ebcce35e522f3R871], [here|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/compare/master...Beedell:wip-MDL-23545-master#diff-f51db7f1fc039f54de7ebcce35e522f3R882].

 *11*. The param [here|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/compare/master...Beedell:wip-MDL-23545-master#diff-f51db7f1fc039f54de7ebcce35e522f3R960] isn't really mixed. From what I see, it's taking an stdClass, so please amend this and make the comment clear as to why.

 *12.* I note that the param added to create_category_path is called $lastcategoryinfo, but then we're calling this using $question [on this line|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/compare/master...Beedell:wip-MDL-23545-master#diff-f51db7f1fc039f54de7ebcce35e522f3R386]. This needs clarification. If it's a question we expect, then name and document it accordingly. The name and docs for $lastcategoryinfo could use some clarification.

 *13.* I'd normally rewrite stuff like [this|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/compare/master...Beedell:wip-MDL-23545-master#diff-a22f7fcc9a0c5e983df0ac8d96aaf5e7R1501] to:
{code}if (!$parent) {
    return [];
}
$categorylist = [$parent];
{code}
*14.* Generally, coding style only changes should be in a separate commit ([https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Coding_style#Policy_about_coding-style_only_fixes]) and I see quite a few here. Given this issue is an aggregation of many people's work, I'm going to ignore this time, but something to keep in mind for future.

So, with all that said, I'm going to reopen this issue for now to allow the necessary changes to be made. Really, this solution is looking very good and it's only a few small things and that linked bug which are holding proceedings up.

 I'd also encourage you to pick up the linked bug and contribute the relevant code there, as it will be very nice to sort that out. 

Thanks
 Jake

IMS Common Cartridge Import Detailed Errors
Description:
In trying to import an Angel-exported IMS Common Cartridge, I received an error "The schema is not valid."

I see several similar issues here, most closed with "not a bug"

Testing with IMS Desktop Validator, I found that, indeed, Angel generates broken cartridges.

But downloading and installing and validating took a fair amount of effort, and I would have preferred Moodle to have just told me specifically what was broken instead.

I therefore humbly submit my first patch, which organizes import errors by level and dumps them out as notify messages.  It's a bit verbose, and perhaps should be an expandable display: none; div instead, but it's a start.  I don't know enough Moodle internals yet to do that properly, and I doubt you'd want inline JS hackery in the patch...

I added a CSS class for level, but did not actually style them in any particular way; I leave that to somebody more familiar with Moodle front-end.

There is not much I can do to convince Blackboard to actually fix Angel IMS CC export; But at least I can help Moodlers know that the cartridge they are trying to import is truly broken, and exactly how.

This also helps nudge Moodle closer to IMS CC compliance, which specifically states:

"On import LMS should confirm that package has imported properly or that there were errors importing the package. Error messages should attempt to direct the user to the problem within the package such as identify a resource that could not be located within the package." section 6.2.4 of imscc_profilev1p0.

06/Aug/10 7:50 AM;712020:16f9264c-6def-45fe-9bb0-11447d6b0bec;Not directly relevant, but in case somebody ends up here:

Your first step to fix the cartridge is to unzip it, edit the imsmanifest.xml file in the root, and replace all '\' with '//' so the URLs look correct, compared to the non-broken ones in the XML.

Then update that file in the zip with:
zip -u YOURFILE.zip imsmanifest.xml

That got me past the XML being invalid.

Moodle claims my course has no title, however, and I'm a bit stuck there for now.

17/Aug/10 11:48 AM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;What is wrong with MyISAM? Pretty much everything if you care about your data:

1/ it does not support transactions - webservices rely on transactions to clean up after invalid requests, only because of MyISAM we did not fix those ugly double click problems yet, ...
2/ it is not atomic - mysql can fail or be stopped in the middle of UPDATE or DELETE statement - our code is not designed to deal with this, you have to recover manually
3/ mysqldump is a joke - it can not produce any reasonable backup without stopping apache or blocking access to all tables (please note you MUST use --single-transaction for innodb tables!); even with innodb you can not run upgrades at the same time
4/ repair tables does NOT fix any data - because it is not ACID engine you can not actually fix the data, there is no way to validate that the "repaired" tables have any meaningful information, the repair only makes your tables readable/writable again, it does not guarantee reasonable state of your data

Summary:
1/ old sites with at least one MyISAM table are warned on the admin/index.php page
2/ there are two tools for migration - the web UI for innodb only, the CLI script that handles any engine migration and list current engine for each table
3/ new installations ignore MyISAM as default DB and use INNODB or XtraDB instead
4/ when adding new tables during upgrade we always use "current" engine detected from the config table
5/ mysql transaction support detection is more intelligent now
6/ you can for override engine and transaction detection via dboptions - no queries used == better perf
7/ the recommendation is a lot less radical than in the patch above, feel free to tweak it as necessary

I hope this will make the transition away from MyISAM as painless as possible.

Thank you for the feedback and ideas!

Petr Skoda

There are a couple of points I'd like to ask you / other core people about further before changing:

The first relates to login/lib.php, points 1 & 3; Duplicates / cold guesses have been made very unlikely by lengthening the size of the secret/token.  With 32 lowercase, uppercase, and numeric characters, there are 62^32 combinations.

My maths on this was: assuming there were 500 password reset requests for valid user accounts (leading to 1 Million valid tokens at any one time), and 500 token guesses per second. With these numbers you'd still expect it to be millions of years before you get a hit.  Much faster to just guess passwords directly.
That said I was keen to avoid the 'clear the secret on failure' functionality on the basis that it meant attackers could be a nuisance by preventing real password resets, without providing security improvements.  It we wanted to limit the 500/sec, then we could add functionality which requires captcha validation above a certain level of reset requests & invalid token redemptions. But again, an enhancement that can come later.

18/Nov/13 5:41 AM;5d2255e36086600c51add7da;Hi Martin,
I'd petition a change from "this would be a security problem" to "this is be a security problem in certain circumstances".

Since in many organisations usernames are schema driven, and publicly known, eg student id numbers.

If an attacker was guessing usernames or passwords, there's a good chance they'd be able to tell when they hit one based on the response time (code path for successful query is very different to unsuccessful query).

So this creates a security problem where you allow weak passwords, but are saved by having obsecure usernames, and the attacker can't tell based on response time when they've hit an account.

So for some (many?) users, it makes sense - they get improved usability, and they aren't worried about revealing usernames (they may be obvious anyway), and are happy with their password strength relative to attacker's desire to compromise the system.

Summary: Switch for update of internal password
Description:
I tried to wrote an Authentication plugin, that authenticates against the field mdl_user.idnumber. At the same time this auth-plugin had a fallback to the manual-auth-plugin. So iff authentication via username and "idnumber" could not be done, a passed password would be evaluated by the manual-plugin to authenticate.
This means when authentication via "idnumber" was done, there is no value in $user->password.

Moodle by default updates the internal password, when user authentication was successful.
In my case, when I authenticated via "idnumber" and the $password thus is empty, Moodle will store an empty string (as hash) in mdl_user.password.
But of course I want to keep the original password, so I can always use it as a fallback!
The method "prevent_local_passwords" is no help either, because it overwrites the internal password with "not cached" as you know.

The method in question is "update_internal_user_password" in "lib/moodlelib.php".
The statement says: 
return set_field ('user', 'password', $hashedpassword, 'id', $user->id);

Wouldn't it be possible to have some kind of switch here, so I can turn that off - either as plugin developer or in general as Moodle Admin in the Moodle configuration?
Comments:
12/Aug/10 12:38 AM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;Hello,

it should be possible to use the loginpage_hook method in your plugin and implement the idnumber login directly there, the password would not be updated because the code you are mentioning above would not be executed at all. In the hook your would access the _POST directly and set up global $user if the idnumber is correct, the standard password would be handled by normal manual plugin.

Petr Skoda

Summary: Implement extra_question_tables functionality like extra_question_fields
Description:
Tim, preg and other question under my development require extra tables, which will store question-specific data. 

I want to implement extra_question_tables functionality to automatically get/save options, delete question, backup/restore and XML import/export for such tables.

I could either test it on my questions, or upgrade numerical to use it for units handling.

Please let me know, what you think about it and will you check in such patch if I'll write it.
Comments:
14/Aug/10 1:50 PM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;I am hesitant for various reasons.

First, we are heading in the direction of writing a general object-relational mapping layer - and such a thing is a hard problem. Not something we should try to do as a subset of Moodle's question system.

Second, the fact that different question types all have their own database tables concerns me. It is really bad for scalability, because it takes multiple database queries to load each question in the quiz. So, for an n-question quiz it is O(n) DB queries, and the best optimisation takes that to O(q), where there are q different question types. So, I don't necessarily want to make it easier to create question types with lots of DB tables.

I agree that writing load/save backup/restore, import/export, etc. is a bit repetitive and dull, but it is not that hard.

And, I am really busy at the moment, so would be reluctant to commit to reviewing more code. I have deadlines at the OU and with what time I have to do core Moodle work, I think I should focus on issues that are important for the Moodle 2.0 release.

Of course, you are welcome to write whatever code you like within your question type plugins, and you could make all your question types based on a common subclass. (And, if you come up with something really amazingly good, we might later refactor it into the general question type base class.)

14/Aug/10 2:21 PM;557058:da9db912-345f-4bcd-930f-662df4367d7c;1. I'm not going to do that soon, there are more important tasks right now. It well may be an autumn or even winter.

2. "Second, the fact that different question types all have their own database tables concerns me. It is really bad for scalability ... So, I don't necessarily want to make it easier to create question types with lots of DB tables." - 

2.1. "I agree that writing load/save backup/restore, import/export, etc. is a bit repetitive and dull, but it is not that hard."  This is very like Petr's argument against git for allowing to easy create and update mods. This is not working thing, irritaiting - but not stopping. Do you think this will stop anyone who really need a new table? Or do you think many people will find it in the depth of default_questiontype class (how many are find extra_question_fields by now?)? After all, adding new tables will only change O (2*n) to O (k*n), which is almost same for scalability. 

2.2. IMHO it will be much easier to control performance and optimise things when you have them universally coded in one place, it is almost impossible when you have them coded in several you plugins and a horde of 3d party plugin authors into the bargain.

2.3. I'm going to add those tables for performance issues too. When doing DFA regular expression matching more than 90% of time going to parsing expression and build FA. If we cache FA's in DB, then it will take a lot less time to match them for grading/looking for feedback to display, while adding only one more DB query per question (even with many regexes).  I've already implemented memory caching, but one answer is rarely matching twice in one page load.

3. "you could make all your question types based on a common subclass" - that's an old problem. I should either give up idea of self-contained plugins (i.e. you should install this abstract qtype separately for the real question type to work), or I should duplicate that code in every plugin. I don't like any of these two options...

P.S. " if you come up with something really amazingly good, we might later refactor it into the general question type base class." -if I write some thing as a part of my plugins and will be happy with the way it is, I don't necessarily will be motivated to do extra work to include it in the core... ;)

15/Aug/10 12:03 AM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;The thing is, the correct scalability is a constant number of database queries to render any page.

The design that lets you do that is a table question_options that looks something like

id, questionid, optionname (VARCHAR), optionvalue (TEXT)

Of course, that is bad in other ways, because it is a non-normalised database schema, and also all values are stored as TEXT, not as their real type.

Oh, and it does not deal with the requirements of question types like match.

So, it is still a vague idea that I will go on thinking about. I would not make any change until I was sure (and others agreed) that the benefits outweighed the disadvantages.

15/Aug/10 2:44 AM;557058:da9db912-345f-4bcd-930f-662df4367d7c;There is another vague idea: what if question type should return join part of the SQL operator to join all it's tables in the one request (and, maybe, other needed parts)? I guess with correct type of join (or subquery, or something), it is possible to combine all questions loading to the two queries (one for questions and one for answers, I guess answers still better been loaded separately). For some questions there will be more than one line per question in results, that's all.

Then each question object will receive all lines with it's questionid as an argument to the get_question_options function and parse it as needed.

I remember one project where I was forced to do quite complex data processing on pure SQL (just select/updates, no stored procedures, views etc) and they were working extremly fast.
15/Aug/10 3:09 AM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;Yes. That is the other possible approach. Again, it has its strengths and weaknesses.

16/Aug/10 9:18 AM;557058:da9db912-345f-4bcd-930f-662df4367d7c;"Again, it has its strengths and weaknesses." - could you explain we its weaknesses please? I can't find them myself and very interested in knowing it.

26/Aug/10 8:09 AM;557058:5188c7d7-5671-48d1-b501-6c3ae2b91f34;Some problems that I have encountered before with this sort of approach:

# Building queries by concatenating SQL from different sources can be very fragile and leads to hard to debug problems. For example, the way we build SQL in the quiz overview report is horrible. Changing that for my question engine rewrite took ages. On the other hand, I chose this approach in question_bank_column_base and its subclasses in question/editlib.php in Moodle 2.0, and it is not too bad there.
# There are name-spacing problems. For example, both match and multichoice want to join in a shuffleanaswers column from different tables. Again, this is solvable, but makes things messier, and again can be hard to debug (the bug will only show up in a quiz that uses the two question types that clash).
# Database query optimisers struggle with queries that reference too many different tables. The number of possible execution plans explodes exponentially.

There are probably other issues too.

01/Sep/10 2:05 AM;557058:da9db912-345f-4bcd-930f-662df4367d7c;Many thanks for explanation, Tim.

1. I don't want to concatenate SQL from different source, the sources must provide only information about tables/fields/links like extra_question_fields. We should generate SQL in one place. 2. This should be solvable (add a prefixed aliance?). I think it is possible to write unit-test that make up a query with one instance of all installed question types to debug such clashes.
3. This is pretty unavoidable. Whe should either have:
3.1. Multiple queries with multiple tables (for each qtype)
3.2. One query with many tables (for each qtype)
3.3. Forcing all questions to add columns to one table for question instances (prefixed with question type).

Now we have 3.1. Is 3.2. worse?

27/Aug/10 1:42 AM;712020:b5150701-426f-4366-8867-eb21bcad988f;Hmm, my comment was incorrect, it is all a lot more complex. Ideally everything should be controlled by one capability only,
If you have more capabilities it is extremely hard to visualise - you have to do AND or OR between the individual results for each user, the prohibit cap breaks all your simple logic.

==AND==
- you have to have at least one role from each group of allowed roles - you have to evaluate capabilities separately, you can not sum roles
- you must not have forbidden role in any group - you can sum all forbidden roles - you must not have any of forbidden roles

==OR===
