Summary: Slow query on course_display in get_complete_user_data()
Description:
In lib/moodlelib.php in the get_complete_user_data() function around line 3777 below the /// Get various settings and preferences comment there's a call to $DB->get_records('course_display', array('userid'=>$user->id)

This function gets called every time a new session starts.  On OpenLearn, there are many guest sessions started frequently, so this particular query gets called a lot.  There's no index on course_display for just userid, though there is one for course,userid.

This query is appearing rather too often in my slow queries log, so I was wondering whether adding an index just for user would help?  I could do this just as an OU customisation, but I guess it must affect some other big sites as well, and since its in Moodle 1.9 and Moodle 2.0 perhaps this is a good time to get the change into core?  Happy to code it myself if someone would just give me a thumbs up?

(Note all these code references are for Moodle 2.0 but the same problem exists in Moodle 1.9 which is where I've actually seen the problem on my live system).

Summary: [Patch] Improve support for horizontal and right aligned docks in dock.js
Description:
The attached patch improves support for horizontal docks and right-aligned docks to the dock.js file.

It makes three main changes:

# The {{dockitem_container}} and {{controls}} divs are now wrapped in a "buttons" container.  In a horizontal dock, each dockitem will need to float.  The controls div would also need to float after the dock items.  Without this additional container, it is nearly impossible for the theme designer to contain the floats (each dockitem floats, dockitem_container floats, and controls float).  Another solution would be to include the {{controls}} div within the {{dockitem_container}} div, but I didn't want to mess up any existing themes.
# M.core_dock.resize has been modified to adjust panel's left and top styles according to the dock orientation and position.  Resize understands orientations {{vertical}} and {{horizontal}} and orientations {{left}}, {{right}}, and {{top}}.
# A new body class is added referencing dock's orientation and position, e.g. {{has_dock_left_vertical}}, {{has_dock_right_vertical}}, {{has_dock_top_horizontal}}.  This will help themes support multiple dock layouts.

This patch doesn't contain any CSS updates.  Existing left-vertical docks should continue to work without any issues.  Obviously, themes would need to update their CSS if a different dock layout was desired.

Summary: Allow users to change order of courses in course listings areas
Description:
Below is a fairly common request by our clients (Remote-Learner), and something that might be nice to see a change in 2.0.

This concerns the My Moodle course overview block, the list of courses area on everyone's main page, as well as the My Courses block listed in both the My Moodle area as well as everyone's main page.
Courses in all 3 areas appear to be in order based on course ID number (in 2.0...in 1.9 the My Courses block is in alphabetical order). This doesn't seem to be efficient because, newer courses will have higher ID numbers, thus putting them at the bottom of the list causing users to have to scroll to find their new courses.

 It is understood that these changes can be made at the site administration level, however, it would be nice if these changes could be made on a user to user basis no matter your role on the site.  There are a few potential hopeful solutions to this issue:

Level 1 (potentially fastest, easiest) - Have courses ordered, in both places (My courses block / Course overview block), based on most recent activity.

Level 2 - Give all users the option to re-order their courses in all areas by giving them move arrows.

Pie in the sky solution: Allow all users to reorder their courses in all areas and create collapsible categories/sub-categories for their courses.

Example of what is happening: One of my colleagues spoke with a teacher who has many courses on her lists. She still needs to be able to access all courses b/c she will potentially be teaching them again in the future, the courses are currently hidden b/c they are not being used, however the hidden courses are at the top of her list, or scattered in between other courses. This makes it difficult to locate the appropriate courses when you have a large number of courses in which you are enrolled. If she could create a category called 'Inactive courses'  and another called 'active' courses - she could then locate the necessary course quicker.

Summary: Change standard Moodle themes to use sans serif fonts
Description:
Based on what I've read, the recommendation for web design and online content is to use sans serif fonts. Since this practice is a fairly well accepted standard and based on research that indicates that sans serif fonts are easier to read on screen, I would propose that all of the themes included with a standard Moodle install use sans serif fonts for text in menus and on the course page. Of course, if someone is aware of new research that says differently, please let me know.

In reviewing the standard themes, I found that anomaly, serenity, and brick all have serif fonts. I viewed these themes in both Firefox and Internet Explorer. The magazine theme has a mix of serif and sans serif fonts, but since the text in the menus and links on the course page are sans serif, I think it's probably okay.

On a related note, the font size in the formal white theme is significantly smaller than the font size in other themes. I think it should be sized to match the other themes; at this point, it's really too small to be friendly to a majority of users. Again, viewed this theme in Firefox on Mac and Windows and in IE.

What are the most suitable fonts for the Web?

"There are two levels to your question. One cannot be sure that any user will have a specific named font installed, so the first aspect is what type or family of font is most suitable for the Web. Much research has been done but opinions differ; some say sans serif fonts are better because their large x-height makes them more legible at low scale, others say serifs give a more distinctive letter form that helps readers scan the words."

It is really just a matter of taste - in my opinion all core themes should have the same design and look - but it is useful to add a setting for selecting font fomily from theme settings so that Michelle can select sans serif font family and those users that prefer serif fonts can select serif fonts :)

Summary: [Patch] Add PHP method to determine if the dock will be visible
Description:
Themes currently have the {{region_completed_docked}} method to determine if *all* blocks in a given region are docked.  This helps to prevent _page jump_ by styling the page correctly even before the dock javascript is triggered.

The attached patch adds a complement method, {{region_uses_dock}}, that returns true if *any* of the blocks in a given region (or regions if an array of regions is passed) will be docked.  This can also help to prevent page jump by pre-styling the page for the dock before the dock javascript is executed.

Summary: Prevent installation of 1.9 modules
Description:
If users try to install a 1.9 module in 2.0, this might not be nicely detected. Potentially the user could get the module halfway installed and then see horrible errors.

We considered using the 'requires' version (if 'requires' is a 1.9 version then assume it won't work) but this is not a good solution because 'requires' is actually optional. Many core code modules have incorrect requires value, by the way (they should probably not have it at all, actually, but).

A better solution would probably to add to version.php (etc) a new flag which can be used as well as requires, specifically for cases where backward compatibility is broken:

$version->apilevel = 2;

I was going to code this for the 'requires' version solution but given that a solution is now unclear, I'm just going to put this on record as a tracker issue, maybe this is something for moodle 2.0.1 for instance.

Summary: Add a warning when exiting out of an editor without saving
Description:
There have been many times where me and several other people have accidentally exited out of the Journal, Forum post, Glossery, and other places where an editor is used without saving and lost a significant amount of work that took a long time to write. Its strange that Moodle doesn't have a basic "Are you sure you want to exit out of this?" dialog box when exiting out of a page.

Summary: Warn if user uploads package with different identifiers than previous package
Description:
When uploading a SCORM package over a previous one , if the item identifier in the manifext.xml file is different to the one being overwritten then the tracking data for that SCORM package in Moodle is deleted. While it is understandable that uploading a new SCORM package would clear the tracking data, there is a common requirement to retain the tracking data. For example, when making minor content amends and bug fixes to the SCORM package the item identifier can accidentally get changed (in some products like Articulate its unfortunately very easy to do this) or, when updating, you accidentally 'choose' the wrong zip file and all the existing tracking data for that SCO gets dumped with no warning whatsoever.

This issue is a cause of much frustration to a number of our customers, hence I have logged it as a bug, but it may actually be a feature request ;)

Steps to replicate: Course Page > SCORM Resource > Update this SCORM/AICC > Choose or upload a file > Choose > Save and Return to Course or Save and display.

Suggestion: When clicking Save... in the above sequence, if a SCORM package already exists for this activity and the user is selecting a different SCORM package to replace it, then add in a message asking the user whether they want to retain or clear the existing tracking data for the current SCORM activity.

Note: this will work for single SCORM package but some thought may need to be considered for how SCORM packages containing multiple SCOs should be handled.

Summary: Enrolment duration daylight saving time (time zone)
Description:
Preliminary note: In Moodle, enrolment duration is usually given in days (e. g. in the course settings). The table field "role_assignments.timeend", however, is unixtime, and Moodle computes using seconds as a base unit.

Problem: If the start time and end time of the enrolment period are in different time zones (because of daylight saving time), the additional or missing hour is ignored. As a consequence, enrolment expiry might vary by +/- 1 hour (i. e. can occur at 00:00 am, 01:00 am, or even 11:00 pm on the day before).

Note that in the participants list the column "enrolment ends" does only show the date (not hours, minutes).

Description:
As described in http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=142880#p679299, when downloading a custom user profile field of menu type, the value that gets downloaded is an integer item number representing which option but not the value. It would be better, IMO if the value displayed was downloaded. 

In /user/profile/field/menu/field.class..php, there is the function edit_load_user_data which 

The user_bulk_download.php calls /user/profile/lib.php's profile_load_data which in turn calls the menu field's 
edit_load_user_data function. Since these functions are used elsewhere, I am hesitant to change edit_load_user_data for the menu function but essentially what we are looking for is something like:

$user->{$this->inputname} = $this->options[$this->datakey];

As for security here is how I understand it. This change allows just about any XSS attack to be broadened to a permission elevation (to the admin no less).
The following scenario for instance:
* Student discovers XSS attack vector.
* Writes some crafty JS that does some nasty that would open a window with the "return to admin user" link.
* Files a support ticket with helpdesk, stating a problem on the given page.
* Unsuspecting admin uses loginas to see what the student sees.
* XSS code opens new window to complete the "return to admin" action.
* Original window with the XSS code now has admin access to the site.

I have no idea if this is actually possible of course - it requires an XSS attack vector, some JS, and code that has not previously existed.
Truthfully I never considered the action worth the link.
The setting was a good idea though - people could turn it on if they want. Really I suppose there is a matter of trust, but for a security conscious site I would bet they would not want this setting on if it does indeed expose this kind of security risk.

Mary Smith, John Smith, and Bill Smith are all in the same class.  When the teacher goes to grade an assignment, and chooses to sort the students by last name, the Smiths are seemingly ordered randomly (I belive it is ordering them by ID), so they appear:
John Smith
Mary Smith
Bill Smith


It would be great if the assignment module could sort by firstname within the same lastname,  so they were listed alphabetically:
Bill Smith
John Smith
Mary Smith

This way, there is an easily remembered order for students with the same last name, which would make grading very large classes much easier, and it would fit well where teachers may have class lists in this format.  

In fact, it looks like the assignment module already subsorts by lastname when sorting students by firstname, (ie. Summary: "Save changes" after uploading a file seems unnecessary and causes confusion
Description:
To reproduce...

* Go to My Private Files block
* Select Manage My Private Files
* Upload a file. Note that uploaded files now appears in list of files
* Navigate away without clicking "Save changes"

.... uploaded file is lost even though upload completed and file was shown in the list of files. I have seen this confuse more than one person. In this case, I can't see the necessity for the extra "Save changes" click. It seems completely unnecessary.
Comments:
10/Jun/11 11:51 AM;6054bf8f4a91ad0068d4de34;I second this notion. The same thing happens when moving files around. To move a file into a folder from the "My private files" page, it takes 7 clicks.

Adding to the confusion is the double-click when selecting what folder to move a file into. I think most users associate double-clicking with desktop applications--not web browsers. More, the user then needs to click "Save changes" to finalize moving the file, which is not desktop behaviour at all (I've yet to have to pleasure of using a file manager where I have to explicitly "Save" for my move operation to take hold). Within a single task we have two completely different behaviours (Desktop app vs. web).

I feel this issue is important, because one of the first things that many teachers do when creating a course is upload a course outline. If a teacher goes through a high number of clicks only to forget to click "Save changes" at the end, then his or her first impression of Moodle will not be a complimentary one.

16/Jun/11 6:26 AM;712020:ea8c6c80-24eb-421e-9e02-4e47f81b8253;The problem is wider than just when uploading a file -- *any* changes made to files in the "My Private Files" area produce a visual feedback that *seems* to indicate that the changes have happened already.  For example, when deleting a file, you get a confirmation dialog that asks "Are you sure?", and when you click "Yes" the file disappears from the list.  But if you click away without clicking "Save changes" the file reappears.  See attached collection of screenshots for the flow of dialogs.

At our institution (UMass Amherst) we already have faculty running into this issue when managing files in their "My Private Files" area.  The behavior of the interface leads the user to believe that the changes have happened, when in fact they have not yet been applied.

The "Save changes" button should go away and non-destructive changes should be immediately applied.  Destructive changes, such as deleting a file or folder, already trigger a confirmation dialog.

"Save Changes" is no more than a submit button. Whenever a user is presented with options to change, he/she is modifying a form. The form is only submitted upon pressing "save changes." We are in agreement that it isn't pretty or a very current UI.

Summary: Lesson rename Branch Table to Content
Description:
We need to change the lesson page type currently called "branch table" to either "content" or "description.   I vote for "content".   I realize this will probably not happen in 2.0 but it is long overdue.

The term branch table is not intuitive to a teacher.  For a developer, the branch table is arguably the unique feature of a visible lesson page that contains the student choices.  This area contains the descriptions of the links,  the action to be taken with the link and other '"stuff".  The code comments seem to indicate that by language a branch table is a question page type.   IMO "branch table" goes back to the concept that "Content shall only appear in a question", which we could argue about as a best practice forever.  More importantly, a "branch table" page does not visibly look like a wood table, a periodic table or even a table of columns and rows.  Neither does a question page that uses this feature.  These pages certainly do not look like tables to a student..  

 If something looks more like a duck, then why call it a "rose", or even an "obscure rose"?   

Quiz calls a similar kind of page "description".   However, every site I work with uses a branch table to present content. Teachers will intuitively understand the difference between a content page and a multiple choice page in the context of a lesson and their experience.     

This change might make the end of branch navigation page confusing, we can explain that a branch starts with the closest preceding content page in the edit order.   I think developers would not mind simplifying the code to contain either "clusters", or "branches".  Either of these features should have a specific navigation page that indicate their start and their end. 

This has been bothering me for a long time.   The use of "branch table" in both our documentation and user interface is confusing because of this terminology.

I'm not sure if you (Kirill) are trying to get it into core moodle yourself - if you aren't, but are just providing the patch for anyone who's interested, then that's fine - but I did a code review anyway as somebody might be interested in getting it into core!

Note: there is SOME prospect that 'somebody' might be me, but not in the short term. I think we do have this as a locally requested feature but it's some way down the list.

Review based on github view of commit https://github.com/netspotau/moodle/commit/991be828565d0219c01d6691d045a035c73861e5

This looks pretty good but in order to be included in core moodle, it would need the following changes. 

Major changes (not in order):

A1) Rebase against current master.

A2) Move code from local plugin (eg install.xml needs to go into core lib/db/install.xml & also upgrade.php)

A3) The table names are a bit horrible but also, in order to go into core moodle, the fields in the first table _dt should go into the main course_sections table (analagous to how it works in course_modules) and the _cg table could then be called course_sections_availability or whatever (by 'whatever' I mean, the same name as the equivalent table for course_modules).

A4) The code in conditionlib_section is based on conditionlib. Instead, new functions should be integrated into conditionlib rather than creating a new file. Where the functions are exactly/almost exactly the same but with $cs instead of $cm, hopefully it should be possible to reduce duplication by changing the existing function into a private function that takes either a $cm or $cs parameter and making two public wrappers for the different uses. (Or something like that.)

A5) There is some code duplicated in the two formats (and would need to be duplicated in other custom formats too). This should probably be replaced by a new ->uservisible parameter in course_sections when you get them from modinfo (oh, except I don't think sections work that way) or a new function or something - as you can tell, I haven't really thought this through and it might require more consideration.

A6) I wasn't quite entirely sure if the new section data gets stored in course modinfo. If it does, that's great because it means this system doesn't add any database queries on course view. If it doesn't, that's bad. Also, if it does, I think there might be need for some extra code in course/lib.php to save space in modinfo by making sure not to store the values of those fields if they are default (off).

And some minor notes:

B1) If calling get_record where it is ok for it to return false, I prefer if it explicitly includes the IGNORE_MISSING strictness parameter. (Also btw, in editsection.php there is a brace in wrong place in this if.)

B2) There are some cases of incorrect whitespace etc - Tim's codechecker plugin will find most of these (when submitting code for moodle core, it should not have any codechecker errors/warnings on the lines you change; obviously there may be errors on other lines in the same file that you haven't touched). Some the codechecker doesn't find at the moment, like there should be spaces around =>. NOTE: I am aware that many of these are wrong because the code was copy/pasted from code I originally wrote, which was wrong :) But we didn't have the detailed code style guidelines back then.

B3) Local variable names aren't supposed to have underlines, e.g. $data_dt should be renamed something like $datetimedata or $datadatetime or, at a pinch, $datadt).
 
B4) What's the reason for using insert_record_raw instead of insert_record? If this is actually needed there should be a comment to say why.

B5) You've included changes to modedit, moodleform_mod which are not needed in this patch (regarding change to support times instead of just date, which is already in master) - kind of covered by the 'rebase' thing above but.

B6) In conditionlib, "if (!defined('CONDITION_STUDENTVIEW_HIDE')) {..." is wrong - this script should only be included with require_once so it should never be defined so no condition is necessary. You've probably done this because of conditionlib_section above.

2) Trivial whitespace points from Moodle coding standard:
a) Space around => please
b) Space after comma.
c) Space before the bracket on 'foreach' and 'if' please.
d) When wrapping lines, please use eight spaces (there are some that use 4 or a random amount), except for associative arrays one per line, then it's still 4 (already correct).
e) Space around = (assignment operator)
f) Except for between classes, you should not have more than one blank line in a row (classes have two blank lines between)
It will be easy to find most of these if you run the local codechecker plugin on files you changed (when editing existing files, obviously you should ignore any problems that are on lines you didn't change - the idea is to make sure new code is correct, old code is not your problem and changing it would make the patch harder to read).

4) There are lines that set up $grouparray using =& for object variables - please change these just to use = as =& does not do anything for objects.

-    $showsection = (has_capability('moodle/course:viewhiddensections', $context) or $thissection->visible or !$course->hiddensections);

9) This is my most serious concern - there is way, way too much duplication in conditionlib. There's no way this code could be accepted. We need to kill all the duplication. Luckily unless I'm missing something it should be fairly easy, here's how:

a. Create a base abstract class condition_info_base which takes the following constructor param $tableprefix (stored in a member variable), and has a second protected member variable $item.

b. Change existing condition_info to extends condition_info_base, calling the base constructor with parameter 'course_modules'. The constructor should be changed to use $this->item instead of $this->cm.

'_availability' (or whatever) instead of hardcoded to course_modules_availability:

fill_availability_conditions
add_completion_condition
add_grade_condition
wipe_conditions
get_full_information
is_available*
show_availability

get_cached_grade_score
wipe_session_cache

e. Make the private functions protected.

f. Reimplement your condition_info_section as another subclass of condition_info_base. I think it will only need a few functions, the constructor and the overridden is_available and get_full_course_section.


That's it. So overall, looking great but that duplication is a big problem, I think that definitely needs fixing - sorry but we really can't have two copies of all that code from condition_info (possibly with subtle, hard-to-spot differences).

17/Dec/12 5:32 PM;557058:800d2609-d1a6-4f60-b9d9-0edd9cbd20bd;Hi Elena,

Thank you for the ideas.

At this point I am going to close this issue, my apologies if you still feel it is a worthwhile endeavor.

The navigation and settings blocks were designed to encapsulate as much of the navigation and actions as possible.
The idea was both to create a structure that represented a Moodle site as closely as possible, and to avoid provide a consistent experience to the user where they could predict where they would need to look to find what they could do on a page.
I know that the navigation block can get unwieldy on a large site, and that for administrators the settings block can as well.
These were however trade off's of our original design.
At present we have no intention of changing our minds on that and splitting the blocks.

If you do feel passionately about this we'd encourage you to create and share blocks that meet your needs.
This would of course solve the problem for you and if shared others may pick up and use the blocks as well.
Should they become popular enough then by all means we could look at changing our minds.

Many thanks
Sam

ad 1:

Summary: Merge Users: Add functionality to Moodle that allows site admins to merge two user profiles.
Description:
I use Moodle in a corporate training environment and, as a site admin, I have a need to be able to merge two student records in Moodle. Our users are authenticated against Active Directory and when they login Moodle authenticates them against Active Directory and then checks if they are already registered as users on Moodle. If they are, then they are logged in. If not, Moodle pulls their user info off Active Directory and creates a new account for that username. This all works beautifully.

However, due to business processes and rules that are outside of our control, we sometimes have a situation where the same user gets registered on Moodle with two different usernames - the result being a duplicate record. Example, a user might change jobs or transfer to a different division. Alternatively, he might resign but then be re-hired sometime later. In each of these cases the user will most likely be given a new username on Active Directory (one of those things that are out of our control) by the HR department when they go through the whole HR recruitment or transfer process.

The result is that when this user goes on training again in his new position and tries to access Moodle with his NEW Active Directory username Moodle sees him as a new user and creates a new record for him. Obviously, all his old activity is still linked to his OLD username on Moodle. The course and activity data linked to his old username doesn't pull through to the new username because Moodle doesn't know that the two user records are related.

An ideal solution would be to have a function in Moodle where the site admin could merge the old username with the new username and all the activity from the old username would be transferred to the new username. The old record would then be deleted.

Over the last few years the Moodle community has developed their own scripts to solve this problem - so there's clearly a need. Quite a few of these scripts are shared on the http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=103425 thread on the Using Moodle forum. However, running these unofficial scripts can be risky as merging records in Moodle seems to be quite an involved process, so we need a solution that's been fully tested on all the operating system and database platforms that Moodle supports. None of these community solutions are platform independent. Example, I haven't been able to get any of them to run on a MSSQL database. So, unless I hire a programmer to develop a MSSQL script for me, I'm stuck. I'd much rather have an official merge function built into Moodle than having to rely on third-party scripts.

11/Oct/13 7:14 PM;557058:cbff4cf0-d741-4344-a8bb-265d2dc0c6ef;Nicolas,

I finally managed to get your script working on a instance of Moodle v2.5.1+ using a MSSQL 2008 R2 database on a IIS/WinXP SP3 laptop. I managed to merge two profiles "successfully" (i.e. without crashing Moodle or getting any errors), but I then found a problem when you have custom profile fields: and that is that after merging two profiles there are now TWO records, one from each of the two user profiles, for each of the custom profile fields. So, if you have ONE custom profile field there will be TWO records for that custom profile field after the merge (the record from the "User ID to be removed" profile and the record from the "User ID to be removed" profile. This is obviously a problem as there should only be one record for each profile field for each user profile - the /user/profile.php page can't handle two records for a custom profile field.

Example: If you have three custom profile fields: X, Y and Z and you have captured data in each of these custom fields then there will be three records in mdl_user_info_data for each student, one record for each of those custom fields:

SELECT id, userid, fieldid, data, dataformat
FROM mdl_user_info_data
WHERE (userid IN (36501, 14710))

gives this data for the three profile fields:

id	userid	fieldid	data	dataformat
20369	14710	1	0
64878	36501	1	0
20370	14710	2	432	0
64879	36501	2	6733	0
64880	36501	3	ABC	0

If you now merge the profile with another profile (i.e. merge 14710 and 36501) each of the above rows will be duplicated with the rows from the other profile - so there will now be two records for each custom profile field:

id	userid	fieldid	data	dataformat
20369	36501	1	0
64878	36501	1	0
20370	36501	2	432	0
64879	36501	2	6733	0
64880	36501	3	ABC	0

Moodle doesn't expect that so the result is that the /user/profile.php?id=36501 page might now show the incorrect data in those custom profile fields of the remaining profile after the merge.

So, profile field "fieldid = 2" might show "6733" instead of "432" on the /user/profile.php?id=36501 page after the merge.

If you're using any custom profile fields in Moodle this report_mergeusers.zip script be aware of this problem with custom profile fields.

29/Oct/13 3:55 PM;712020:b2bdefdc-c71e-4422-8c44-741e81f698d4;Hi all,

I'll try to explain I think removing user's data is necessary in certain cases. Remember that the actions are done in this timeline:

# Merge users.
# (if necessary) delete old user.

In the current version in github, when do we delete data?

# On grade_grades, but given the backup appears on grade_grades_history, actually, we are not removing anything. Afterwards, this table grade_grades_history will be updated also.
# On groups_members, given that if you do not remove it from the groups, with debugging enabled, you see warnings of duplicated ids when selecting groups' members. And actually, you do not know which database record is selected.
# On journal_entries. It is not a standard plugin, and it is necessary to detect when the data has to be updated  or removed.

The general behavior on all these three cases is as follows:

* Case 1: only "User ID to be removed" appears in records of the given table. They are simply updated with the new user id. The activity on that table was done by the old user and has to be updated.
* Case 2: only the new user id appears in records of the given table. Do nothing. Any activity on that was done by the user to be maintained and that data is correct.
* Case 3: both users appear in records of the given table for a given compound index/key. That means that the person using the old user id and the new id did activity on that table. If we simply update the "User ID to be removed" with the new user id, we will have duplicated indexes/keys in the database table, which is not allowed, and if allowed, Moodle afterwards would give us warning for the same issue (duplicated entries, like in the groups_members). So we need to do clean up. So, which database records are correct? We assume that the activity done with the new user is the correct, since it is the most recent. Most of the times, the "User ID to be removed" is deactivated (auth plugin does not allows to log in), so person cannot log in with that username any more.

And that is important, user deletion is done if necessary/possible after merging user (if it was ok). And we do not know the time that will pass between merging users and old user deletion. In that sense, we have to guarantee a correct Moodle behavior in any case.

Checking the admin/user.php?delete=12345 functionality, one can see that the database table we skip, the grade_grades and groups_members are clean up by the function delete_user(), and that an event 'user_deleted' is triggered. But in our Moodle installation there is no event handler registered for that, so there is no action taken for tables/plugins not covered in the core function delete_user(). 

The good thing would be all plugins with user interaction to have registered handlers for 'user_deleted' events. But that task is out of scope of this plugin. 

In conclusion, the job of this plugin is just in the scope of this plugin: Moodle have to work as well as before merging users, without warnings or problems of any kind. And that is what this plugin is making :-D

Any other comments/suggestions from other plugin participants to clarify that are welcome.

Have a nice day,

Jordi

Some years ago I wanted to build it from scratch, maily the part of configuration, going from the current config/config.php to an online settings.php, and also adding full of testing. Pros of your approach, building it from scratch:
 # Most of the edge cases I think come from having this plugin the "master of the Moodle" knowing how all things and elements work, their column names related to user.id field, and their dependencies, to name the few. So, building the plugin such a way, based on a user merging API, will help overtake most of those edge cases (just my impression).  # I also wanted to build it from scratch, at least a part of it, to make it more usable and customizable from web, and less code modifications (mainly for the config/local.config.php that can be added to override the default preferences of the plugin).

 # There are some aspects that you do not consider:
 ## Dependencies among steps of merging users.Just an example:  It would be necessary to process "activity completion" AFTER merging records from activity modules. The same for the grades. Special attention on quizzes and their attempts, or files uploaded to assignments. So, some kind of dependency management between the plugins should be added, to list them in order so that all dependencies are applied.
 ## Compound keys may exist in database as indexes or not. If you take a look at config/config.php, you can see compound keys that are unique indexes, non unique indexes or even do not exist such indexes at all. However, all of them are treated from the plugin viewpoint, as unique compound keys. How did we know that? Because of the behaviour of the Moodle after merging information and dealing with the code and understanding it. So the idea is to load automatically all indexes (unique or nonunique) and detect if includes some user.id related column to include them in the settings page. But also, let the administrator choose a specific table and add manually a compound index for that table. Not all the administrators have the possibility to add or modify code in the Moodle site.
 ## Command line API. You didn't mention that at all. The current plugin provides a simple proof of concept with an interactive CLI process to merge users. We, at our institution, extended that API so that every nigh we merge users. Our institution have defined a procedure of changing the id within the institution (for instance, from a passport to a new passport, or from a passport to a national id card, to list some few cases). This is very necessary.

However, not all the necessary information appears on that detail, and the SQL being broken is not fully listed to know what exactly happened. This has to be considered seriously and let the administrator know what exactly failed.

There is no unique solution. So the plugin MUST provide the functionality to help most of the administrators on their job and needs. So, as the current version of this plugin lets, we should provide a way to let administrator merge all tables or include some exceptions on tables to process by default as we do. It would be the responsibility of every administrator to omit some tables when merging, or merge all Moodle tables.
 ## Keep events ocurring. When a merging actions is success or a failure, just emit an event. This way, it is very easy to handle such cases and complement default plugin actions with additional ones.

Depending on the user (for instance, with lots of logs and a lot of activity on the Moodle site) may take several minutes. If a failure comes out and and Exception would be thrown, this should be catch, otherwise the adhoc_task would be requeued forever. Saludos,

Jordi

08/Sep/20 10:48 PM;712020:29ca2ae1-9330-4b1e-8509-8170df380e69;In addition to yesterdays discussion in the Moodle devchat I worked out an example on how the architecture could be improved:

!tool_mergeusers(2).png!
 Explanation why I designed it like this:
 - I think we can all agree that all plugins must merge their user data themselves. Therefore it is necessary to have some interfaces in the core that they can implement. This way we can call the merging functionalities in a uniform way. The core_user namespace probably makes the most sense.
 - The merge_tables function in the merger interface can return a string which represents a callback function that is called after the transaction has been committed. This is necessary because we want to separate the things that can be rolled back (the sql queries) and other things that can not be easily rolled back (like deleting files making calls to external services etc). There could be a plugin that executes a faulty SQL statement which would roll back the transaction. But plugins that ran their merging logic before that may not be able to recover files. So we move these actions after the database commit. Only SQL queries should be executed in the merge_tables function.
 - The get_options method is also necessary because we need to know if there are any settings for the merging logic of this plugin. And we want to collect them at a single place. I chose the parameter to be "pass-by-reference" because it saves people from creating an admin_settingpage object by themselves every time they implement this interface. 
 - As suggested by Andrew Nicols, I added a merge_operation class. The idea behind that is that it could provide some useful helper functions and data. Edit: Completely forgot that this object was also meant to deliver the merge configuration. I added that. So the plugin can now retrieve the values of the config it supplied in the get_options function.
 - Additionally I added the generic_table_merger to the core_user namespace. I think it is a good idea for every plugin that has tables with user columns but has not any settings and there is not any other user data that lives outside of the database. The plugins could use this class in their merge_tables function to easily implement the interface. I have written some merging functions for the core tables the past few days and used it a lot there. This is probably the point where I should point out some concrete examples.
 - I left the rest of the current plugin as a separate tool. The Privacy API seems to do it like this too, so I thought that would be a good idea.
 - There is also a core merger which takes care of all the core tables and other user data that is connected to that. I am not quite sure if it is in the right namespace. I think it doesn’t make sense to distribute the logic for the core tables even more so I packed it all into one class.
 - Now to the tricky part: The three interfaces. I have no idea if they are sufficient enough or not. I took a look at the Privacy API and how all those interfaces work together and get implemented. I also took a look at the documentation on how the components communicate. Especially the ‚subsystem‘ part is still a bit abstract to me. But I think that will get better once I start implementing the logic for these systems.

Note that I am pretty bad at choosing good names. So feel free to suggest better ones as well.

Summary: Extend filter manager API so that options can be passed to the filters
Description:
This is a proposal to introduce a cosmetic change in filter manager API so that runtime options can be passed to the filter() method. One of the use case (see MDLSITE-1026) is to pass the original format in which the text was inserted by the user (as is illustrated in the patch). Other options can be added later if/when needed.

Although this adds optional parameter $option (empty array by default), the patch has to modify all current filters because they extend common abstract base class. However note that the change itself is backward compatible as none of the current filter actually use the new parameter. This change is required if we want to solve MDLSITE-1026 and other similar issues.

Summary: allow custom profile fields to be synced though MNET
Description:
This is a patch proposal to improve MNET based strategies allowing custom profile fields to be consistant in a MNET based deployement.

Rationale : for distributed configuration within big organisations, several profile fields can be used. While the user is roaming to MNET subnodes, the actual code of mnet/auth/auth.php does not car about user custom profile fields.

The proposed patch allowes to automatically join profile fields value to the remotely submitted profile so the remote Moodle can sync matching values in fields which names are consistant.

We did not think further regarding to possible collision effect we could find in an "open" Moodle network, but our practice of MNET on realprojects barely focus real "open" networks. 

Syncing custom user fields allow integrators to add sturctural superstructures that can be based on additional user attached information.

Since we tryed it on 4 big installations, this way of doing work. Any objection welcome !

Cheers.

Summary: Group submission of activities
Description:
I was told in the forum that this would make a good item for the tracker as there may be others interested in this feature.
When I set up groups in the offline world, I can have those groups submit a single copy of an assignment and when I grade that assignment, the feedback and grade can be shared by the whole group.  I would like to be able to do the same thing in the online Moodle world.  Yes, there are times that I want to place students in groups but still have them submit assignments individually that the whole group can then view, view feedback and even see grades on.  However, for some assignments, since the groups are working collaboratively, it would be a waste of time (and online disk space) to have students submit the same assignment 4 or 5 times so that it could be graded 4 or 5 times, assigned feedback 4 or 5 times and assigned a numerical score 4 or 5 times.  It would be much more beneficial to both students (so they don't have to log out one student so another can log on and upload the file) and me as a teacher to be able to have an assignment (whether online text or upload) checked as being not just separate groups but a Shared Group Assignment so that a submission by one person in the group would count for everyone.  The person who replied in the forum said the only way to simulate such a thing now would be to setup a "dummy" student where all students in the group shared the password and could upload the information.  However, that doesn't allow each person's individual grade book to be updated when the assignment is submitted and graded.  It seems that this would be fairly simple except that it does involve more than just a single submission...it also involves the grade books, etc.
Comments:
03/Dec/11 9:25 AM;5a5023cc1d26e937aff10fbe;At our institiution we had the same desire to have what we called Group Assignments.  For 1.9.x a student (before my time at the institution) had copied the assignment module and adapted it as necessary to create the "group assignment" module as we saw it.  This had one submission per group, which every member of the group was allowed to see/update.  It also provided the Grader with an interface to easily assign the same grade/comment/outcome(s) to all of the members in the group, while also allowing the user to edit group members individually.

Ive since then written an implementation that provides the same functionality in Moodle 2.  It is written as an assignment subtype (there are 2 that we care about Upload and Offline so actually 2 types: groupupload and groupoffline) and so uses as much of the stock assignmetn code as is possible.  None of the core Moodle code has been altered to make this work.

If there is interest I will upload the code here for others to peruse.

Summary: Improve get_coursemodules_info
Description:
This proposal is intended to provide extra hooks allowing add-on modules to do things which are currently hard-coded so that the built-in modules (only!) can do them. See original forum discussion http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=152085 for earlier discussion.

There is a function plugin_get_coursemodule_info. At the moment this is permitted to return an object with a list of return information:

* extra - in the case of label , this appears as text instead of the normal link. In the case of everything other than label , this can be used to put extra attributes inside the <a> or <span> tag for the line (but not the class attribute because that might be set already).
By the way, this API is appalling.

* icon , iconcomponent - change or set the icon for the component

* name - change or set the name for the component

This information is used in print_section. It may also be accessed in other places that use get_fast_modinfo .

My suggestion has two parts.

1 Provide extra features for use in print_section

* Add an extraclasses variable (which can be used so that modules can customise some of their links with additional classes/styling).

* Leave extra defined as it is for modules other than label (retaining backward compatibility), but remove the special-case for label .

* Add a url parameter which, if set (to a moodle_url (or string?), customises the link. If you set it to null that means there is no link.

By a combination of the url parameter (=null) and the existing name parameter (=label content), it should be possible to change the implementation of label so that it does not require any hack in print_section.

2 Provide extra generic feature to enable other uses by plugins

At present only named parameters are permitted from plugin_get_coursemodule_info and these have defined meanings. Frequently it is useful if plugins (and, though not recommended, modifications to core code) can add other information that should be cached. This should be possible without having to change the core code.

* Add an optional options parameter which is a Moodle-style undefined object. If specified, this may include any number of parameters which will all be serialised into modinfo and returned by get_fast_modinfo.

Here is documentation for the changes, which should be placed in a wiki page. I'm not sure where this API is currently documented...

{code}
== _get_coursemodule_info ==

This optional function returns additional information about an instance of your module, which can be accessed quickly when displaying the module.

You should return an object $info which may contain the following fields, all of which are optional:

* ->url (2.1): leave blank to use the default URL, or set to the constant MOD_URL_NOLINK if this module does not need a link. In the current version we do not recommend setting this to any other value.
* ->name: name of instance (text displayed in link on course page) - this will not be used if MOD_URL_NOLINK is specified.
* ->content (2.1): HTML content to be displayed on the course page where this module is placed; appears below the link, if present (this is how Label displays content on course page)
* ->extraclasses (2.1): Additional CSS classes to be added to the A or DIV tag(s) for this item on main menu.
* ->icon: specifies an icon to use for this instance instead of the normal module icon; you can either use the name of an icon which will be directly passed to the $OUTPUT->pix_icon function, or the special format mod/mymodule/iconname which will be passed to that function as two parameters iconname, mymodule.
* ->customdata (2.1): A place to store a string or object containing custom data for this module, which needs to be available course-wide via the get_fast_modinfo function. If present, this data should be small in size.

* ->extra (deprecated in 2.1): puts content in a weird part of the A or DIV tag for the item; can be used to add attributes
* ->iconcomponent (deprecated in 2.1): doesn't appear to do anything
{code}

Summary: Generic way to include dynamic module information on course view page
Description:
This proposal is intended to provide extra hooks allowing add-on modules to do things which are currently hard-coded so that the built-in modules (only!) can do them. See original forum discussion http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=152085 for earlier discussion. 

(There may be performance concerns here which will need to be resolved during implementation or detailed design.)

At present it is possible for the forum to show dynamic(non-cached) information about unread posts. This is not possible for other modules because it is achieved via a hack in print_section .

* Add a plugin feature FEATURE_DYNAMIC_LINK_INFO. Modules implement this feature if they provide dynamic link information.

* Add a new plugin API plugin_get_dynamic_link_info($course,$modinfo) which would be called when displaying the link for plugins that support dynamic link info. This would return arbitrary HTML to be added after the link.

* Implement this API for forum (ensuring that we retain precisely the existing performance characteristics)and remove the forum-specific hack from print_section.

This change allows other modules to add information to their links on the front page. (You may notice a ForumNG-shaped vested interest; it could also apply, for example, to last-modified dates for wiki, that sort ofthing.)

Summary: Separate visibility of front page course list from the site/config capability
Description:
We have a situation where we have a team of "Learning Technology Advisors" who have a Role (LTA) based upon the Teacher role assigned at the system level (They can be a teacher in EVERY course and we have about 1500).

This means that the course list on the front page can take a very substantial amount of time to load, especially over mobile connections.

At present the listing of courses is dependant on whether or not the user has the "moodle/site:config" capability, which is typically only given to Admins. We do not want to give this capability to the LTA roles but we do want the effect of this to be applied.

We propose the (attached) modification which adds a new "moodle/site:hidecourselist" capability and modifies the index.php page to observe this capability instead of the "config" one.

Add_HideCourseList_Cap.patch adds the capability to the /lib/db/access.php file
Add_language_string_HideCourseList_cap.patch adds the appropriate language string to /lang/en_ut8/role.php
Observe_HideCourseList_cap.patch modifies Index.php to use the new capability

Summary: Retrieve copyright information from (at least) Flickr Public repository
Description:
Received an email from a Copyright officer out there in Moodle land who was asked to comment on whether the Flickr Public repository should be enabled on an upcoming site, with the response (paraphrased) as follows:

"The file picker itself strips all of Flickr's branding, which could be an infringement of moral rights (false attribution) and therefore creates the impression to the user that the images are housed within Moodle and not, in effect, gathered from multiple Flicker user accounts. Each of these users must be attributed. This is a requirement of the Copyright Act.
 
Another issue is that a user cannot determine what kind of licence to attach to an image. This is also a requirement of the Copyright Act as it is an infringement to remove any DRM (Digital Rights Management) or ERM (Electronic Rights Management). The file picker has no mechanism to attach or drag the licence with the image.
 
In each instance staff will need to go to the Flickr account, check the licence and then determine whether they need to rely on our copyright licence or the user account copyright licence which is attached to the image.
 
In essence it is really no different from searching for an image using Google Images and then having to click on the image to determine which website it came from and what kind of licence is attached to it.
 
I suggest that in most instances, each image which is selected using the file picker will need to be recorded in our Copyright Database as staff will be relying on our copyright licence.
 
There is no advantage to staff by using this tool. In effect it will become a burden for staff as they will need to perform the extra steps to ensure that they are not infringing copyright."

Harsh, but a definite and valid blocker to using this repository, or for that matter any repository that searches public content (assume YouTube at least would be the same).

Suggestion then (and no idea if its feasible) - can copyright information such as license information and copyright owner be automatically retrieved from Flickr and stored somewhere in Moodle - either loaded into the alt_text by default or stored in a separate table which we could then report against for copyright purposes? 

And yes, I know Moodle isn't a file repository or a content management system, but I can already see me having this conversation with numerous clients in the next couple of years, and it would be a shame to have to advise them that although its a neat trick to be able to search public content from within Moodle, the realities of copyright law coupled with the current functionality mean that it is about as useful as a chocolate teapot.

Summary: Differentiate between notifications and personal messages in messaging
Description:
There have been a lot of complaints about forum notifications appearing within the messaging system. Several options for resolving this were outlined at http://docs.moodle.org/en/index.php?title=Development:Forum_notifications_as_messages

To differentiate between messages and notifications we would add a "notification" column to both message and message_read. One they are read they would be moved from message to message_read as per normal. The message screen however would ignore read notifications.

Summary: relax user_not_fully_set_up() by allowing empty last names
Description:
Some countries, such as Indonesia and India, actually officially allow names without last names.  It means, however, that if such a user logs in to Moodle, the user_not_fully_set_up() function from moodlelib.php will return TRUE, and, as the result, the user will be redirected to edit their preferences.  Now, if they are not allowed to edit their preferences, they won't be able to do anything on the site at all.

We have had several cases  like this because we are international logistic company and we have students in Indonesia and India, where quite a few of our students only have one name, for example:  Mina or Prajith or Indra etc..   Since our policy is to maintain user preferences for authenticated users by ourselves, these students are not allowed to edit their user preferences, and, as such are not able to use Moodle.

Suggestion is to relax the rule in user_not_fully_set_up() so as to allow either firstname or lastname to be defined.

Summary: Moodle 2.0 local help module
Description:
With new Moodle 2.0 help system help strings become shorter and complex (and most needed!) help often moved from in-site files to the Moodle Docs wiki (with links from help strings).

Lack of in-site help is a downgrade from Moodle 1.9 and could be harmful in many cases, here are some examples:
1. Many moodle installations are located in 3d-word countries where there is no cheap Internet around
2. University/school may choose to don't allow Internet access from their classes, to allow the students/pupils concenrate on the tasks they were given. I know several such institutions personally. Moodle installation is accessible via local network.
3. Company (some examples I know) with Moodle installed in local network could have strict policy about Internet access for the employes for security reasons.
4. Teacher/developer doing their work on the notebook with no mobile Internet around.

One idea mentioned in http://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=160469#p703279 is to create periodical a snapshot of necessary Moodle Docs wiki pages and either bundle them with Moodle or make a separate, but pluginable module, that could be easily added to the Moodle installation and would redirect moodle-doc links from the site pages to the local help.

Only pages with end-user documentation should be included in package. They may be either marked by some tag in wiki or computed from links in the moodle help strings (and links on the bottom of the pages).The module should probably have different packages for different languages, just like moodle strings.

I also like the idea of adding functionality that lets a school link to their customized help files easily.

Summary: nolink spans should be searched for only once and not ignored by some filters
Description:
From a chat with Eloy:

only filters using "filter_phrases" (one function) are considering the nolink spans

this has 2 drawbacks:

1) not all the filters respect nolink spans.
2) the same function, looking and skipping nolink spans is executed multiple times, if I'm not wrong.

1) = inconsistency
2) = slow

IMO it would be optimal to perform that nolink treatment only once

it's one small improvement but that affects to each text displayed in one moodle page, so I guess it will save some miliseconds at least

This is the list of filters currently handling "nolink" sections:

filter/activitynames/filter.php
filter/censor/filter.php
mod/data/filter.php
mod/glossary/filter.php

Any other filter is ignoring nolink sections

and, as commented, if the site has enabled: activitynames, data and glossary... the nolik sections are being handled 3 times, if I'm not wrong.

confirmed, each filter of the 4 above... repeat the handling. And each filter not in the list above, ignores the nolink sections completely.

Summary: 'Manage backup files' reverses display order
Description:
This is not a major issue, but it is a little annoying.

On the 'Restore Course' screen, you are shown a list of backups, sorted with the most recent backup at the top of the list and showing the date/time for each of the backups.

If you click on 'Manage backup files', you are taken to another screen, missing the 'date/time' information and sorted by filename. This means that, if you are using the default names, the list is now sorted to show the oldest backup at the top of the list, rather than the most recent.

I can see this switch around potentially leading to the wrong backup files being deleted from the server (as the user decides they need to delete, for example, the 'last 3 backups in the list', then clicks 'Manage backup files', deletes the last 3 items, only to discover they were the 3 most recent backups, not the 3 oldest backups).

Summary: Allow any value to be specified for backup_sche_keep
Description:
Site admins are able to set the number of course backups that the scheduled backups function keeps by specifying a value on the "How many recent backups for each course do you want to keep" (backup_sche_keep) option under Administration / Courses / Backups. This option is implemented as a drop-down list which means that the site admins are restricted to the values that appear on the list. Example, admins can select 1, 2 or 5, but not 3.

These list values hard-coded in the \admin\settings\courses.php page. To use different values than those on the list the admin has to modify this php page. But in our organisation we try to avoid making changes to Moodle core, unless it's absolutely necessary - and in this case it's not important enough...

An alternative solution that might solve this problem is to change this drop-down list to a textbox. This will allow the user to enter any value that they want and not be restricted to the options that are currently on that list.

Summary: Statistics performance improvements for large log tables in Oracle databases
Description:
This patch may be of interest to crazy people like us who run a single Moodle instance on an Oracle database for all of the university's courses. What follows is a bit of a story explaining the rationale behind this patch.

We currently have 90.6 mil records in our m_log table, and a little over twelve months ago discovered that once the logging table reached a certain number of rows (around 30 mil seems to come to mind), Oracle would take too long to process certain phases of the statistics job, eventually to the point where it would time out running the query and just stop working completely. It also affected the use of certain pages in Moodle for looking at log data. We could not delete any logging records because of data retention policy, and splitting old records into archival tables was looking like a pain. We also thought about trying Oracle partitioning but discovered we weren't licensed, so instead I went looking for an alternative to restore functionality.

I looked at the queries in the stats job where the process began dying and discovered the index on the time column of m_log just didn't seem to be having any benefit. Since stats processing deals with log events in day-sized lumps, I wondered what might happen if I could convert the timestamp range test into a simple equality test and use better indexes.

The patch adds an extra column to m_log called 'timeday' which contains the timestamp of the log event rounded down to the 0th second of the day on which it occurred. There are also additional indexes that include this column as appropriate for the different stats phases. Modifications are made to scripts that deal with log data to refer to this column when possible and benefit also from the optimisation. All of these changes made the processing job go from not working at all to processing a typical day of log data in about 20-30 seconds.

I didn't have the chance at the time to see whether I could have used Oracle function-based indexes to do the same thing, and it may be worth investigating to see if it's a better alternative. Hopefully this patch may prove useful in some way.

18/Feb/12 7:29 AM;557058:4af380fd-7ec3-47cb-b4e9-f7d6f3da6d4c;I have complex criteria for determining which courses need an automated course backup each night. Rather than writing some correspondingly complex Moodle PHP code for implementing a filter, I just hack the database directly. It is quick and effective.

In Moodle 2.0, column "nextstarttime" of the "backup_courses" table determines the next time that a backup for a given course will run. For those courses that I do not want to backup each night, I just set "nextstarttime" to a far future date.

For example, when using a MySQL database and a prefix of "mdl_" for the table names, if the criteria for preventing automated backups depend only on columns of the "mdl_course" table, SQL of the following form can reset the "nextstarttime" to Jan. 1, 2020 for all courses satisfying "arbitrarily complex SQL":

update mdl_backup_courses bc, mdl_course c
set bc.nextstarttime = unix_timestamp('2020-01-01')
where bc.courseid = c.id and (arbitrarily complex SQL);

05/Feb/14 1:14 AM;712020:2c9f2780-0a69-4150-85a9-2d5e9d95f4af;This issue is still relevent to current versions. In general, the largest contributors to session size are the following:

SESSION->completioncache
SESSION->dst_offsets
USER->access
USER->ajax_updatable_user_prefs

In my testing, these variables accounted for 76.12% of total session size (at the time of this writing).

A large amount of the data saved here is refreshed from the database when needed. In Moodle, the $_SESSION values are typically only used during a single page execution, which is an incorrect way to use the $_SESSION global variable (whose intent is to persist across page executions, such as multi-page forms or other user-specific items that do not convey authorization).

Summary: Add a reduced server load Vs real time data administration dial
Description:
There are a number of places within Moodle that have time delays to reduce server load. For example if an RSS feed is requested the cached version is automatically served if the cached version is less than 60 seconds old thus avoiding expensive database queries to check for new items.

Off the top of my head timers like this exist in the 3 RSS feed generation points (glossary, database activity and forum) and within message_popup_window() (the check for new messages isn't done if the user was shown a popup less than 2 minutes ago). There are almost certainly more places where things like this are done.

It would be handy to have a single admin setting that could be used to control these delays allowing the admin to set them to anything from 0 (use real-time data) to a lengthy delay to reduce server load. This would provide a convenient way for an admin to dial up and down how real-time their Moodle is in response to server load. Automating this so Moodle could respond dynamically to current server load would be very cool but is probably too difficult to do in a way that would work correctly on an arbitrary server.

Summary: Use temporary tables in sync_users of external database authentication
Description:
Here at Universidade Federal de Santa Catarina we are starting the upgrade of our  infra-structure to 2.0 and our first major goal is to sync users from the academic control system.
In Moodle 1.9 we use a custom system, developed from beggining, and with a lot of features. One of these is to create users in Moodle from a table, and now we know that Moodle's External Database Authetication plugin can do the work, but it is not that "performatic".
As the documentation says, it uses arrays to calculate the set of users to be created, instead of a temporary table and a left join like what is done in ldap plugin.
This patch i am submitting changes this behaviour and introduces the temporary table in the proccess. A lot of duplicated code from ldap, that we may think about refactor.
I haven't tested the original process, but the new one can calculate the users to create in almost zero time in a fresh install (just 2 or 3 records in user table) and it took about 5 minutes to calculate the set with 38K records in the external table that were already in moodle.
Also, the update process can be a lot improved. The current code does an update for each user, that consists of one SELECT and N updates, where N is the number of update keys. I don't have numbers but should be better to construct only one UPDATE TABLE query and let the database calculate which records differ. This is valid for remove/suspend process too.

06/Jul/11 7:14 AM;5b04c63b88b6744fe4207a9b;I've been working on some improvements on the current implementation of the db authentication plugin.

The improvements I've been working on do not use temporary tables, but drastically reduce both the memory consumption and the number of database queries. As a result, the time for a complete run of the sync is also drastically reduced.

My test system is as follows:
* Postgres 9.0 with out-of-the-box configuration (no tuning)
* Moodle on Master

My test database has 15,000 records.

Using the current implementation of the db auth mechanism, I'm seeing something like the following. This is a straight compare where no data has changed.
{panel}
www-data@moodle:/home/nicols/git/software/moodle$ time php auth/db/cli/sync_users.php > /dev/null
PERF:  time: 554.768607s memory_total: 138010140B (131.6MB) memory_growth: 137127328B (130.8MB) memory_peak: 155578500B (148.4MB) includecount: 77 contextswithfilters: 0 filterscreated: 0 textsfiltered: 0 stringsfiltered: 0 langcountgetstring: 15005 langcountmemcache: 15002 langcountdiskcache: 0 includedyuimodules: 54 includedjsmodules: 2 db reads/writes: 30013/0 ticks: 55484 user: 17319 sys: 520 cuser: 0 csys: 0 serverload: 1.70 

real    9m14.861s
user    2m53.223s
sys     0m5.212s
{panel}

Notice in particular the memory growth/total, and the db reads/writes

I've heavily optimised it now such that:
{panel}
www-data@moodle:/home/nicols/git/software/moodle$ time php auth/db/cli/sync_users.php 
PERF:  time: 8.187989s memory_total: 15399384B (14.7MB) memory_growth: 14517032B (13.8MB) memory_peak: 51300208B (48.9MB) includecount: 43 contextswithfilters: 0 filterscreated: 0 textsfiltered: 0 stringsfiltered: 0 langcountgetstring: 5 langcountmemcache: 3 langcountdiskcache: 0 includedyuimodules: 54 includedjsmodules: 2 db reads/writes: 16/0 ticks: 822 user: 156 sys: 7 cuser: 0 csys: 0 serverload: 0.95 

real    0m8.259s
user    0m1.592s
sys     0m0.080s
{panel}

The memory use for the same dataset, and the same operation has gone from 131.6MB to 14.7
reads have gone from 30013, to 16.

Looking at the code in further detail, the update code seems to do the following:
* Select all users from your external db
* Select all users from moodle who need updating
* Loop through each user needing updating
* Retrieve the user from the moodle database again
* Retrieve the user from the external database again
* Loop through each key that is set to onlogin
* Compare each value in turn
* If the value is different, call set_field on it

As a result, if you have 15,000 users, and you change three fields on each (e.g. set the City, State, and Country), you'll be doing:
* One select to initially retrieve all records from moodle
* One select to initially retrieve all records from the external DB
* 15,000 selects to select each individual record from moodle
* 15,000 selects to select each individual record from the external DB
* 3 set_field operations per 15,000 records.

You'd have a total of:
1 + 1 + ( 1 * 15,000 ) + ( 1 * 15,000 ) = 30,002 selects
3 * 15,000 = 45,000 updates

I've made the same optimisation with both ADODB, and with the moodle database stuff. Both give massive performance boosts over the current.
The standard moodle database engine uses marginally less memory than ADODB (0.5MB in my test)

My tests show similar performance gains for all operations (create, undelete, update, delete).

I'm happy to submit my changes to Moodle Core, but have on question first:

At present, the db auth plugin uses adodb. Moodle has since introduced it's own database system, but this doesn't have the same support as ADODB.
I've tested by changes with both of these and it's very little work to submit either -- what is the preference upstream?

I didn't understand what it was until I read the code. Perhaps an example could be provided... we can always ask Helen to help with this as well, she is very good with this sort of thing. Also document what is to be provided e.g. full regex delimiters inc. # It would be great if we could validate the regex somehow for the devicedetectregex setting (the first one I tried I didn't put a delimeter in and got a pile of notices). In the interests of getting this in ASAP perhaps we can create a bug report for this to see it improved after it has been integrated. # Variable names shouldn't contain underscores as per guidelines - http://docs.moodle.org/en/Development:Coding_style#Variables # That is one massive line in moodlelib with the regex's to pick mobile devices. I think those two regex's should be split out to vars to shorten that line. # core_renderer::theme_switch_links shouldn't use $PAGE it has $this->page. (the $USER global should be removed as well as it isn't used) # core_renderer::switchlinkdisplayed should be protected not private so that overriding renderers can control the placement of the switch link as well. # Looking at moodle_page::legacy_theme_support I am wondering when $CFG->themes will not be set up? (See note c below ... I wrote more later) # get_device_type You need to check that HTTP_USER_AGENT is set and likely return default if not (A quick search shows code checking if it is empty) # get_user_switched_theme returns null at one point - should return false just for accuracy sake (I wondered whether this should be renamed as it is more about getting device switches.. food for thought I'll leave that up to you) # get_selected_theme_for_device_type The check to make sure the theme exists is incorrect, themes can exist within either the theme's directory of $CFG->themedir if set - You either check manually (grep for CFG->themedir) or try using theme_config::find_theme_location. # switch.php url should be using PARAM_URL # For switch theme why not use key => value pairs rather than an array of objects? This way you wouldn't need to check if the user pref already exists you would just overwrite it if it does? (I think there were other places where similar thing was being done that could be improved in the same way) # A quick grep shows there are still a couple of places using $CFG->theme (see note c below) General notes: a/ After looking for a while at _legacythemeinuse I think that it should be removed and that what it was doing should be done for everything but the default. From what I quickly noted if _legacethemeinuse == true then the following would occur: * A class was added to the body tag. * A message was printed in the footer stating that a legacy theme was in use. I think that it would be nice if we could do that same for all but the default so that you would always have a body class that themer's could utilise (legacytheme, tablettheme, mobiletheme). As for the notice I see you already have the theme_switch_links function doing that which is cool, perhaps just improve the string. Actually having looked at that I think it would be cool if the string were 'You are currently using the mobile theme, switch to the standard theme' or something - again Helen is the person to talk to about strings. Perhaps the best option would be to store the device type being displayed for as a protected moodle_page var and expose it through a magic method so that future code may use it as well (I see this idea was tossed around in the spec blocks etc). It would of course mean initialising it at an appropriate time. b/ I'm not entirely convinced that changing from $CFG->theme to the json encoded CFG->themes is a good move. I think using separate CFG variables would be a better option e.g. $CFG->theme, themelegacy, thememobile, themetablet. The advantage of doing this is that it would be backwards compatible with existing code (in that it at least would find the default theme). Then again that is my personal preference, I will talk to Eloy about it and see what his prefence is (although reading through the bug again after reading it I see Tim raised this same point so perhaps we should go ahead with it). c/ I don't like legacy_theme_support I think we should try to come up with a way of avoiding that. Given that the upgrade code is going to remove the current $CFG->theme and set $CFG->themes I think if $CFG->themes wasn't set it would be safe to assume that an upgrade/install was occuring and that it would be fine to fall back to the default. As I said I certainly think this going in the right direction, and as I'm sure you know Martin is keen to get this in for 2.1. If you have any questions or want to discuss any of the points go for it (if you think I've missed the point of anything etc let me know!), this is a high priority item on my list now so I'll aim to get back to you with answers etc as quickly as possible. Otherwise I'm looking forward to seeing how you get along. I should add this doesn't constitute a full review sorry - I went as far as I could before I kept coming back to the same areas and while I have used the new setting to test the basic operation of things I havn't given it a proper/complete test. Cheers Sam

Summary: Provide a reason why a category/course total is not being displayed
Description:
In the gradebook forum users are regularly asking why a category or course total isn't being displayed. While calculating the grades the gradebook could store a reason why a total is blank then give the user a way to access the reason. The "-" could be clicked to display a popup containing the reason for example.

Common reasons include aggregation is weighted mean and all weights are 0 and the category contains a hidden item and is set to hide the total when a hidden item is found.

This would make the gradebook much more user friendly and reduce the frequency with which users have to resort to asking the community to diagnose their gradebook mis-configuration.

Summary: course action scheduler
Description:
Original description by Petr:
There are very many time based options in course, modules and gradebook, users keep requesting more and more new options. This adds code complexity and clutters normal UI. Example of these features is hidden until and lock after - majority of users do not need these options. Long term solution could be new action scheduler defined at the course level, it would enable teachers to specify actions to be executed at specified time - such as lock gradebook item, hide/unhide items, hide activity, etc. The user interface could be pretty simple, something like current calendar. The actions would be queued and executed from cron.

Notes by Andrew:
Splitting out the showing/hiding of grades and the recalculation of final grades from the displaying of grade reports could improve performance.
